title: How the documentation site is written
text: The pages in this folder are the source of `planetai.fab.city/docs`. `tools/build_docs.py` renders them, together with a few pages taken as they are from `docs/`, into static HTML on the programme layer's tokens. Nothing here is served by a node, with one exception: `tools/build_learn.py` cuts short quotes out of these pages into `app/static/learn.json`, which the dashboard's learn mode shows in the ask pane, and cuts every page at its `##` headings into `data/docs_site.json`, which `GET /docs/search` reads. Move one of those spans, or edit any page, and `make lint` says so until `make learn` is run.

title: How the documentation site is written · What a page is for
text: A person reads these pages to build a node one part at a time. The node is the local unit of PLANETAI, hyperlocal compute and intelligence for distributed production, and its purpose is fixed: clean air, water and soil for the people and the other living things around it. It measures its place, acts on what it measures, keeps its raw readings at home and sends upward only what a district, a bioregion and the Fab City Index need. The canonical wording is the lead and "What it is for" in `introduction.md`; the README, `llms.txt`, `AGENTS.md`, the dashboard's footer and the programme page quote it, and `tools/check_site.py` checks that they still do. So every page that has steps says, in its first lines, which part of the node the reader is adding and what the node can do once it is there. Steps are numbered when the order matters, and each one says what to do, what the screen shows when it worked, and what that means for the node. A step the reader cannot check is not a step. The page ends by naming the next part to add. The path the pages follow: run a node → connect what measures your place → read it → let it ask, and answer → measure whether it worked → extend it with packs and sources → join the network → put an agent on it.

title: How the documentation site is written · Voice
text: Written for the person installing at 9 pm with a sensor that just went quiet. Plain words. Say what to do. Short declaratives mixed with longer ones; never a march of same-length sentences. Sentence case everywhere; no emoji, no hype, no "simply", no "robust", no "seamless". No em dashes: a comma, a colon, a full stop or a bracket does the work. No "it's not X, it's Y" unless a real misconception is being corrected and the replacement is named. A page states what the node does in this version, not what it will do. Where the code and an older document disagree, the code wins and the page says which version it read. The mission is stated in specifics (what stays, what goes up, which cell, who may be counted), never in slogans. Only facts that are in the code or in the canonical documents (`ARCHITECTURE.md`, `SPEC.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `docs/*.md`). No line numbers in the prose. A gap or a known bug is stated plainly: "In v0.72.1 the AirGradient adapter exists and is tested but is not registered for polling." The pages are Fab City's, and they read the way Tomas Diez writes: direct and warm, "you" for the reader, "we" only where Fab City itself speaks (we run node #1, write to us), never "I". Clauses joined by commas rather than chopped into fragments. Say each thing once, on the page where a reader would look for it, and link to it from everywhere else. What reads as written by a machine, and is cut on sight: framing sentences that announce what comes next, headline titles and colon reveals, "X, not Y" pairs, tidy groups of three, false ranges ("from a sensor on the wall to a satellite overhead"), claims of significance, a run of three-word fragments for drama, an `-ing` clause bolted on to sound deep, "Note that", "It is important to", "simply". What does not belong on these pages at all: the history of how a feature came to be ("since v0.72", "until v0.80 it did"), dates of internal decisions and who took them, pull request and issue numbers, the names of the people and agents who built a thing, and node #1's diary. The CHANGELOG keeps history. A page says what the node does now. Node #1 may appear as a worked example, with numbers, when an example is clearer than a rule.

title: How the documentation site is written · Conventions the renderer understands
text: - One `# Title` per page, first line. The sidebar uses it. - `## ` and `### ` headings make the right-hand "On this page" list. Keep them short. - Endpoints are `### GET /path` (method in capitals, then the path). The renderer draws the method as a chip. - The line right after an endpoint heading may be `Access: public` · `Access: open` · `Access: token` · `Access: admin` · `Access: loopback or token` and so on. The renderer draws it as an ink chip. - Settings, commands, files, metric names, cell names and values are in backticks. - Tables are GitHub tables. A table is for parallel facts (settings, routes, rules); prose is for everything else. - A note is a blockquote starting with a bold word: `> **Note.** …`, `> **Careful.** …`, `> **Gap in v0.72.1.** …`. - Link to another page by its file name: `[the API](api.md)`. The renderer turns it into the right URL. - Link to a repository file with its path from the repo root: `[init.sql](../../init.sql)`; the renderer turns paths that leave `docs/` into GitHub links at the built commit. - Numbers, units and ids as the node writes them: `µg/m³`, `°C`, `pm25`, `Environmental|Community`.

title: Bring your own agent
text: An agent is a guest on the machine, never a part of it. It can read everything the node knows and help the person in front of it install, diagnose and run the node in plain language. It drafts and a person dispatches: no agent dispatches without a human row in `actions`, and the loop closes only when a person says what they did. The repository is written for agents. `AGENTS.md` at its root is the front door: its first section is a table that routes an agent to one of eight skills, and the rest is what an agent must not break. `llms.txt` indexes every document for an agent arriving from outside, and `make lint` fails if a skill names a command or a path that does not exist. Paste this to your agent and nothing else: > You are helping me with a PLANETAI node, an open-source program that turns a spare computer in my home or lab into > a hyperlocal environmental monitor. Start by reading > https://raw.githubusercontent.com/fabcity/planetai-node/main/AGENTS.md. Its first section is a table that routes > you to the right skill for what I am asking, and the rest of it is what you must not break. Read that skill before > you tell me to run anything. Never ask me for the contents of my `.env` file, and never suggest exposing the node > to the internet; to reach it from elsewhere, use Tailscale.

title: Bring your own agent · Connect Claude Desktop over the tailnet
text: 1. **Put the node on your tailnet.** On the node, run `planetai mesh`. When it is done the node is reachable by name from any of your devices, with no ports opened on any router, and the name is recorded as `MESH_NAME`. 2. **Get the snippet.** On the node, run `planetai agent`. It prints the twenty-one tools by class (read, act, admin), the address on this machine (`http://localhost:8080/mcp`) and on the tailnet (`http://<MESH_NAME>:8080/mcp`), the header every call carries, `Authorization: Bearer <ADMIN_TOKEN>` with the real token in it, and a block for `mcp.json` or `claude_desktop_config.json`: ```json {"mcpServers": {"planetai-bayu-ungasan": {"type": "http", "url": "http://bayu-ungasan:8080/mcp", "headers": {"Authorization": "Bearer <ADMIN_TOKEN>", "X-Agent": "kitchen-claude"}}}} ``` Put it into Claude Desktop's configuration on a machine on the same tailnet, with your agent's name as `X-Agent`. The token in it is the admin token, so treat the file like a password. 3. **Tell the agent its name.** The audit trail records the name passed in each write tool's `agent` argument, and the `X-Agent` header does not reach it. Say it once: "your name for this node is kitchen-claude; pass it as `agent` on every write." A write that leaves it out is recorded as `agent`, and then the ledger cannot say which agent it was. You see the name come back in step 5. 4. **Ask for status.** "Call `health_check`, then `status`." You get `ok` and a list of checks, each failing one with its fix, then the node's name, version, last poll, per-loop errors and ρ. The agent can read the node. 5. **Ask it to record an act.** "I closed the north windows about alert 361." The agent calls `act` with `alert_id` 361, your words as `note` and its name as `agent`, and the tool answers `{"recorded": true, "alert_id": 361, "by": "kitchen-claude"}`. With no words, or with `acted`, `done` or `ok`, the tool refuses and tells the agent to ask you what you did. On a node set to `DECISION_REQUIRED=1` it gets 409 until somebody records a decision on the dashboard. 6. **Find the row.** On the dashboard, Data › Ledger (on `?layout=classic`, Act → "What was decided, and by whom") shows `kitchen-claude` with `acted` at the top, and the `alerts` tool shows the alert's `acted_at` filled in. The row is in `actions` because a person said it happened, and it counts in ρ. Claude Code, Codex and any client that speaks MCP over HTTP connect the same way; [MCP](mcp.md) has the other clients and every tool with its class.

title: Bring your own agent · The eight skills
text: | the person says | skill | what it makes the agent do | |---|---|---| | "help me install this", "will it run on my old laptop?" | `skills/setup-node` | Run the preflight first and read its exit code, and never continue past exit 2. Install with the one line or `planetai setup --answers`. Then Telegram, the test alert (the only end-to-end proof), the dashboard, the doctor. Never a machine that sleeps, never print `.env`, never tune a threshold during setup, never pip on the host. | | "it stopped working", "no alerts since Tuesday", here is a log | `skills/troubleshoot-node` | Ask for exactly `planetai doctor --json`, `status --json` and twenty lines of logs, plus `sensors --json` for a sensor. Never `.env`; if one arrives, tell them to revoke the bot token. It may read, restart, update and back up; it may not change a threshold, record an action, move the database or edit `.env` without consent. | | "connect this to Claude / Codex", "reach it from outside" | `skills/connect-agent` | Get the URL, token and snippet from `planetai agent`. Tailscale, never a port forward, ngrok or a public reverse proxy. Name yourself in every write's `agent` argument. Call `health_check` first, then `status`. | | "put our city on the Fab City Index" | `skills/publish-to-index` | Establish the tier first: one node per pilot writes, a home node never does. `planetai cells --json`, and the state must be honest. The writer lives with the Index and needs a per-pilot token issued by hand. See [Federation](federation.md). | | "I want a pack for my city", "share our pack" | `skills/write-a-pack` | Decide the tier first: a pack for one place is wild, in its own repository, never a fork of this one. Start from a core pack of the same kind; `id` equals the folder; keys go under `secrets:`, never a value. Test with `tools/check_rules.py` and `planetai packs` on the person's node, then list it at fabcity/planetai-wild-packs from their account. See [Packs](packs.md). | | you are about to change this repository | `skills/preflight` | `tools/session.sh preflight` first. Your own worktree and your own branch, never the one holding `main`. | | you are cutting a release | `skills/release-docs` | Re-read every page of this site against the code, fix what changed, and move each page's checked stamp to the release; `make lint` refuses the release until every page is done. | | you are about to end a session that changed this repository | `skills/land` | `tools/session.sh land`: nothing exists only on this machine, and the gates ran. | The first four are for an agent operating a node, the fifth for one writing a pack with its author, the last three for one changing the code. When a document and a skill disagree, the document wins and the skill has a bug.

title: Bring your own agent · Two ways in
text: Over MCP, from this machine or anywhere on the tailnet: `http://<node>:8080/mcp` with the header `Authorization: Bearer <ADMIN_TOKEN>`. Start with `health_check`, every failing check names its fix. A person driving an agent gets all twenty-one tools, because somebody reads what it proposes; [MCP](mcp.md) lists them. A shell on the node, for what needs Docker or git: ```bash planetai status --json planetai doctor --json planetai sensors --json planetai cells --json planetai report planetai report last planetai report every <h> planetai report at <h> planetai update planetai backup planetai restart planetai logs planetai setup --answers node.json ``` The container has no Docker and no git, so the `maintenance` tool hands these back as commands with an explanation. An agent with no shell tells the person which one to run.

title: Bring your own agent · A local model may already be running
text: `planetai agent local` puts Ollama on the node and a loop that answers the household on Telegram. That model gets the 17 `read` and `act` tools and shows up in the audit trail as `local-model/<rung>`. A remote agent is not alone on the node, so it reads the alerts and the actions before acting, and does not undo what the household's own model did without asking. See [The bot](bot.md). `actions` also holds `decided` rows, written from the dashboard's Decide card. A decision records what somebody said they would do and moves nothing: it closes no alert and is not in ρ. The answers to an alert event (Done, Not now, Doesn't fit, with an `event_id` and no `alert_id`) are rows there too. No MCP tool writes either kind.

title: Bring your own agent · Invariants an agent must not break
text: - Raw readings stay on this machine. Exports and aggregates travel, rows never do. - `.env` holds secrets. Never print it, paste it or commit it. A log containing `api.telegram.org/bot` is a leak. - The database lives on a local disk, never a network mount. Backups are how data reaches a NAS. - A model or a portal is `partial`, whatever its quality. `live` means measured here. - Alerts say what to do in one sentence and name the threshold's source. Do not add alerts a household would ignore. - Nothing runs pip on the host. The CLI runs on Apple's Python 3.9 with the standard library only. - The dashboard names no metric. Issues are declared in each pack's `issue.yml`, ordered by `NODE_ISSUES` and served at `GET /issues`. The node computes and the page draws. - Do not put the node's database on IPFS. Only the daily export goes to the commons. - Peers never roll up, and never drive an alert or a report line. Custody, a generated column (`kind='child' OR (local AND kind<>'peer')`), is the only thing a cell may count. - State is never upgraded by aggregation. A parent's cell is `partial` if any input was. - Exact place never leaves. A coarse cell may, and says how coarse. The Reticulum announce is an H3 cell never finer than resolution 6, roughly 3 km across. - Exactly one node per pilot writes to the Index's spine. - `act` needs the person's own words. It has no default note and refuses a placeholder. ρ is the share of act-level alerts a human answered, and a row written without anything a human said is a model measuring itself. If they did not tell you what they did, ask.

title: Bring your own agent · Reading the node well
text: `status.errors` is per loop: a key present means that loop failed on its last run. `sensors[].local` means the person's own and at this node, both. "Outside" means their own outdoor sensors, else the three nearest public references, else the model, in that order everywhere. `cells[].state` is provenance: `live` is measured here, `partial` is derived, modelled or not yet backed by enough data, and a cell with no source is absent. Do not fill what cannot be measured. The tone `AGENTS.md` asks for: "Plain sentences. One at a time. Say what you know, say what you do not."

title: Bring your own agent · Where this leads
text: [MCP](mcp.md) lists every tool with its arguments and what it records. [The bot](bot.md) is the model that lives on the node and answers the household on Telegram.

title: Alerts
text: An alert is the node asking a person to do something. When a reading crosses a line, the node sends the household one plain message, then records what somebody did about it. Every answer is a row in `actions`, and [ρ](rho.md) is counted from those rows. The node has two ways of turning rules into messages, chosen with `ALERT_ENGINE`: | `ALERT_ENGINE` | what happens | |---|---| | `rules` | the default. Every rule sends on its own, each with its own cooldown. Anything else typed here behaves as `rules` | | `shadow` | the rules keep sending, and the [event engine](#the-event-engine) runs beside them: it records each message it would send in `event_messages`, with the reason it was held, and sends nothing | | `events` | the event engine sends the heat and air messages, one per event. The heat and air-quality rules still record their alerts (the dashboard and Home Assistant read those) but stop sending. Every other rule and the reports are unchanged |

title: Alerts · From a rule to a message
text: Every 60 seconds the rules loop runs each loaded rule (the five in `config/rules.yml` and every pack's `rules.yml`) as the read-only database role `planetai_ro`, which can read every table but `settings` and write nothing. Every row a rule's SQL returns is a candidate alert for the `sensor_id` in that row, or for `node` if the row has none. A rule that declares a `kind:` belongs to the event engine and is skipped here. For each candidate: 1. **Cooldown.** If an `alerts` row for the same rule and sensor is newer than `cooldown_minutes` (default 60), nothing happens. 2. **Message.** The template for `ALERT_LOCALE` (falling back to English) is filled with the row's columns by Python's `str.format`, and `{line}` with the rule's `watch.over`. A `None` renders as a dash. A template that does not fit its row is sent as the raw template. 3. **Record.** The alert is inserted into `alerts` and handed to every pack's `on_alert` hook whatever its level (the `home-assistant` pack publishes it there). From here it is on the dashboard. 4. **Send.** It goes out through `notify()` only if its level reaches `ALERT_LEVEL` and quiet hours do not hold it. On `ALERT_ENGINE=events` a heat or air-quality alert is not sent at all; the engine sends instead. How to write a rule, with every key, the tables its SQL may read and the lint that checks it, is on [Packs](packs.md#rules).

title: Alerts · Levels
text: | level | meaning | under `rules` | |---|---|---| | `act` | something needs doing | always sent, even in quiet hours, and also to the LoRa mesh and Reticulum where they are set up | | `warn` | something changed | sent only if `ALERT_LEVEL` is `warn` or `info` | | `info` | everything else | sent only if `ALERT_LEVEL` is `info`; otherwise it waits for the next report | `ALERT_LEVEL` (default `act`) is the floor for interrupting a person, and `planetai report level warn` lowers it without a restart. Below the floor an alert is still recorded, still drawn on the dashboard, and still in the bundle the next [report](report.md) is written from.

title: Alerts · Quiet hours
text: `QUIET_HOURS=1` (default) holds everything but `act` between `QUIET_FROM` (22) and `QUIET_TO` (6), local time from `NODE_TZ`, wrapping midnight when the start is after the end. A report due inside quiet hours is stored with `held_quiet` and not sent; the next one that goes out covers the held hours. The event engine is stricter: inside quiet hours it sends only `danger`.

title: Alerts · The event engine
text: Under `rules` one cooking event or one hot afternoon can send a dozen messages. The event engine (`docs/SPEC_alerts.md`) folds the rows of the rules that declare a `kind:`, today those of the `heat` and `air-quality` packs, into one event per issue, and sends one message for the event as it opens, escalates and clears. An event is a row of `alert_events`. It opens at the first candidate over its line. A candidate under the line but inside the margin keeps an open event open and never opens one. The event **escalates** when its kind climbs (`ahead`, then `unusual` or `spike`, then `sustained`, then `danger`), when its level rises, or when its value is clearly past what it last said (2 °C for heat, 25 µg/m³ for air). It does not escalate twice within three hours unless it climbs into danger. Danger already said is said again only when the value is clearly worse (air doubles, heat passes the peak by 2 °C), and never within 30 minutes. The event **clears** when no candidate has been seen for 30 minutes, with an all-clear if it ever sent anything. These gaps replace the rules' cooldowns. Every message, sent or held, is a row of `event_messages` with its reason (`open`, `escalate` or `clear`) and what held it (`quiet`, `ceiling` or `level`). Whether a message is sent: | message | held by | |---|---| | `danger` | nothing: quiet hours, `ALERT_LEVEL` and the ceiling do not hold it | | anything else | `ALERT_LEVEL`; quiet hours (`QUIET_HOURS`, `QUIET_FROM`, `QUIET_TO`); and the ceiling, once `ALERT_MAX_PER_DAY` messages (default 4) have gone out that local day | | an all-clear | quiet hours only; it does not count against the ceiling | A held message is still recorded, and the alerts the old rules record reach the next [report](report.md). Each message is the story and, under 👉, one action chosen from the issue's own list by what is true now: inside against outside, the hour, and what the home has (`HOME_HAS`: `purifier`, `ac`, `fan`, `windows`). An action the home cannot use is not offered, and a reading the node does not have never makes an action eligible. With no usable action the message is the story alone, and an all-clear carries none. An event is answered with three buttons in `ALERT_LOCALE`: **Done** (`acted`), **Not now** (`acknowledged`) and **Doesn't fit** (`dismissed`). Telegram draws them once the bot has announced itself (`TELEGRAM_BUTTONS=1`, see [The bot](bot.md)), and the dashboard draws each open event once in Decide. Each press is one `POST /actions` with an `event_id`. The buttons show while the event's `asking` is true: until somebody answers, and again after a Not now once its three hours run out. On the dashboard the action is chosen again from the readings as they are now; the message that was sent keeps its words. On a node on `shadow` or `events`, an issue's state follows its event: `act` while the event is open and unanswered (and for `danger`, answered or not), `notable` once somebody answers it, for the `warn`-level air spike, and for 24 hours after it clears. The old heat and air alerts there no longer count as open asks.

title: Alerts · What an alert says
text: Three paragraphs separated by blank lines: what is happening, what it means for the people in the house, and what to do. The first line opens with one emoji, and the level's icon is not added in front of it. From the heat pack, whose `{line}` is the rule's own `watch.over`: ``` 🚨 Dangerous heat at Kitchen: it feels like 41 °C, past the danger line here, 40 °C. This is heatstroke territory. The body cannot shed heat at this level, and it goes wrong fast. Cool the room or leave it. Wet skin, a fan, shade, water. Do not leave anyone alone in it. ``` A rule names its threshold's source in its pack's README, and the sentences carry the numbers its SQL returned. A rule may not print a number its SQL did not compute. On the classic dashboard, which is what a node on `rules` shows in Decide, a third paragraph that opens with 👉 is drawn on its own on the alert card as "what this node suggests". The `trust/` and `nearby` rules, among others, open it so. The `air-quality`, `heat` and `fire` rules do not, so their cards say there is no suggestion, and the page does not invent one. An alert asks for nothing back and carries no id. The test alert (`POST /test-alert`, `planetai test-alert`) is the exception: it ends with `👉 Reply /act N to show me how you close the loop.` when the bot runs, or `👉 In the terminal, planetai act N records that you closed the loop.` when it does not.

title: Alerts · Languages
text: `ALERT_LOCALE` is `en`, `id` or `es`. Every rule with a message carries all three: the five core rules and the 33 messaged rules in the packs that ship. The report, the test alert and the Telegram bot's own replies follow the same setting; the bot's few fixed lines fall back to English for `id`. The presets set `id` for Bali, `es` for Menorca, Barcelona and Santiago, and `en` for Boston and Delhi.

title: Alerts · Where alerts go
text: `notify()` sends to Telegram every alert that reaches it, prefixed with the level's icon (ℹ️ ⚠️ 🔴) unless the text opens with its own sign. An `act` heat or air alert that weighs on someone ticked under *Who is in the house* ends, in Telegram only, with one line such as "This matters more here: you said there is a child under five." That line never goes to the mesh, Reticulum, Home Assistant or the stored text. An `act` alert also goes to the LoRa mesh (first line only, with `MESH_ALERTS=1`) and to the Reticulum bridge for LXMF delivery. Home Assistant is the `home-assistant` pack's `on_alert` hook, which hears every recorded alert whether it was sent or not. Setting each one up is on [Channels](channels.md).

title: Alerts · The rules the core knows
text: The core names no metric. Its rules in `config/rules.yml` are about the instruments. Two say whether a sensor is heard at all: | rule | level | cooldown | fires when | |---|---|---|---| | `sensor_silent` | warn | 720 min | a local sensor's newest reading is more than 90 minutes old (`silent_minutes > 90`; `trust/channel_dead`, below, checks the values) | | `daily_pulse` | info | 100000 min | once, on an old node. The report replaced it, and it stays so existing nodes lose nothing until they update | and three, under [Trust](#trust), whether what it says can be believed. Every other rule (`air-quality/indoor_pm25_high`, `heat/heat_danger`, `nearby/only_here` and the rest) is a pack's, and is listed with its condition and cooldown on [Packs that ship](packs-reference.md).

title: Alerts · Trust
text: Whether the node's own sensors are telling it the truth: coverage over the last week, channels that have stopped changing under a kit that still reports, and collocated sensors that disagree about the level. Its three rules are the core's, at the end of `config/rules.yml`, and run on every node. They were the `trust` pack until 22 October 2026 and keep its ids, `trust/channel_dead`, `trust/coverage_low` and `trust/peer_disagreement`, so an alert already sent keeps its cooldown and its history. There is no cell: a trust score is a fact about the node's instruments, and a cell for it would invite tuning the score instead of fixing the sensor. Every rule joins the same `seasoned` gate, a sensor whose first reading in the last 30 days is more than seven days old, because a day says more about the weather than about the instrument. All three rules are `info` with a seven-day cooldown, so they speak in the week's instrument paragraph and never interrupt an evening. | rule | level | cooldown | fires when | |---|---|---|---| | `trust/channel_dead` | info | 10080 | a local `kind='sensor'` channel with role `ambient` or `enclosure` has all 24 of the last 24 hourly buckets present and flat (`max − min = 0`), the flat value is not 0, the kit reported within 2 hours, and another ambient channel on the same kit moved | | `trust/coverage_low` | info | 10080 | a seasoned local ambient comparable channel reported for under 60% of the 168 hours in 7 days | | `trust/peer_disagreement` | info | 10080 | two seasoned local ambient comparable sensors within 50 m, each with at least 100 buckets in 7 days, have a 7-day mean ratio outside 0.85 to 1.15 and an absolute difference at or above a per-metric floor (5.0 for `pm1`, `pm25`, `pm10`; 2.0 for `temp`; 5.0 for `humidity`; 0.3 kPa for `pressure`; else 15% of the pair mean). One row per pair, `sensor_id = a\|b` | `channel_dead` reads values, not timestamps, because Smart Citizen's per-reading `recorded_at` is null and a frozen channel still gets a fresh timestamp on every poll. A full day of flat buckets is longer than any night, so a light channel at dusk does not trip it. The PM floor in `peer_disagreement` is Plantower's own ±10 µg/m³ below 100 µg/m³, halved. `GET /trust`, which the trust card and the agent's health check read, counts a sensor's frozen channels by running `trust/channel_dead`'s own SQL, so the card and the alert say the same thing. Until 22 October 2026 it kept a copy of the older test, six flat hours out of 24, and called a light channel frozen every night. `peer_disagreement` cannot tell a badly sited sensor from a badly calibrated one, which is why its message asks the reader to swap the two units for a day instead of naming the wrong one. They do not see PurpleAir's `channel_disagreement` or Meshtastic's `altitude_m`, which never gets a role. None of the thresholds has met a burn season.

title: Alerts · Answering an alert
text: An alert's `acted_at` is null until somebody answers it. An answer is a row in `actions` with a stage, an actor and a note; the six stages, and which of them count in ρ, are on [ρ](rho.md#stages), and every way of recording one is under [Recording an action](rho.md#recording-an-action). `POST /actions` takes `acknowledged`, `acted` and `decided` for an `alert_id`, and refuses the rest with a 400. Given an `event_id` instead (not both), it takes `acknowledged`, `acted` and `dismissed`, writes one row with the `event_id` and no `alert_id`, and answers 404 for an event that does not exist. ρ and the funnel count an event's answer; `GET /effect` does not, because it joins `actions` to `alerts`. A `decided` row closes no alert and counts in neither ρ nor the funnel; the node keeps watching. It changes the record: a household that looked, decided and did not manage it no longer leaves the same trace as one that never looked. With `DECISION_REQUIRED=1` (Set up → Alerts, off by default), `POST /actions` answers an `acted` with no earlier `decided` row for the same alert with a 409, whichever way the act came in. Turn it on only where everybody answering has a screen to decide on, because the radio, the terminal and the bot have none. It does not apply to an event's buttons.

title: Alerts · Conditions that are not events
text: A heat alert is a condition that holds for hours, and the ratio test between inside and outside cannot tell a stopped stove from an opened door. Under `rules` every alert is an event with a cooldown: an `alerts` row has no notion of clearing. The dashboard marks an open act-level alert as *current* only while its condition still holds (the house over the line, or the alert under two hours old), and otherwise says the reading came back on its own and the alert is still open. The event engine does clear, but its events are rows of their own, in `alert_events`. For the old alerts, what the node has is the derived `measured` stage and `GET /effect`, which counts per rule how many acts were followed by the condition stopping. No rule carries a `recovery` block.

title: Alerts · Reading them
text: `GET /alerts?limit=50` lists the most recent with `id, ts, rule_id, sensor_id, level, text, acted_at`, and is where an alert's id comes from. `GET /actions` lists every answer with its stage, actor and note, and answers only a token or the machine itself, because a note is a household's own words about its own house; `GET /actions?events=1` adds the answers given to events, with their `event_id`. `GET /issues` carries the events as `events`: what is open, its action chosen from now, the message it sent, its latest answer, whether it is still `asking`, and the alerts it covers. `planetai status` shows the last three alerts and ρ. On the dashboard, Decide draws each open event once, and each open alert on a node on `rules`. *What was asked, and what was answered* is the record of what was sent and answered, and *What was decided, and by whom* is the ledger of answers. The report's second part says, per room, where the window's act alerts stand now.

title: Alerts · Where this leads
text: The node can now ask. Next, choose where the asking reaches people: [Channels](channels.md) sets up Telegram, the LoRa mesh, Reticulum and Home Assistant. Then [ρ](rho.md) is how the node measures whether the asking worked.

title: HTTP API
text: Every node exposes the same API on port 8080. The dashboard, the `planetai` command, the MCP tools, a NAS pulling backups, Home Assistant and a parent node are all clients of it, and none of them has a private path in. A request carries a token as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` or carries nothing, and the `SHARE_LEVEL` setting decides what a request with nothing may read. The port is published on every interface of the host (`APP_PORT`, default 8080); Postgres listens on `127.0.0.1:5432` only. The node speaks plain HTTP, the tailnet encrypts the hop, and the [sharing page](sharing.md) says what to do on a network that is not a tailnet. Answers are JSON unless a route says otherwise. A request that asks for gzip, as every browser does, gets JSON, scripts and styles above 1 kB compressed; `/mcp`, the `/ask` stream, the backups and the images are sent as they are.

title: HTTP API · Access rules
text: A request is trusted when it comes from loopback or carries a household token: `ADMIN_TOKEN`, `BACKUP_TOKEN` or `ACT_TOKEN`. An untrusted request is checked against the allowlist for the current `SHARE_LEVEL` and gets 403 when its path is not on it. The handler then makes its own token check, if it has one. Each route below names its class. | Class | Who is answered | |---|---| | `public` | Anyone, at every `SHARE_LEVEL`. | | `open` | Loopback or a household token; anyone else only at `SHARE_LEVEL=open`. | | `token` | Loopback or a household token. | | `admin` | `ADMIN_TOKEN` only, from loopback too. | | `pull` | `ADMIN_TOKEN` or `BACKUP_TOKEN`, the read-only token for a NAS. | | `act` | Loopback with no token; from anywhere else `ACT_TOKEN` or `ADMIN_TOKEN`. | | `children` | `AGGREGATE_TOKEN`, which a parent gives its children. It opens `POST /aggregates` and `POST /events` and nothing else. | The `off` allowlist, the default, is `/`, `/ui`, `/tester`, `/health`, `/llms.txt`, `/settings`, `/export`, `/presence`, `/nodes`, `/offers` and anything under `/static/`. The `open` allowlist adds `/stats`, `/sensors`, `/observations`, `/alerts`, `/series`, `/sparks`, `/rho`, `/cells`, `/packs`, `/trust`, `/nearby`, `/forecast`, `/earth`, `/earth/change.png`, `/earth/year.png`, `/earth/frame.png`, `/report/latest`, `/readings`, `/reach`, `/shape`, `/effect`, `/history`, `/exports`, `/sources`, `/ask`, `/ask/status`, `/docs/search`, `/geo/cell`, `/learned/place`, and anything under `/exports/`, `/issues`, `/sources/` or `/ground/`. The pack routes among them (`/offers`, `/nearby`, `/forecast` and the `/earth` paths) are put there by their pack's `pack.yaml` (`share:`). Any other value counts as `off`. The lists match the path whatever the method, so at `open` an anonymous `POST /readings` reaches the handler and gets 401. A path with no route also gets 403. Tokens travel in the `Authorization` header only, never in a query string, and are compared in constant time. `ADMIN_TOKEN` is in `.env`, the other three in settings, and `planetai ui` prints them. An optional `X-Agent` header names the caller; `PUT /settings` writes it to the ledger. Loopback is the socket's peer address, never a header: `X-Forwarded-For` is not read, so a proxy in front of the node does not make its clients loopback. Inside Docker that is the node's own MCP tools and a shell in the container. A browser on the machine hosting the node arrives from the Docker bridge and is treated like any other client on the network. An untrusted caller gets less, in four ways: - Room names: each local sensor's `room`, `name` and `source_name` become `Room A`, `Room B`, `Sensor 1` and so on, in every field and sentence. Alert sentences written under older names are left out: `/alerts` answers `text: null`, and so do the alert texts in `/issues`. - Positions: nothing finer than the node's resolution-8 cell: `/health` and `/export` carry its centre, the household's own sensors in `/sensors` and `/stats` stand there (a child's at its own cell's centre), and other sensors are rounded to 3 decimals. `/forecast` and `/earth` carry the exact point and are `open`, while `/place/geojson` and most `/geo/` routes are `token`. - Private values: a channel a pack declares `private`, such as the counts of what a home keeps, is in `/readings`, `/history`, `/series`, `/sparks` and `/observations` only for `ADMIN_TOKEN`, and in `/stats` for `ADMIN_TOKEN`, `ACT_TOKEN` or loopback. A request carrying `X-Agent` never gets one. - Who answered: the `actor` and `note` of every answer in `/issues` are null. Timestamps are ISO 8601 with an offset: `NODE_TZ` for what comes from the database, UTC for what the node stamps itself (`last_poll`, `generated`, `as_of`, `observed_at`).

title: HTTP API · Errors
text: The middlewares answer `{"error": "..."}`. A share-level 403 names the level and the path, and says the fix when there is one: ```json {"error": "this node is set to SHARE_LEVEL=off, so /alerts answers only this machine or a request carrying a token. Set SHARE_LEVEL to open in the dashboard's Set up view to let anything on your network read it."} ``` For a path no level opens it ends "No share level opens this one, so it always needs a token from anywhere but the node itself." `/mcp` without the admin token is 401 `{"error": "the agent surface needs Authorization: Bearer <ADMIN_TOKEN>"}`. Some routes are a pack's, served from `packs/<id>/routes.py`: `/forecast` (forecast), `/nearby` (nearby), `/earth`, `/earth/change.png` and `/earth/year.png` (earth), `/earth/frame.png` (earth-engine), every `/captures` route and `/species` (eyes), and `/things` and `/offers` (things). While its pack is off on the node, such a route answers 404 `{"detail": "the <pack> pack is off on this node"}`. Handlers answer `{"detail": "..."}`. The token checks: | Check | Token not set on the node | Wrong or missing in the request | |---|---|---| | `admin` | 403 ``ADMIN_TOKEN is not set in .env; run `planetai ui` to create one`` | 401 `bad or missing admin token` | | `pull` | 403 `no BACKUP_TOKEN or ADMIN_TOKEN set on this node` | 401 `bad or missing token` | | `act` | 403 ``no ACT_TOKEN or ADMIN_TOKEN set on this node; run `planetai ui` to create one`` | 401 `closing a loop from off this machine needs Authorization: Bearer <ACT_TOKEN>` | | `children` | 403 `this node accepts no children: set AGGREGATE_TOKEN in .env and give it to them` | 401 `bad or missing Authorization: Bearer <AGGREGATE_TOKEN>` |

title: HTTP API · Status
text: The routes a screen asks first, to know whether the node is up and which version and cell it is. ### GET /health Access: public What every screen in the house polls. Answers at every `SHARE_LEVEL` and never makes an outbound request of its own. Returns `ok` (true once a poll has run), `node`, `version`, `schema`, `uptime_s`, `lat`, `lon`, `position` (`cell` or `point`), `city`, `polls`, `last_poll`, `last_error`, `ingested`, `errors` (each loop's last error), `locale`, `tz`, `cell` (`{id, res, edge_m, caption}`, null before setup), `docs`, `mcp` and `llms`. With their features on it adds `mesh` (`MQTT_HOST`), `direct` (`MQTT_HOST` with the smartcitizen pack on), `reticulum` (`RETICULUM_URL`) and `release` (`{latest, current, newer, checked, asked}` from the hourly check, with `UPDATE_CHECK=on`). `schema` starts with `unreachable` when the database refuses the app, usually a wrong password after a reinstall; `planetai doctor` says why. ```json {"ok": true, "node": "bayu-ungasan", "version": "v0.90.0", "schema": "0.61", "uptime_s": 86121, "lat": -8.825, "lon": 115.159, "position": "cell", "city": "bali", "polls": 287, "last_poll": "2026-10-20T08:35:02+00:00", "errors": {}, "locale": "id", "tz": "Asia/Makassar", "cell": {"id": "...", "res": 8}, "docs": "https://planetai.fab.city/docs/", "mcp": "/mcp", "llms": "/llms.txt"} ``` ### GET /health/sources Access: token The sources every node needs, each running or not, and for each that is not, the one thing to do. `planetai doctor`, Set up and the MCP `health_check` all show it. The rows are `own-sensors`, `alerts` (Telegram), `nearby-stations`, `weather`, `satellite-air`, `backup` and `map`. `?backup_age=` passes the minutes since the newest dump where the backups really are (`-1` for none), as `planetai doctor` measures it on the host. Returns `{ok, missing, sources: [{id, name, state, ok, minutes, age, detail, fix, setup, command, why}]}`. `state` is `ok`, `missing`, `quiet` (nothing inside its window), `waiting` (no poll finished yet), `na` or `elsewhere` (backups the container cannot see). A row with `ok: false` carries a `fix`, the Set up section it is in (`setup`) and the `planetai` command that does it. ### GET /llms.txt Access: public Plain text for an agent handed the node's address: the purpose, the version, the read routes, `/mcp` and what it needs, and the documentation's URLs. It says nothing about the house. ### GET /presence Access: public What the node announces about itself on Reticulum, read by the bridge container, which has no token. `{"enabled": false}` unless `RETICULUM_PRESENCE=1`, then `{enabled: true, node, cell, res, version, kind}`, with `cell` coarsened to `RETICULUM_PRESENCE_RES` (default 3, never finer than 6). ### GET /nodes Access: public The nodes the programme lists, from `registry.json` on the repository's `main`, read every hour. Returns `{read, from, nodes, error?}`, and each node has `name`, `place`, `scale`, `operator`, `since`, `cell` and `ll` (`[lon, lat]` to one decimal). `UPDATE_CHECK=off` reads nothing and serves an empty list. ### GET /machine Access: token The machine under the node, read from `/proc` and `/sys`: `arch`, `system`, `cores`, `load`, `cpu_busy_pct`, `memory`, `container_memory`, `temperatures`, `uptime_s`, `python` and `database`. On macOS that is the container engine's virtual machine, and `seen_as` says so. ### GET /storage Access: token How much room the node takes: `database_bytes`, `readings`, `readings_last_7_days`, `bytes_per_reading`, `growth_bytes_per_day`, `out_bytes`, `exports_bytes`, `backups` (with `keep_days` from `BACKUP_KEEP`), `disk` and `days_left`, the free space less what backups will take, divided by the daily growth. Nothing is pruned, so the readings are what grows.

title: HTTP API · Pages and files
text: The dashboard and the files it loads, sent with `cache-control: no-cache` so a screen follows the new version after `planetai update`. ### GET / Access: public The dashboard, the same as `/ui`. ### GET /ui Access: public The dashboard: the five doors by default, the older dashboard with `?layout=classic`, the phone page with `?layout=mobile` (or `walk`). All of them read the same routes with the same token. ### GET /tester Access: public The sensor bench, the same page as `makingsense.fablabbali.com/test/`, reading this node's `/health`, `/sensors`, `/readings` and `/nodes`. It reads boards over USB only at `http://localhost:8080/tester`, where the browser counts the page as secure. 404 when the build does not ship it. ### GET /static/{name} Access: public The files the dashboard cannot inline, by name only; any other name is 404 `no such asset`. The names are `node-ground.svg`, `jetbrains-mono-latin.woff2`, `FunnelSans-VariableFont_wght.ttf`, `Figtree-VariableFont_wght.ttf`, `Figtree-Italic-VariableFont_wght.ttf`, `dashboard.js`, `dashboard.css`, `d3.min.js`, `plot.umd.min.js`, `planetai-theme.css`, `tokens.css`, `signs.svg`, `kilometre-cells.json`, `learn.json`, `maplibre-gl.js`, `maplibre-gl.css`, `deck.gl.min.js`, `qrcode.js`, `mobile.html`, `mobile.js`, `walk.js`, `world-land-110m.json`, `docs_site.json`, and `doors-<name>.js` for `load`, `nodegeo`, `core`, `fig`, `now`, `placemap`, `place`, `data`, `flow`, `wallmap`, `wall`, `node` and `setup`. `node-ground.svg` is drawn from `NODE_LAT` and `NODE_LON` when they are set, and `?variant=paper` draws it in the paper register. ### GET /static/fonts/jetbrains-mono-latin.woff2 Access: public The mono font, at the fixed path `planetai-theme.css` asks for.

title: HTTP API · Sensors and readings
text: These routes read what the node has measured, from the sensor list down to raw readings and hourly means. ### GET /sensors Access: open Every sensor this node reads, its position, and where its numbers come from: `sensor_id`, `source`, `name`, `room`, `source_name`, `lat`, `lon`, `indoor`, `local`, `custody`, `kind`, `scale`, `cadence`, `meta`. An untrusted caller gets no `room` or `source_name`, and `meta` cut to `licence`, `attribution`, `model`, `dataset`, `network`, `note` and `corrected`. A `facility` row, a fab lab, keeps its public description too. ### PATCH /sensors/{sid} Access: admin Names the room a sensor is in: `{"room": "Kids"}`, at most 40 characters, or `null` to get the platform's own name back. The room becomes the sensor's `name` everywhere, the platform's name stays in `source_name`, and alerts already sent keep their words. Returns `{ok, sensor: {sensor_id, name, room, source_name}}`. ### GET /readings Access: open Raw readings, newest first, as `{ts, sensor_id, metric, value}`. Filters `?sensor_id=` and `?metric=`; `?limit=` 1 to 10000, default 200. ### POST /readings Access: admin A phone or a DIY pod on the LAN posts raw readings. The sensor becomes a local sensor, so its values can fire act-level alerts and enter live cells, and that is why this needs the admin token. ```json {"sensor": {"sensor_id": "phone-abc", "source": "mobile", "name": "kitchen phone", "lat": -8.827, "lon": 115.157, "indoor": true, "meta": {}}, "readings": [{"ts": "2026-10-20T08:30:00+00:00", "metric": "pm25", "value": 12.3}]} ``` Only `sensor.sensor_id` is required. `source` defaults to `contributor`, `indoor` to false, `ts` to now, and a duplicate `(sensor_id, metric, ts)` is ignored. Returns `{"accepted": <n>}`. ### GET /stats Access: open Rolling statistics per sensor and metric over 24 hours, for sensors only: `last`, `last_ts`, `silent_minutes`, `mean_15m`, `mean_1h` and `mean_24h`, with the sensor's `indoor`, `local`, `kind`, `scale`, `lat`, `lon` and `name`. Local first; slow sources are in `/observations`. ### GET /observations Access: open The latest value of each slow source and metric, such as a city statistic, a model point or a survey: `sensor_id`, `metric`, `value`, `ts`, `name`, `kind`, `scale`, `local`, `cadence`, `meta`. ### GET /trust Access: open One row per local sensor for the trust card: `{sensor_id, name, coverage_7d, frozen_channels, age_hours}`. `coverage_7d` is the share of the last 168 hours it reported in, and `frozen_channels` is how many of its channels the core rule `trust/channel_dead` names right now, from that rule's own SQL (a full day flat while the kit still talks, see [Alerts](alerts.md#trust)). ### GET /history Access: open Every reading of one metric from one sensor, oldest first, for series that are not hourly. `?sensor_id=` and `?metric=` are required, `?limit=` 1 to 5000 (default 500). Returns `[{ts, value}]`. ### GET /series Access: open Hourly means as aligned arrays: local indoor, everything outdoor, and the model (`cams-point`). `?metric=` (default `pm25`) and `?hours=` 1 to 168 (default 24). Returns `{metric, hours, buckets, indoor, outdoor, model}`, null where there is no data. ### GET /sparks Access: open Hourly means per sensor, on the same buckets and parameters as `/series`. Returns `{hours: [bucket, ...], series: {sensor_id: [mean or null, ...]}}`. ### GET /reach Access: open How far back the node's own record goes, per kind of source: `[{kind, oldest, newest, buckets, sources, days}]`, from `readings_1h`. ### GET /shape Access: open The day this place usually has: one mean per local hour of day, over the whole record, indoor apart from outdoor. Only this node's own sensors (`local`) count. `?metric=` (default `pm25`). Returns `{metric, days, first, last, hours, windows}`, each hour `{hour, indoor, outdoor, n}`. `windows` says what the record can support: `day` from 7 days, `week` from 14, `month` from 60, `year` from 365. > **Careful.** At `SHARE_LEVEL=open` anyone on the network reads this house's indoor hours here.

title: HTTP API · Issues
text: The one document a client draws. A page, a Telegram handler or a wall screen reads `/issues` and does no arithmetic of its own. The whole `/issues` prefix is on the `open` list and not on `off`, because it carries 15-minute means and alert texts. ### GET /issues Access: open Every issue this node declares, computed: state, values by distance, the line, attribution, a sentence in each locale, open alerts and series. Nothing in it came from a model. The order is `NODE_ISSUES`, and an issue the node does not watch appears with `watched: false`. Returns `{schema: "issues-v0", order, undeclared, dropped, headline, as_of, lead, headline_rule, distances, labels, issues, stations, stations_silent, metrics, asks, digest, mesh, geometry, sections, events}`. The full key set is in `app/issues/engine.py`. - `headline` is the issue of an open alert event, or else the one with the highest state; `lead.by` says which step picked it (`event`, `state`, `moved` or `order`). - Each issue carries `state`, `reason`, `name`, `metric`, `unit`, `line`, `stack`, `series`, `buckets`, `readouts`, `provenance`, `trend`, `open_asks`, `sentence`, `title` and `tagline` (by locale), `asking` (what the house is asked about it now), `hero` (what the page draws when it leads), `about`, and `usual` with `usual_absent`. - `stations` is every station with a position: its `read` (the 15-minute mean per metric) and its hourly `series`, both only for the metrics in `metrics`, at two decimals. - `asks` is the act ledger: `acts` (every act-level alert, first line, with its `level`), `actions`, `levels` and `where`. - `digest` holds a sentence per stage and locale, the ask pane's `prompts` and the `simple` paragraph. - `sections` are the readouts enabled packs declare under `sections:`, such as the shipped `fire` and `surface-heat`. - `events` is the alert events (see [Alerts](alerts.md)): the engine (`rules`, `shadow` or `events`), the button labels, the `open` events with `asking`, the `recent` ones and `sent_24h`. ### GET /issues/days Access: open Each issue hour by hour over several local days, by the same engine. `?days=` 1 to 90 (default 7) and `?locale=` `en`, `id` or `es`. For each issue: `distance`, `series` (room, yard, ring and region), `hours` (a title and tagline per hour), `provenance`, `per_day` (`date`, `over`, `read`, `of`) and `line`, plus the `events` of the window. Wire format `days-v0`. ### GET /issues/fixtures Access: open The snapshots this node ships: `{"fixtures": ["name", ...]}`. ### GET /issues/fixtures/{name} Access: open One shipped snapshot recomputed at the hour it was captured, which the dashboard reads with `?fixture=<name>`. 404 lists the names.

title: HTTP API · Alerts and answers
text: The node asks and a person answers. Every client uses the same two routes, `GET /alerts` and `POST /actions`. Each answer is a row in the `actions` ledger, and ρ is counted from it. ### GET /alerts Access: open Alerts newest first, with the id `planetai act <id>` needs: `[{id, ts, rule_id, sensor_id, level, text, acted_at}]`. `?limit=` 0 to 1000 (default 50) and `?since_hours=` up to 2160 (0 is no bound). `acted_at` is the time of the first `acknowledged` or `acted` answer. ### GET /actions Access: token Every answer a person gave, newest first: `[{ts, alert_id, stage, actor, note}]`. `?limit=` up to 5000 (default 500), `?stage=` one stage (`settings` gives the node's own settings rows), and `?events=1` adds the answers to alert events with their `event_id`. > **Careful.** The handler checks no token of its own, so `BACKUP_TOKEN` and `ACT_TOKEN` read the household's notes too. ### POST /actions Access: act A person closes the loop. From loopback it needs no token; from anywhere else `ACT_TOKEN` or `ADMIN_TOKEN`, so someone in the house can answer without the admin key and a NAS's token cannot write ρ. ```json {"alert_id": 12, "stage": "acted", "actor": "ibu wayan", "note": "closed windows"} ``` | `stage` | What the row does | |---|---| | `acknowledged` | Somebody saw it. Counts for ρ | | `acted` | Somebody did the thing. Counts for ρ and closes the alert | | `decided` | Somebody said what they would do. Moves nothing | An alert event is answered with `event_id` in place of `alert_id`: `{"event_id": 3, "stage": "dismissed", "actor": "made", "note": "ran the AC instead"}`. Done is `acted`, Not now `acknowledged`, Doesn't fit `dismissed`. Any other stage, or both ids, is 400, and an unknown alert or event is 404. The node derives `measured` itself (see [`/rho`](#get-rho)). With `DECISION_REQUIRED=1`, an `acted` post is 409 until the alert has a `decided` row. `actor` is cut to 80 characters and `note` to 500. Returns `{"ok": true}`. ### POST /test-alert Access: admin Fires one act-level alert now through every channel, as `planetai test-alert` does. Returns `{"ok": true, "alert_id": <id>}`.

title: HTTP API · Whether it worked
text: Only the node holds both the alert and the answer, so ρ is measured here. ### GET /rho Access: open The share of act-level alerts in the last 30 days that got an `acknowledged` or `acted` answer within 24 hours, over this node's alerts and its children's. See [rho](rho.md). Returns `{window_days, days_ago, alerts_act, acted, rho, median_minutes, funnel}`. `funnel` counts this node's own alerts by stage (`asked`, `acknowledged`, `acted`, `measured`), where an `acted` alert whose rule stayed silent for the next 48 hours counts as `measured`. ### GET /effect Access: open Per rule, how many acts were followed by the condition stopping, and how long recovery took. `?days=` up to 3650 (default 365). Returns `{window_hours: 48, days, rules: [{rule_id, acted, cleared, watch, hours, measured, already}]}`. `hours` is elapsed time and says nothing about cause.

title: HTTP API · Reports
text: ### GET /report/latest Access: open The last report the node wrote, sent or held: `{schema: "report-v0", id, ts, due_local, window_hours, depth, rung, text, sent, held_quiet, fallback_reason, note}`. Before the first, every key but `schema` and `note` is null. ### GET /report/bundle Access: pull Every number the node has about a window, the document a report is written from. `?hours=` up to 168 (0, the default, means `REPORT_EVERY`). Returns `meta`, `series`, `observations`, `now`, `alerts`, `open_act`, `sensors_quiet`, `rho`, `previous`, `cells`, `rules`, `facility`, `health` and a key per pack that adds a block. ### POST /report/now Access: admin Writes and sends a report now; the next scheduled one still happens. Returns `{id, text, depth, rung, sent}`.

title: HTTP API · Context
text: What surrounds the node's own numbers: other people's stations, the forecast, the satellite record, the buildings around the address. ### GET /nearby Access: open The ring of other people's stations around this node, from what is stored, so the page never waits on someone else's server. The stations come from every enabled pack that declares `stations:` (here `bali-air-dispatch`, within `BAD_RADIUS_KM`) and reported in the last 24 hours. Returns `{ring, stations, lowest, p25, median, p75, highest, nearest_km, mine, mine_sensors, radius_km, attribution, mine_minus_ring}`, each `ring` row with its `km`, `pm25` and `reporting`. `?audit=1` also asks each pack's archive for a verdict per station. ### GET /forecast Access: open Official and model weather for this point, from `forecast-bmkg`, `forecast-om` and `forecast-gap`. `?hours=` 1 to 72 (default 24). Returns `{point, sources, hours, attribution, far_from_node}`, where `far_from_node` lists any source more than 10 km away. ### GET /earth Access: open What the earth packs hold for this node's square: `{node, enabled, years, bytes, latest, changes, frames, dir, imagery, png, lat, lon, radius_m, attribution, hint}`, from the AlphaEarth years, the land-change comparisons and the Sentinel-2 or Landsat frames. Empty until `planetai run earth fetch`, never an error; `hint` names the next command. ### GET /earth/change.png Access: open A land-change map, `?pair=YYYY_YYYY` (default the latest). 404 `no such land-change map: planetai run earth change`. ### GET /earth/year.png Access: open One year drawn from the embeddings in grey, `?year=` required. 404 `no frame for <year>: planetai run earth frames`. ### GET /earth/frame.png Access: open One year of real imagery, `?year=` required and `?source=` `sentinel` (default) or `landsat`. 404 names the years the node has. ### GET /place/geojson Access: token The buildings, uses, green and roads the place pack stored within `PLACE_RADIUS_M`, plus satellite footprints (`sat`), as `{type: "FeatureCollection", features, diag, center, radius_m}`. `?kinds=` (default `building,poi,green,road,sat`) and `?tolerance=` in degrees. Token only, because these are the exact footprints around the address.

title: HTTP API · Maps and cells
text: H3 cells and the node's own map tiles, so a browser map computes no H3 and asks nobody else. Every `/geo/` route but `/geo/cell` is `token`, since a fine cell or a ring centred on the node gives away its point. ### GET /geo/grid Access: token The cells covering `?bbox=west,south,east,north` at `?res=`, one ring wider, and the node's own cell: `{res, may_leave, edge_m, node, cells_ll}`. A box of more than 2,500 cells is 422. ### GET /geo/cell Access: open One cell's facts, by `?id=` or by `?lat=`, `?lon=` and `?res=`. `?children=` adds finer rings and `?polar=1` distances and bearings from the node. Returns `{id, res, area_m2, edge_m, parent, may_leave, is_node, cells_from_node, ring}`; an untrusted caller gets none of the fields relative to the node. ### GET /geo/measure Access: token Great-circle metres along `?path=lon,lat;lon,lat;…` (2 to 200 points), with `?from_node=` and `?each=`. Returns `{legs_m, total_m, points}`. ### GET /geo/planet Access: token Every cell on the planet at `?res=` 0, 1 or 2 (default 2), as `{res, cells_ll}`. ### GET /geo/rings Access: token Circles round the node, `?km=` up to eight distances (default `2,5,15`). Returns `{rings: [{km, ring}]}`. ### GET /ground/meta Access: open Which of the node's map layers (`vector`, `drone`, `imagery`, glyphs, wind) are in `out/ground/`, with source, licence, size and the command that fetches each. ### GET /ground/{layer}/{z}/{x}/{y} Access: open One tile of the node's own map: `vector` (OpenStreetMap, gzipped), `drone` (OpenAerialMap) or `imagery` (Sentinel-2). 204 where there is no tile. ### GET /ground/glyphs/{font}/{span} Access: open Label fonts for the vector map, as MapLibre asks for them: `/ground/glyphs/Noto Sans Regular/0-255.pbf`. ### GET /ground/wind Access: open The forecast pack's Open-Meteo wind field over the node's square, hourly for the next day: `{source, licence, attribution, fetched, n, km, lats, lons, times, speed_kmh, from_deg, at_node}`. `speed_kmh[t][row][column]` runs south to north and west to east, and `from_deg` is where the wind comes from. 204 with `FORECAST_OPENMETEO=0`.

title: HTTP API · Images and things
text: A capture is one picture with the facts a reading has: when, which cell, who, with what. The file lives in `CAPTURES_DIR`, the row in the database. These routes are on no allowlist and `BACKUP_TOKEN` opens none of them, and no picture goes into an export, an aggregate or a parent push. The file is cleaned of EXIF and GPS on arrival. ### POST /captures Access: act Adds one picture as a multipart form: `photo` (jpeg, png, heic or webp, up to 40 MB), and optionally `kind` (`microscope`, `phone`, `camera`, `drone` or `balloon`), `lat` and `lon` or a resolution-10 `cell`, `note`, `taken_at`, `actor`, and `describe=1`. GPS in the picture wins over `lat` and `lon`; with neither, the capture stands in the node's own cell. A picture already there answers `duplicate: true` and writes nothing. Returns `{"ok": true, "capture": <row>}`; 503 when `CAPTURES_DIR` is missing or not writable. ### GET /captures Access: act The images, newest first, each with `at`, the point a map draws it at. `?cell=` at any resolution, `?kind=`, `?limit=` up to 500 (default 50). ### PATCH /captures/{cid} Access: act Changes an image's `note`, `kind` or `meta`. `{"confirm": true, "actor": "<name>"}` confirms the model's findings and `{"findings": [...]}` replaces them with a person's list; both are 409 before the image is described. ### POST /captures/{cid}/describe Access: act Asks the image model (`EYES_MODEL`, in this machine's Ollama) about one image now and keeps its `analysis`: a summary and `findings` by class. The model is told never to describe or count people. With `SPECIES_MATCH=on` a plant or animal gets GBIF's `taxon` and whether the country's GRIIS checklist lists it as introduced. 409 when no image model is set, 503 when Ollama does not answer. ### DELETE /captures/{cid} Access: admin Deletes an image and its file, from loopback or with `ADMIN_TOKEN`. Returns `{"ok": true, "deleted": <id>}`. ### GET /captures/{cid}/file Access: act The picture itself; `?w=` up to 1024 answers a JPEG thumbnail. ### GET /species Access: act The species people here confirmed in images, per taxon, most counted first: `{cell, species: [{key, name, rank, class, count, images, cells}]}`. `?cell=` narrows it to one cell. ### GET /things Access: admin What this home keeps: `{things, classes, choices, summary: {things, idle, repair, offered}}`. Each thing has `class`, `name`, `count`, `used` (`weekly`, `monthly`, `yearly`, `never`), `condition` (`works`, `needs_repair`, `broken`), `offer` (`no`, `lend`, `give`), `capture_id` and `note`. ### POST /things Access: admin Adds a thing; `class` and `name` are required. Every change to the things rewrites `stock.<class>`, `idle.<class>` and `repair.<class>` as `private` readings on the `things:<node>` sensor, and nothing sends those. Returns `{"ok": true, "thing": <row>}`. ### PATCH /things/{tid} Access: admin Changes a thing's fields. Returns `{"ok": true, "thing": <row>}`. ### DELETE /things/{tid} Access: admin Deletes a thing. ### GET /offers Access: public What this home chose to lend or give: `{node, cell, contact, offers: [{id, class, name, condition, offer, count, ask}]}`, never a note, a photo or a place finer than the resolution-8 cell. `contact` and `ask` open the node's Telegram bot ([the bot](bot.md)). The offers are also in the daily export.

title: HTTP API · What the node learned
text: None of this changes a rule or a setting. An agent, a request with `X-Agent`, reads the house's learnings only while every model stays home: `AGENT_PREFER=private` and no model at an address outside your network. ### GET /learned Access: admin `{learnings, digests, checked}`. A learning's `kind` is `worked` (per act-level rule, acted against unanswered, net of the street, with a `verdict`), `usual` (the house's and the street's usual hours) or `asks` (how often a rule asks and is answered, with a `suggest`). Each has a `status`, a `statement` the node wrote from its `numbers`, and `for_whom`. Checked again once a day. ### GET /learned/place Access: open The holding `usual` learnings of scope `place`, the outdoor sensors' usual hours, for the doors' Wall. It holds nothing about the house. ### GET /learned/search Access: admin The diary and the learnings, searched: `?q=` words, `?scale=` `day`, `week`, `month` or `year`, `?limit=` up to 50 (default 12). Returns `{q, results}`. The node writes one digest for each completed day, week, month and year. ### GET /household Access: admin Who is in the house, as the household said: `older` (over 65), `under5`, `lungs`, `pregnant` and `outdoor` (works outdoors), each true or false. It sets `for_whom` in `/learned` and adds one line to a matching heat or air alert on Telegram. It changes no threshold. ### PUT /household Access: admin `{"people": {...}}`, with only those keys and only true or false. An agent may not write it.

title: HTTP API · The Index contract
text: What the node computes for the Fab City Index, and what the network has registered as measurable. ### GET /cells Access: open The Index cells this node can compute, in the `fci-cells-v0` row shape. Domain cells come from the packs' `cells.yml`, and a pack cannot claim `live` before its `min_buckets` of hourly data exist. A `Governance|<Scale>` row appears after an act-level alert in the last 30 days, `partial` while fewer than 5 were answered. ```json {"city": "bali", "cell": "Environmental|Community", "value": 18.4, "unit": "µg/m³ PM2.5 (24h mean, sensors in this node's custody)", "source": "planetai-node · pack:air-quality", "observed_at": "2026-10-20T08:35:02+00:00", "state": "live", "notes": "...", "registered": 2, "adapter": true, "reviewed": 2, "candidate": 1, "capable": 2} ``` `state` is `live`, `partial` or `mock`, and nothing downstream upgrades it. The last five fields are the registry's counts for the cell (see `/sources`). ### GET /sources Access: open The network's registry of what can be measured, a pinned copy of `awesome-fabcity-data` in `data/sources/`; at v0.90.0, pin `cd90289` with 283 entries. Filters `?pillar=`, `?scale=`, `?cell=`, `?pilot=`, `?wired=` and `?status=`, combined with AND. Returns `{registry, counts, count, sources}`, where `counts` gives every cell its `capable`, `reviewed` and `candidate` numbers (12, 17 and 55 over 19 cells at this pin). See [the source registry](sources.md). 503 when the registry is missing. ### GET /sources/{pillar}/{scale}/{slug} Access: open One registry entry, such as `economic/community/fablabs-io`. ### GET /packs Access: open The packs this node has loaded: each `pack.yaml` as parsed, with `id`, `path` and `kind` (`data` or `code`).

title: HTTP API · Federation
text: A child sends its parent hourly means and alert timestamps. Raw readings do not travel this way. See [federation](federation.md). ### GET /aggregates Access: token This node's hourly means, newest first, without `private` channels: `[{bucket, sensor_id, metric, mean, min, max, n}]`. `?hours=` up to 2160 (default 24). ### POST /aggregates Access: children A child pushes the hourly means of its own sensors, each row saying whether it is indoors. ```json {"schema": "aggregates-v0", "node": "bayu-ungasan", "scale": "community", "rows": [{"bucket": "2026-10-20T07:00:00+00:00", "sensor_id": "sc-1234", "metric": "pm25", "mean": 18.4, "min": 12.0, "max": 25.1, "n": 12, "indoor": false}]} ``` The parent keeps each mean as one reading of sensor `<node>/<sensor_id>`, of kind `child`. Returns `{"accepted": <n>}`. ### POST /events Access: children A child pushes one row per alert it raised, timestamps only: `alert_id`, `rule`, `level`, `kind`, `raised_at`, `responded_at`, `acted_at`, `measured_at`. No text, actor or sensor travels. The parent counts them in its ρ. Returns `{"accepted": <n>}`.

title: HTTP API · Open data and backups
text: ### GET /export Access: public One day of this node as open data under CC BY 4.0, for `?day=YYYY-MM-DD`: hourly means, the Index cells, the first line of each alert, ρ and, with the things pack on, the offers. Never raw readings, `private` channels or secrets, and the node's own sensors are named by role (`indoor-1`). `backup.sh` writes it every night to `exports/<node>/YYYY-MM-DD.json`. ```json {"schema": "export-v0", "node": "bayu-ungasan", "lat": -8.825, "lon": 115.159, "day": "2026-10-19", "version": "v0.90.0", "licence": "CC BY 4.0", "hourly": [{"t": "2026-10-19T00:00:00+08:00", "sensor": "indoor-1", "metric": "pm25", "mean": 11.2, "n": 12}], "alerts": [], "cells": [], "rho": {}, "offers": []} ``` ### GET /exports Access: open The daily exports on disk: `[{node, name, bytes}]`. ### GET /exports/{node}/{name} Access: open One export file. ### GET /backups Access: pull The database dumps, newest first, so a NAS can fetch the ones it lacks: `[{name, bytes, mtime}]`. ### GET /backups/{name} Access: pull One dump as `application/gzip`.

title: HTTP API · Settings
text: ### GET /settings Access: public Every runtime setting with its group, label, help and value, the bootstrap keys, and the keys the installed packs declare. Secrets are always masked, and without the admin token so is every value outside the public set (`settings.PUBLIC`). At `SHARE_LEVEL=off` an untrusted caller sees only `UI_LAYOUT` and `SHARE_LEVEL`. Returns `{unlocked, runtime, bootstrap}`; each row has `key`, `group`, `label`, `secret`, `restart`, `help`, `value`, `set`, `source`, `choices`, `default`, `outward` and `runs_code`, and a pack's key also has `pack`. ### PUT /settings Access: admin `{"KEY": "value", ...}` sets runtime settings and pack keys, in effect within about 20 seconds; a blank value goes back to `.env`. An unknown key or a value outside its choices is 400. Each call writes a `settings` row to the ledger under the `X-Agent` name (default `gui`). Returns `{changed, by, effective_within_s}`. ### GET /settings/phone Access: admin `{"act": <ACT_TOKEN>}`, which Set up draws as the QR code a phone unlocks with. ### GET /settings/raw Access: admin Every setting unmasked, for the node's own processes; `BACKUP_TOKEN` does not open it. Never call it from a browser.

title: HTTP API · The agent surface
text: ### /mcp Access: admin The MCP server over streamable HTTP at exactly `/mcp`, with `Authorization: Bearer <ADMIN_TOKEN>` on every call. Its tools call the API back on `http://127.0.0.1:8080`, as loopback. They are `status`, `health_check`, `sensors`, `context`, `readings`, `report_latest`, `report_now`, `report_bundle`, `learned`, `history`, `alerts`, `act`, `settings_get`, `settings_set`, `packs`, `cells`, `issues`, `series`, `export_day`, `run_pack_script` and `maintenance`. `act` refuses an empty note or a placeholder such as `done`. The [MCP page](mcp.md) describes each.

title: HTTP API · The ask pane
text: The dashboard's pane asks the model in Set up → Model about what the page shows, and keeps nothing it was asked or answered. It changes nothing either: a write comes back as a proposal for the person to press. See [Ask](ask.md). ### GET /ask/status Access: open Which model the pane asks first, where it runs and whether it answers: `{model, rung, where, host, running, why, rungs, leaves, tools, stored}`. `leaves` is true when an online model is in the order. 404 when no model is set up, with the tag `planetai agent local` would pull. ### POST /ask Access: open One answer, streamed as `text/event-stream`. Takes `{messages, view, mode, focus?, prompt?}`, at most 24 messages. The node builds the model's context from `/issues` with no coordinate, sensor name or id in it, and `prompt: wall` builds the Wall's public context instead and offers the model no tools, so it answers from that context without thinking. The model reads `learned` only for the admin or act token or this machine. The events are `token`, `tools`, `retry`, `proposal`, `done` and `error`. 404 when no model is set up. ### GET /docs/search Access: open This documentation searched without a model, `?q=` of 2 to 200 characters: the whole query as a phrase first, then the sections that hold most of its words, a rare word weighing more than a common one. Returns at most 20 `{page, anchor, title, snippet}`.

title: HTTP API · Wire formats
text: Each document that travels between nodes names its format in `schema`: `issues-v0`, `export-v0`, `report-v0`, `aggregates-v0`, `events-v0` and `days-v0`. A receiver never refuses on it: an unknown value is logged once and the fields it knows are read.

title: HTTP API · What the node calls out
text: | To | When | What travels | |---|---|---| | `POST {PARENT_API_URL}/aggregates` | Hourly, with a parent set | The last 2 hours of hourly means of its own sensors, with `PARENT_TOKEN` | | `POST {PARENT_API_URL}/events` | Hourly, after an alert in the last 36 hours | Alert timestamps | | Telegram | Each alert at or above `ALERT_LEVEL`, each report, once per newer release, and `getMe` once a day for the bot's name | The message, with `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` | | `planetai.fab.city/node0/get/VERSION` | Hourly, unless `UPDATE_CHECK=off` | Nothing about the house | | GitHub's `registry.json` | Hourly, unless `UPDATE_CHECK=off` | Nothing about the house | | GBIF | With `SPECIES_MATCH=on` and the eyes pack on: each new scientific name, and weekly the country's checklist and the record counts for the seven cells | A name, a country, seven cells | | `POST {RETICULUM_URL}/send` | Each act-level alert | The alert text | | MQTT | Each act-level alert (`MESH_ALERTS=1`), Home Assistant discovery (`HA_DISCOVERY=1`) | The alert's first line, discovery and state topics | The sources the node polls are on the [sensors page](sensors.md).

title: HTTP API · Where this leads
text: The [schema page](schema.md) says what each table and view holds. [Federation](federation.md) points a child at a parent, and [MCP](mcp.md) puts an agent on the node.

title: Ask the node
text: The dashboard can be asked about what it shows. A pane opens beside the page and talks to the model Set up names for this node, the same one the Telegram bot uses, through the same tools. It reads the page and the node, it explains, and it changes nothing. When a question needs a change, it puts the change on a card and the person presses it. Nothing asked or answered is kept. The pane needs a model. Without one it still searches this documentation.

title: Ask the node · Opening it
text: 1. On the classic dashboard (`/?layout=classic`), press **ask the node**, right of the modes in the header. On a phone the button is in the foot, and the pane opens as a sheet from the bottom. Learn mode opens it by itself. The five doors, the default layout, have a smaller box of their own (below). The phone page (`/?layout=mobile`) has none; its **Full dashboard** link goes to the doors. 2. The pane's header names the model and where it runs (`runs on this machine`, `runs on <host>, on your network`, or `runs online at <host>`), and says what it may do: `reads the page · records what you did · changes nothing`. If it says `no model on this node yet`, see the last section. 3. Press one of the three questions under the thread, or type one. The node writes the questions from tonight's figures: why the lead leads, the oldest open alert, what the lead's line means, then the other issues and alerts. A new three shows each time the pane opens and after each answer, and a question already asked in this conversation is not offered again. The answer arrives word by word. Under it a ledger line says which model answered and where it runs, and **read 3 things** (or however many) opens to name every read the model made and how many milliseconds each took. When the first model does not answer, the next one does, and the ledger says so. `UI_ASK` under Set up turns the pane off for everybody, with no toggle left on the page. It is `on` by default. The Wall never shows the pane. With `UI_ASK` off the doors' box is gone too, and the Wall's narration, which otherwise asks the same model every ten minutes, draws nothing and sends nothing.

title: Ask the node · The doors' ask box
text: On the five doors, the speech-bubble icon in the header, or **Ask the node** in the foot, opens a pane on its own grey, so the page's paper is only ever the data. It asks the same `POST /ask`, with the door you are on as its `view`, and draws only the words of the answer as they arrive. It reads like any chat: the box is at the bottom, each question appears as your own line with the answer under it, and the exchanges stay on screen while the tab is open. Only the new question is sent, never the ones before it. It shows no ledger line, no list of reads and no cards, so a change the model reaches for is not drawn there; make it in Set up. Type in the box and press Enter, or the arrow inside the box; Shift and Enter starts a new line, as the line under the box says. Above the box, three questions are offered, written by the node from tonight's figures (`digest.prompts` in `GET /issues`), such as "What should I know about the heat today?". With learn on, the two that the parts of the door carry come first. Pressing one asks it, and after each answer the next three come round. The line at the top of the pane says what answers. With no model set up, the box is a search of these docs: the question's words are looked up in every section (`GET /docs/search`), the rarest words weighing most, and the five best sections come back as links with a line of each. When a model answers a question you typed, the three best sections follow its answer under **In the docs**, and when it does not answer, the search answers instead and says so. When the node itself does not answer, the box says "The node did not answer. Check this screen is on the home network, then try again." **Learn this page**, in the same pane, numbers every part of the door you are on, the bar and the foot included, and lists for each one its name, its stage in the loop, what this documentation says about it, a line on what the part draws, the routes it reads, the pack that drew it, and a link to the section it quotes.

title: Ask the node · What it may do
text: | class | tools | in the pane | |---|---|---| | `read` | `status`, `health_check`, `sensors`, `context`, `readings`, `report_latest`, `history`, `alerts`, `packs`, `cells`, `issues`, `series` | run, through `/mcp` as `dashboard-chat` | | `act` | `act` | not run: a card with the page's own **I did this** form | | `admin` | `settings_set`, `run_pack_script`, `maintenance`, `report_now` | not run: a card, or a sentence naming where it is done | `settings_get`, `report_bundle` and `export_day` are read tools the pane is never given: it can be open on a wall at `SHARE_LEVEL=open`, and the person typing is not always the person who set the node up. `learned` is given only to a request carrying the admin or act token, or coming from this machine, and never to the Wall's narration, because what the house learned stays with the house. A tool result is cut at 8,000 characters, and when it is cut the model is told so, with the full length. For a count, `alerts` takes `since_hours` and answers with the count itself. After a tool result the model answers with `reasoning_effort: none`; a server that refuses the field is asked again without it, and not sent it again. A setting card says what the setting is now, what it would become, what leaves the house (the setting's own help text) and how to set it back. **turn it on** writes it with the admin token the page holds for Set up; with none held, the card asks for it and says `needs your token`. **open Set up** goes to the setting's group instead. A value the setting would refuse is not proposed, and the card offers the values it takes. An act card carries the alert's number and nothing the model wrote. What the person did is theirs to say, in their own words, because ρ is built from those sentences.

title: Ask the node · What it never sends
