text: The bar runs along the top of every door but the Wall: the node's name and place, the five doors in the order Now, Place, Node, Data, Wall, then an as-of line (`LIVE · as of 19:00`, or `CAPTURE` on a fixture, with `· locked` on a screen without a token), the **Paper** / **Dark** switch, the documentation, **Ask the node** and the gear for Set up. When a newer release is out, one small line says so ("v0.84.0 is out") and opens Set up › Updates. On a phone the bar also offers **Phone view**. The register is kept in this browser as `planetai_theme`; with nothing kept the doors follow the system's setting. The Wall is always dark. The foot closes every door but the Wall: what the node is in one line, its version, the documentation and "These pages, explained" (this page), `llms.txt` for agents, Ask the node, Set up, **Unlock this screen**, today's open export (CC BY 4.0) and links to PLANETAI, Fab City and the source. > **Gap in v0.90.0.** The doors read the node when the page opens, and again only after an answer on Now or an > unlock; nothing re-reads it while the page stays open. A Wall left on keeps the figures of the moment it was opened, > and only its narration is new every ten minutes. Reload the page, or use the classic wall, which re-reads on > `POLL_SECONDS`.

title: The dashboard · Now
text: Now reads in the order a household asks. ![The Now door: the air sentence, the day figure and the week strip](img/now.jpg "Now on node #1, seen from a screen on the house network without a token.") **Right now.** A kicker ("Right now · Heat at 19:00" and the provenance pill), then the sentence and the day as one block: the issue's sign, the node's title (no number in it) with its tagline smaller beneath, and the [day figure](#the-day-figure) with the week under it. The kicker links to the node's cell on Place ("497 m · 0.64 km² ›"). The four distances follow as one quiet line; a distance with no reading says `none` or `not recorded`. Point at an hour, drag across the day, or use the arrow keys (left and right an hour, up and down a day, End for now): the sentence, the distances and Decide follow the hour, and **Back to now** returns. **What to do.** While the node is asking (`asking` on the issue in `/issues`), a framed card: the issue, the kind of event and when it began, the peak against the line, the action the node chose in its own words, and **Done**, **Not now** and **Doesn't fit**. Once somebody has answered, the buttons go and the line under the card says who answered, when, and when a Not now asks again. An alert still true that no event stands for is drawn the same way, without buttons, because it is answered on Telegram. When nothing is asked the section is one plain line, "Nothing is asked now.", with the hour this issue is usually worst for a screen holding the admin token. A past hour shows what was open then, and is read, never answered. An issue with no line says the node only reports it and never asks you to act. **Did it work** and **Yesterday** (admin token only). For the issue on screen: the last time the node asked, what was done, what the air or heat inside did in the hours after against the street, and the node's verdict from what it learned ("It helps here.", "No clear difference here yet.", "Too early to say."), with who it matters to, or a link to say who lives here. Yesterday is the node's diary entry for yesterday, condensed from its own numbers, with a link to the whole entry on Node. **Around the house.** A row for each issue drawn by the hour, its state word, its value now and its hours over the line today; pressing one moves the page to that issue. Under them, the map of the stations around the house: each public station with its 15-minute mean, a red square beside one over the air's line, the house as one mark with its own sensors' range, and the distance rings and cells for a screen with the token. Pressing a station opens it in Data. Without WebGL the map is a rose of bearings and distances. With the admin token one line counts the things this home keeps, how many sit idle and how many need repair, and opens Data › Home. Land and coast change yearly and have no hours, so they are on Place, under **What is changing**. Now opens on the headline issue when it is drawn by the hour, else on the first issue that is. Under 480 px everything is one column, the bar is three rows of 44 px targets, and the week is one row a day, the whole row a target.

title: The dashboard · The day figure
text: Each issue with a day has one drawing of its last 24 hours. Every distance is a trace, the house heavier, and an hour with no record is a gap in its trace. The grey band is the usual for each hour, from the node's own last 14 days. The red dashed line is the issue's line, labelled in ink (`WHO 15` for PM2.5, the WHO 2021 24-hour guideline), and red ticks along the floor mark the hours over it. Hours not yet come are hatched. An alert event is a bar from when it opened to when it cleared, and its answer is a ring, green for Done. A reading above the scale is clipped and printed, so one spike cannot flatten the day. The line under the drawing says the hour in words.

title: The dashboard · The strips
text: One row a day and one cell an hour, the newest day at the bottom: the last seven days under each day figure, and every day the node holds on Historical. A darker cell is a higher reading on that issue's own scale. An hour over the line is an ink cell with a red tick on top, and an hour nothing was recorded is left empty. The figure at the end of each row is the node's own count of hours over the line that day, from `GET /issues/days`.

title: The dashboard · Place
text: The ground this node stands on. The head gives the cell's id, resolution, edge and area (and the node's position, for a screen with the token), and three views: | view | what it draws | |---|---| | **Map** | every layer with a position, on the node's own street map | | **From orbit** | the node's Sentinel-2 annual medians, then and now side by side, with the hectares that changed between them by its AlphaEarth record | | **What changed** | the hectares that changed year on year (one square per 10 ha), and what the ground within 1 km is made of: built, trees, crops, water, by satellite | **The map.** Eighteen layers in five groups sit in a strip above it: **Base** (the street map, satellite at 10 m, drone imagery), **Grid** (H3 cells at the scale in view, the cell the node stands in, what leaves by radio), **Readings** (this house's stations, public stations, model points, distance rings), **Images** (the household's images and the species confirmed in them) and **Packs** (buildings only the satellite knows, the wind, places to make, and three that have no shape on a map: the land change raster, the Index cells and nodes heard nearby, each saying where it is drawn instead). Each row has its swatch, what it draws and from where, its pack and its opacity. Five start on: the street map, the node's cell, the house's stations, the public stations and the images. A layer whose pack has nothing here says so. Nothing is labelled on the map itself: every mark leaves on a thin leader to a ruled margin, **At the house · by position**, one row per mark with its distance in metres from the node, measured by the node (`GET /geo/measure`, and `GET /nearby` for public stations). The inspector is one line under the map. With nothing pressed it says what is in view; press a station, an image, a place to make or a cell and the line gives its facts, and with the token how far it is from the node and which cell it is in. A station of this house says it counts toward the cell; a public one is shown and never counted. The scale rail (Street, Block, Cell, Village, District, Island, Radio) and the tools sit on the map: zoom, back to the node's cell, **Inspect**, **Measure** with **Done**, **From the house**, and save as PNG. The resolution drawn follows the zoom, and rungs 6 and coarser, the cells that may leave the machine, are dotted. The grid, the rings and every distance are the node's own answers from `GET /geo/*`, and the plan is `GET /place/geojson`; all of them need a token at every sharing level, because together they place the house. Without the token, the house's marks say **withheld** where they would stand and the map opens on the published cell. The street map comes from `/ground/*` once `planetai run place basemap` has run; until then Set up lists **The map of this place** under what is left to finish. **+ Add an image** (token only) opens a dialog: the file, what took it (phone, fixed camera, microscope, drone, balloon or kite), a note and your name, and whether the image model on this node describes it. The image lands where its own GPS says it was taken, else in the node's cell; the node strips EXIF and GPS from the file and keeps it. Below the map, three columns. **Where the readings come from**: how far back each kind of source reaches, from `GET /reach`, and the public stations within 5 km. **Species confirmed here**: a table of what somebody here confirmed in an image, how often, where, and GBIF's open records by others in the node's seven cells, token only. **What is changing**: land and coast with the node's sentence and figure, the Index cells, and what is not here yet (production and trade, water and soil).

title: The dashboard · Node
text: Node opens on a verdict: "Working. Last reading 19:19; 6 of 6 sensors, 10 of 20 stations heard in the last hour." A poll older than 15 minutes, a loop that failed on its last run, a sensor of its own not heard in the last hour, or, with the token, a fundamental source not running (`GET /health/sources`) turns it into "Needs a look", saying which, with a link to finish setting up. Under it, the version, uptime, readings since the restart, the cell and the time zone. ![The Node door: what comes in and what goes out](img/node.jpg "Node draws every link in and out of the machine, at its real rate.") | part | what it holds | |---|---| | **What comes in, what goes out** | the node as a hexagon, its sources on one side and what leaves on the other, replaying the last six hours in 30 s (24 hours on a press). Drawn vertically under 700 px | | **Fab City Index cells** | the Index cells this node computes from its hourly buckets, "N of 20", each with its value and provenance word | | **What it remembers** | admin token only, and never leaves the machine: the **Diary** as a table by day, week, month or year, each entry opening as the node wrote it, with a search; **What is usual** (the shape of the day inside and out, the week against the three before); **What worked**, per alert, the change inside when somebody acted and when nobody did, and the node's verdict; **Who lives here?**, five boxes that rank the learnings by who they matter to. `#node/remember/day/<date>` opens one entry | | **The nodes around it** | the nodes listed and heard by radio, then a globe at most a third of the screen high | | **Running** | the version and schema, how long since the restart and the polls since, then, with the token, the processor, memory, temperature and disk, with how long the disk lasts, and the mesh in the house | | **What this node will not do, at any stage** | the five refusals in plain words, each beside a link to where it can be checked |

title: The dashboard · Data
text: Every reading the node holds, one tab at a time, routed `#data/<tab>`. The tab bar is sticky; on a phone it wraps into 44 px targets. ![The Data door: every kind of reading the node holds](img/data.jpg "Data, Readings: one tile per kind of reading, the median of each source's latest 15-minute mean.") | tab | what it shows | |---|---| | **Readings** | every kind of reading as a tile, with the median of its sources' 15-minute means now. Press one to draw every source that reads it over 24 hours on one scale, each linked to where its source publishes it (the hourly table needs the token). Then every issue at every distance over seven days, and the hours over the line per day | | **Models and satellite** | one table: a row per value the models and the satellite give for this point, how often it is fetched, its unit | | **Home** | **Images**, newest first: when and who, what took it, the note, what the image model saw and whether somebody here confirmed it. A row opens the image to edit, confirm or delete. Then the species confirmed, and **Things**, what this home keeps, how often each is used, its state and whether it is offered (admin token). With the `eyes` or `things` pack off, its part says so | | **Ledger** | every decision, newest first, a run of the same answer as one row ("decided ×10"), who answered in words, and a filter by stage. Without a token, only the time and the stage | | **API** | every route on this node, one line each, with a search | `#data/<sensor-id>` opens a station in Readings. The diary and the Index cells are on Node.

title: The dashboard · Wall
text: The keeper's one screen for a room, always dark, read from about three metres and operated by nobody. Its map walks out from the house a scale at a time, house, street, ring and region, and under it the node's model says in plain words what is happening. It names no sensor, room or person, and shows what is asked without a button to answer it. [Wall mode](wall.md) has all of it.

title: The dashboard · Set up
text: The gear opens Set up, a page of its own with a sticky list of its twelve sections under five headings: This place (Basics, Rooms), What it reads (Sources, Packs), How it speaks (Alerts, Model), Who can see it (Sharing, Keys, This screen) and The machine (System, Machine, Updates). Point at a section, or tab to it, and it says what it is for and which settings it holds. ![Set up, locked: the sections on the left and the token form](img/setup.jpg "Set up on a screen without a token: everything is visible, nothing can be changed until it is unlocked.") | section | what is in it | |---|---| | **Basics** | what this place watches, in order; what kind of node it is; its language; how the page opens. Name, city, position and time zone are read once at start: edit `.env`, then `planetai restart` | | **Sources** | your sensors and accounts, the public stations and portals around you. A source that comes as a pack is set in its card under Packs | | **Alerts** | reports at the hours you choose, what interrupts between them, quiet hours, which engine sends the heat and air messages (`ALERT_ENGINE`), how many it may send a day (`ALERT_MAX_PER_DAY`), what this home has (`HOME_HAS`), mesh alerts, and whether an act needs a decision first | | **Model** | which model answers, on the ask pane and on Telegram alike | | **Packs** | which packs load, and one line per pack: its switch, its name and how many settings it has. **+** opens what it does and its settings, and **Open all packs** opens every one, remembered by this browser; a key the pack lists under `secrets:` is masked once saved | | **Keys** | every secret, masked once saved and never shown again | | **Sharing** | who may read this node, and everything it sends or announces beyond this machine | | **System** | tuning numbers, how the classic ground is drawn (`UI_GROUND`), the layout Arrange writes, whether [Grafana](grafana.md) is running and how to open it, and what is read once at start | | **Rooms** | the household's word for where each of its sensors is, which every alert, the report and every page then use. Never on the Wall; a screen without the token reads "Room A" and "Sensor 1", see [Sharing](sharing.md#rooms-and-sensor-names-stay-in-the-house) | | **Machine** | the machine under the node (`GET /machine`) and how long its disk lasts (`GET /storage`) | | **This screen** | the two token fields and **Unlock this screen**. With the admin token, **Show the code** under "A phone" draws a QR code that opens the phone page holding the token for closing a loop | | **Updates** | the version running, a newer release if there is one, and how to update | A save sends only the fields you edited. A value saved here is live within 20 seconds and wins over `.env`; a blank returns the key to `.env`. Every change is an `actions` row with `stage='settings'` and the actor `dashboard` (`planetai-cli` from the command line, the agent's name over MCP). If a key changed on the node after the page drew it (from the CLI, an agent or another screen), nothing is saved: the field says what the node holds now, and a second Save replaces it. The node's own refusal is printed beside its field. A change that sends something beyond this machine (the node marks those keys `outward` in `GET /settings`) or runs code here that is not the node's (`runs_code`: `PACKS_ALLOW_CODE`, or a code pack switched on) is not written at the first press. The save bar counts them, and a panel, **Before this is saved**, lists each with its new value (never a secret) and its help, with **Back** and **Save anyway**. Turning one of them off asks nothing. A pack's own keys save the same way and reach the pack at its next run, see [Configuration](configuration.md#keys-the-packs-declare).

title: The dashboard · Ask the node
text: **Ask the node**, in the bar and the foot, opens a pane at the side of the page, on its own grey. On the doors it takes one question at a time and streams the answer from `POST /ask`; Enter asks, and the three questions above the box are the node's own, written from tonight's figures. With no model set up, the box searches these docs instead. The node searches its own notes and readings first and asks a model only if one is set up: the one Set up › Model names, the same as the Telegram bot's. That is the model `planetai agent local` set up on this machine, one on another machine of yours, or an online one only when `AGENT_PREFER` allows it. It reads and changes nothing, and the node keeps nothing asked or answered. `UI_ASK=off` removes it, and the Wall never shows it. The whole of it is on [Ask the node](ask.md). **Learn this page**, the box under the question, numbers every part of the door you are on and lists what each one is: its name, its stage in the loop, what this documentation says about it, a line on what it draws, the routes it reads, the pack that drew it, and a link to the section it quotes. The bar and the foot are numbered too. With learn on, the questions under the box start with two about those parts. The words come from `learn.json`, which `tools/build_learn.py` cuts from these pages at build time, so learn mode works on a network with no route out. On the classic dashboard, learn is a mode, see [Modes](#modes).

title: The dashboard · Issues, states and distances
text: `GET /issues` is the whole of what the page knows about the place. For every issue the keeper declared in `NODE_ISSUES` (an undeclared one is still shown, as `watched: false`), the node computes a `state`: `act` (something is asked), `notable` (something changed), `quiet`, `context` (an issue that informs and never asks) or `none` (no record). The doors print those states as "act now", "worth a look", "fine", "background" and "not read". With the state come the four distances, each with its value and provenance word. The wire keys are `room`, `yard`, `ring` and `region`; the page prints house, street, ring and region. Then the sentence in three languages, with its title and tagline, the open asks (`open_asks`) and `asking`, the series for the day, the `digest`, the geometry the ladder is drawn from, the `asks` ledger, and `events`: the alert events, with what is open, its one action, its latest answer and the alerts it covers. On a node whose alert engine is `shadow` or `events`, an issue's state follows the alert events: `act` while an act-level event is open and unanswered (a `danger` event stays `act` whatever the answer), `notable` once somebody has answered it, while a warn-level event nobody answered is open, and for a day after an event clears. Whether anything is asked of the house is one answer, `asking` on each issue: the open event while it still asks, then any alert still true that no event stands for. Now, the Wall and the phone all read it. The `headline` is the issue of the most serious open event, when there is one (`lead.by` is `event`). Otherwise it is the issue with the highest state; among issues in the same state, the one that moved most in the last three hours, and an exact tie goes to the declared order. The node sends that rule as `headline_rule`. The same object comes back from the `issues` MCP tool, so an agent and the household describe the same evening in the same words. The declarations are one `issue.yml` per issue, in the pack that watches it; see [Issues](issues.md).

title: The dashboard · What a screen without a token sees
text: What a screen without a token can read is set by `SHARE_LEVEL` (see [Sharing](sharing.md)): - At `off`, the doors draw the node's name, its own sentence for the refusal and the two token fields, so a refused screen can be unlocked where it stands. On `#wall` they draw one line instead, "This screen needs sharing turned on.", because nobody operates a wall. - At `open`, the issues, the events, the stations' 15-minute means, the models, the Index cells, the satellite years and the ledger's stages and times are drawn, without who answered, what each alert said or the notes. - At every level, the map's cells and distances, the plan, the hourly table, the diary and learnings, the images and species, the things, the machine and the alerts need a token. A screen holding no token does not ask those routes at all, so it leaves no 403s in the node's log, and each locked part says why and links to Set up › This screen. A browser on the node's own machine counts as a reader on the network, because inside Docker it arrives as the bridge gateway.

title: The dashboard · The phone page
text: A phone gets its own page (`mobile.html` and `mobile.js`, which reuse the doors' loader). The choice is made once, before anything loads: a coarse pointer and a screen side under 600 px moves `/` to `/?layout=mobile`. A narrow desk window and a tablet stay on the doors, and nothing is decided again on a resize. "Phone view" and "Full dashboard" switch between them, and the browser remembers. A link to a door the phone page has no section for (`#setup`, `#data`, `#wall`) keeps the doors. ![The phone page: Now on a 390 px screen](img/phone.jpg "The phone page reads the same node in one column.") One scrollable page: - **Now**: the node's title and tagline, the reading at the household's own distance, the Decide card with its three buttons (the first answer asks for a name, kept as `planetai_actor`), the other issues as rows, and on an unlocked phone **Add an image**, which opens the phone's library. Where an image was taken is the picture's own GPS, else the phone's location if you allow it (browsers give it to https pages only), else the node's cell. - **Walk out from the house**: the map stays pinned while the story scrolls under it, one step per scale (house, street, ring, region, planet), drawing that scale's cell heavy with the smaller ones faint inside it. Each step says what that scale can: the house against its line, the street against the house, the outdoor stations, every scale on one axis, and the listed nodes on a globe. The switch on top lists every issue the node carries; a scale an issue has no reading at says so. `walk.js` and MapLibre load only as the walk nears the screen, so a slow phone gets its sentence first. `/?layout=walk` opens the same page. - **Node**: from `/health` only, so it draws even when everything else is refused. The answers need the act token; without it the card says the question went to Telegram. To unlock a phone without typing a token, use **Show the code** in Set up › This screen. At `SHARE_LEVEL=open` the walk needs no token, map included: `/ground/*` is public data (OpenStreetMap, OpenAerialMap, Sentinel-2) cut around the node, and `/geo/cell` answers without what it says relative to the node (`is_node`, `cells_from_node`, `ring_polar`, `children_polar`). At `off` it walks only on an unlocked phone. The phone page reads the node again when it is shown again and what it drew is more than five minutes old.

title: The dashboard · Times, languages and fixtures
text: Every time on the doors and the phone page is the node's own local time (`/health` `tz`), whatever zone the route wrote it in. The household's language comes from `/health.locale` (`ALERT_LOCALE`, which answers at every sharing level), and the node's sentences are drawn in English, Bahasa Indonesia or Spanish. `?fixture=<name>` replays a committed snapshot through the node's own engine, `GET /issues/fixtures/<name>`, on every layout, and shows a screen without the token only what the node would show it. Eight ship, six captures of node #1 and two derived ones where coast and land lead; `GET /issues/fixtures` lists them. `node1-2026-10-06-figures` carries the days the strips draw. `planetai snapshot` writes a new one from a running node; a snapshot missing a table the engine reads comes back with an error in place of the issues.

title: The dashboard · The classic dashboard
text: `/?layout=classic` serves `index.html` and `dashboard.js`, the dashboard the doors grew out of. The sections from here to the end of the page describe it. ### Views | view | URL | what it shows | |---|---|---| | **Now** | `#now` | the ladder, the lead, the ground, then the four stages in the order a person reads them: Decide, Observe, Act, Measure. The default | | **Historical** | `#historical` | the day this place usually has, what the satellite says year by year, how far back this node can be asked, and what the node doubts about its own sensors | | **Network** | `#network` | what moves through this node, what this place could read, what leaves by radio, the mesh and the hardware in the house, and what this node may say and send: whose word over how much ground, what each rung is worth, what this page asked of the world | | **Wall** | `#wall` | the dark register, for a screen on a wall; see [Wall mode](wall.md) | | **Arrange** | `#arrange` | Now in another mode: move a section within its stage, hide one, restore it; saved as `UI_LAYOUT` | | **Set up** | `#setup` | the settings in the same eight groups as the doors, behind a token, and every registered section with whether it is drawing | The header also carries the mode switch, **ask the node**, the Paper / Dark switch (`?register=` reads first and remembers nothing) and **↻**, "Ask the node again". The resolution travels in the URL as `?res=`, so a link into any view keeps it. Other query keys: `?view=` works as the hash does, `?state=empty` or `?state=refused` draws those states for a capture, `?worth=1` opens the ladder's fold, and on the wall `?var=` and `?vars=all`. The page re-reads `/issues`, `/health` and `/rho` every `POLL_SECONDS`, clamped to 20 to 600 seconds. A poll keeps the scroll and the open folds, and holds off while the tab is hidden, while a Set up group has an unsaved edit, and on a fixture. When a poll gets no answer the figures stay, the pill says `stale`, and the as-of line reads "Read at … · the node has not answered for N min". The asking screen is held at least `--motion-asking-hold` (3 s) on a load or a press of **↻**, never on a routine poll. > **Gap in v0.90.0.** On the classic dashboard at `SHARE_LEVEL=off`, a browser that has never stored a token draws > the refused page on every view, Set up included, so there is nowhere to enter one. Unlock the screen on the doors > (`/`), which keeps the token in the same place, then open `/?layout=classic`. ### Modes | mode | what it draws | |---|---| | **simple** | on Now, Historical and Network only. On Now: the lead in plain words, the open event with its three buttons (or an alert with **I did this**), the ground with a one-line key, one paragraph the node writes (`digest.simple`) and **also watched here**, every other issue with its value. Pressing one draws it in the lead until the page reloads. No ladder, no stage names, no figures | | **advanced** | every section registered for the view. The default | | **learn** | advanced, with a mark at each part of the page. Pressing one puts a card in the ask pane that quotes this documentation for that part, names the page and section, links out, and walks to the next with **previous** and **next**; *walk the page* starts at the first. The quotes are in English only | `UI_MODE` is what the page opens as. A reader who switches changes only their own browser, and `?mode=simple` is read first and remembers nothing. The wall has no mode switch. The classic ask pane keeps a thread in the tab until it closes, **new conversation** is pressed, or half an hour passes with no question. With no model it still searches this documentation (`GET /docs/search`).

title: The dashboard · The lead
text: The **ladder** sits above the lead: eleven rungs, one per H3 resolution from 2 to 12, opening at 8. Rungs coarse enough that a cell may leave the machine (resolution 6 and coarser, the presence floor) are dotted rather than blue, and rungs finer than the node says where it is are struck through. Each rung names its edge length, and pressing one re-draws the page at that resolution. The chip under it, "one cell here", opens a fold, *What one cell at resolution N is worth*: a log ruler from 10 m to 200 km, three hexagons to true relative scale (the rung you are on against the rungs either side), and what each thing the node speaks for costs to cover at it. Each rung is about seven times finer by area than the one above. The first thing on Now is the ladder, and under it the lead: the headline issue's kicker, its numeral and pictogram, a title with no number in it, a smaller tagline under the title, a why line and the rule. The last line gives when the numeral was read, what is open (`1 event open · heat · sustained since 13:00 · in Decide`, `nothing open · 2 cleared today`, or on the old engine `2 alerts open · in Decide`) with a link to Decide, and a pill: `live`, `stale` or `cached`. The why line ends on the node's own `headline_rule`, so a reader can check why this issue is on top. The lead draws the issue's `hero` from `/issues`, so a new issue leads the page with no change to the page. The rule's two ends are the issue's own; a reading past an end sits on it and prints its real number. Coast has a rule and no line. Land has no rule, and its last line says when the satellite looked and when it looks next. At resolution 8 one cell is 639,778 m² on node #1, about 0.64 km², with an edge of 497 m. The resolution line counts the cells this node's stations with a coordinate fall in, how many of those stations sit in the node's own cell, and how many of those are its own. It is on Network, under "What each rung is worth".

title: The dashboard · The ground
text: The section behind the lead is the node's own ground at the current rung: its cell in the cells blue, its neighbours as ink hairlines, its own stations filled and other stations hollow. A node with no `NODE_LAT` and `NODE_LON` draws the grid from `/static/node-ground.svg` and says it stands for no particular place yet. Three bases: `plan`, offline, from `/place/geojson` (the building footprints within `PLACE_RADIUS_M`, drawn in the browser, nothing leaving the house); `sat`, Sentinel-2 cloudless tiles; `osm`, OpenStreetMap tiles. Live tiles need `MAP_TILES=on` and are offered at resolution 8 and coarser. Each base's tab says what it costs before it is pressed: `sends nothing` for the plan, a count of requests for the others, and a press may only ever reduce what leaves the house. The plan needs a token at every sharing level, because it is the shape of your building. With `UI_GROUND=map` the same ground is drawn by MapLibre and deck.gl and pans and zooms, and also offers what the node keeps of its own map once `planetai run place basemap` or `planetai run earth-engine basemap` has run: `street map, on this node`, `satellite, on this node` and `drone, on this node`, each saying `sends nothing` because it is read from `/ground/*` with the page's token. Without WebGL2 the page draws the svg ground and says why. A cell is not the thing (three indoor sensors share one coordinate), containment is exact in the index and approximate on the ground, and the four distances are not four resolutions.

title: The dashboard · The sections
text: Every section is registered with the page contract: `id`, `pack`, `stage`, `title`, `reads` and `render` (or `lead`). The shell draws each one in the stage it belongs to. The loop runs observe, decide, act, measure, and Now draws Decide first. Optional keys are `order`, `needs`, `controls`, `wall`, `learn`, `notes`, `level` and `anchor`. `reads` names the routes the section's data comes from, printed beside its title as links that open the JSON it was drawn from; `tools/check_ui.py` fails a section with no `reads` or a route that neither `app/main.py`, a core router nor a pack's `routes.py` defines. A section whose `needs` are not on this node prints one line in their place ("The <pack> pack has nothing here yet: … is not on this node."), never a blank and never a guess. A section that throws says that it did not render and why, and every other section still draws. The notes every section wants to make are gathered at the foot, in *Where these numbers come from*. Four card kinds and no fifth: readout, stack, series, row. A gap in a series is a gap in the line, never a ramp across a line nobody measured. The node's own words are never uppercased: `µg/m³` once became `MG/M³` on the hero, a factor of a thousand. Twenty-four sections are registered: | stage | view | sections (pack) | |---|---|---| | **observe** | Now | The ground (place) · Every issue, at every distance · The day this place just had · The day it is about to have (forecast) · What the stations read (air-quality) | | | Historical | How far back this node can be asked · The day this place usually has · What the satellite says (earth) | | | Network | This node, and what moves through it · What this page is made of · What leaves this house by radio (reticulum) · The mesh in this house (meshtastic) · The hardware in this house (hardware) · What this place could read, and where it could go · What this page asked of the world (place) | | **decide** | Now | What to do about it | | | Network | Whose word, over how much ground · What each rung is worth | | | Historical | What the node doubts about its own sensors | | **act** | Now | What was asked, and what was answered · What was decided, and by whom | | **measure** | Now | Whether it worked · Which of these worked · Every figure on this page, and where it came from | Sections with no pack named are `core`. A section a pack registers that is on none of these lists is drawn on Now, in its own stage. ### Observe The evidence for Decide, in the order a decision reads it. "The day this place usually has" draws the strips of every day this node holds (up to 90, `GET /issues/days?days=90`), and above them, once it has 7 local days, the hour inside and the hour outside that are worst (`GET /shape`, which needs 14 days for a week, 60 for a month, 365 for a year). "How far back this node can be asked" gives the oldest and newest hourly reading per kind of source (`GET /reach`). "What this place could read, and where it could go" reads the pinned registry (`GET /sources`): how many sources are registered and how many have code here, the three counts per cell (see [The source registry](sources.md#three-counts-per-cell)), and the places to make things and designs to build. "What the stations read" lists a station silent in the last 30 days in a fold, with when it was last heard. ### Decide An event is the bot's own unit: one issue in one house, from when its rule first fires to when it clears, however many rule rows that took. Decide draws one card for each open event: the peak with its comparisons, the action the node chose, and the message it sent. The numeral is red only when the peak is past the issue's line. The action and the message are the node's words, in the household's language; in shadow the message reads "would have sent". Under the card, "from 9 rule rows" opens the rows in `alerts` the event covers. An open act-level alert that no event covers is drawn after the cards, with **I did this**. **Done**, **Not now** and **Doesn't fit** each write one answer to the event: who pressed, and when. Done closes the loop. Not now holds the card, muted, for three hours unless the reading reaches danger. Doesn't fit asks one optional question, what you did instead, and keeps the answer as the note. Once somebody has answered, the buttons go and the card says who and when; after a Not now they come back when the hold runs out. The first press asks for a name, which this browser keeps. From another device an answer needs the act or admin token, entered once in Set up. ρ does not count events, so none of the three moves it, and `DECISION_REQUIRED` applies to alert acts only. On a node on the old engine (`rules`), Decide says "This node sends alerts, not events." and draws one card per issue with an open alert: what was seen, what the node suggests (the rule's own recommendation, or a line saying it carries none), **Decide about this**, which records `stage: decided` and moves nothing, and **I did this**, which records `stage: acted`. With `DECISION_REQUIRED=1` the node refuses an act with 409 unless a decision was recorded against the same alert first, and the page prints the node's sentence. When nothing is open, Decide says so in words. "Whose word, over how much ground" covers with H3 cells the footprints this node already declares, six with every pack on, from `COAST_MAX_KM` for the sea to the three decimals `/health` rounds a position to. Each produces one number, and its card says how many cells of the rung you are on that one number has to cover. The other four are the stations pack's radius (`BAD_RADIUS_KM` in Bali), `EARTH_RADIUS_M` and `PLACE_RADIUS_M` (each a `footprint:` in its pack's `pack.yaml`, and counted only while that pack is on), and `LOCAL_RADIUS_M`. The node sends the coverings in `GET /issues` as `geometry.claims`, widest first. ### Act "What was asked, and what was answered" is one ring for each event of the last seven days, closed if somebody answered and hollow if not, and a row for each: the issue and kind, when it began and cleared, the rooms, the action the node sent and the answer. "Cleared 40 min after" appears only on a Done that a clear followed. Below sit the nearest place that could make something, where the `make` pack is on, and the filter life of a purifier the household owns. "What was decided, and by whom" is the ledger, newest first: who, which button or stage, how long ago, and `decided first` on an act that had a decision before it. The note is shown only to a reader with a token, because `GET /actions` is on no sharing allowlist. ### Measure Measure counts the hours over the line, today and this week. "Whether it worked" draws ρ as a row of rings with the median minutes from alert to answer; it counts alerts, because ρ does not count events. Beside it the funnel, `asked`, `acknowledged`, `acted`, `measured`, where `measured` is derived: an act followed by 48 hours of silence from the same rule on the same sensor. The care label under it is the five refusals as signs. "Which of these worked" reports per rule how many acts there were and how many were followed by the condition stopping; a rule that declares `watch: {metric, over}` also gets a typical recovery time. It is evidence that the condition ended, never that the act ended it; see [ρ](rho.md). "Every figure on this page, and where it came from" is the node's provenance for each figure, with a link to the same day as open data, `GET /export?day=<the day>`, and the days before it at `GET /exports`.

title: The dashboard · Where this leads
text: The page answers when somebody is looking at it. [The report](report.md) is the same node speaking at the hours the household chose, and [Alerts](alerts.md) and [Channels](channels.md) are how an alert reaches a person who is not looking. What Measure counts is [ρ](rho.md). A screen on the wall is [Wall mode](wall.md), and how the page is drawn is [Design](design.md).

title: Design
text: The design language every PLANETAI surface is drawn in: the colours and the one thing each means, the type, the four card kinds, the signs and the motion. [The dashboard](dashboard.md), [the Wall](wall.md) and the phone page all follow it, so a number reads the same, drawn the same way, on every node. Every value comes from one table, `planetai-design/references/planetai-layer.md`, which the design repository turns into `app/static/planetai-theme.css`. The node carries a pinned copy of that file, `signs.svg` and `kilometre-cells.json`, and does not edit them: `tools/check_theme.py`, in `make lint`, holds each to the sha256 in `data/frozen_layer.txt`. To change a value, change the table and regenerate. `tokens.css` is the Fab City foundation the layer imports; the layer's own tokens are unprefixed and redefine no `--fc-` token.

title: Design · The plate
text: `--ground` is `#F9F5F2` on paper and `#171717` in the dark register, and `--ink` is the reverse. Everything drawn is ink on ground: buildings, roads, labels, provenance. The register is one attribute on `<html>`, `data-theme="dark"`, so a page carries both. The Paper / Dark switch is in the bar of the doors and the classic dashboard and in the phone page's foot; the choice is kept per browser, and the doors and the phone follow the system's setting until one is chosen. The Wall is always dark. Corners are square. There are no gauges, no dials with needles and no rounded verdict: a reading is a number with its comparison beside it.

title: Design · Colour
text: Four colours, one meaning each. A surface that uses one of them for anything else is wrong. | token | paper | dark | what it means | |---|---|---|---| | `--cells` | `#20388D` | `#7FA5E8` | an H3 cell, and where a reading is from. On the doors it is also the keyboard focus | | `--rings` | `#00A057` | `#00A057` | a loop closed: somebody was asked and somebody answered | | `--signal-worse` | `#E62038` | `#E62038` | a reading got worse or crossed the line its issue declares. A mark, never small type | | `--satellite-only` | `#DB7200` | `#FF931E` | what only the satellite knows | `--loop-closed` and `--rho-closed` are both `var(--rings)`, so a closed ring is the same green in the ρ row as anywhere else. Everything else is ink. Contrast decides which register a colour may appear in, and the generator computes it. `#7FA5E8` is 2.29:1 on paper, so it appears only in the dark block. `#20388D` is 1.72:1 on ink, so it never appears there. `#DB7200` is the paper orange at 3.02:1; `#FF931E` is 2.05:1 on paper and 8.06:1 on ink. Neither crosses into the other's block. ### State and provenance are not colours State is carried by weight, fill and dash, never by hue. On a map a live node is a 2.5 stroke, a registered one 1.5 dashed `5 4`, a pilot 1 at 45% opacity. On a page the same rule is type weight: a state word is set at 500 in the muted ink, and `act` alone at 700 in full ink. Nothing in a table is tinted. The ladder follows it: rungs whose cell may leave the machine are dotted, rungs that stay are plain, rungs finer than the node says where it is are struck through, so a reader who cannot tell blue from grey still sees three zones. Provenance is ink only and square (`--prov` is `var(--ink)`): the word's sign, then the word. The words are `live`, `partial`, `model`, `cached` and `example`, and the classic dashboard also prints `stale` when the node stops answering; see [Concepts](concepts.md#provenance-words-on-the-page).

title: Design · Type
text: | role | face | where | |---|---|---| | display | Funnel Sans | headings, stage names, a section's title | | body | Figtree | the node's own sentences: the lead, the reason, a caption | | mono | JetBrains Mono (`--mono`) | every number, unit, timestamp, cell id and chip label | All three are self-hosted and served by the node, because its page may be read on a network with no route out. `--num-face` is the large numeral on the lead and the Wall. It defaults to `var(--mono)`; whether it should be Funnel Sans is open item O13. The node's own words are never uppercased, because `µ` uppercases to `M` and `µg/m³` becomes `MG/M³`, a thousandfold error. Anything the node wrote is drawn inside `.said`, which turns uppercase off. On the classic dashboard `tools/check_ui.py` fails a new uppercase rule, and a `µ` written outside `.said`. The Wall has its own floor, `--wf`: 28 px at 1920×1080, scaled with the screen, and nothing on the Wall is smaller.

title: Design · Four card kinds and no fifth
text: Everything on a node's page is one of four things, and each part of the doors says which in `data-kind`. | kind | what it is for | |---|---| | **readout** | one figure, with its comparison beside it | | **stack** | the same quantity at several distances, on one scale | | **series** | a quantity over time | | **row** | a list of like things, counted in signs | A drawing sits inside a card, it is not a fifth kind. A gap in a series is a gap in the line, never a ramp across a line nobody measured. Every numeral carries its comparison (`data-num` names it, `data-cmp` says against what), and a numeral with nothing to compare it to says so in words. The figures are drawn with Observable Plot 0.6.17 and d3 7.9.0, served by the node (ISC, licences in `app/static/licences/`) and pinned in `data/vendor.sha256`. Plot draws the marks and the rules above decide them: ink for readings, red for the line and the hours over it, green only for an answer that closed a loop, blue only for a cell or focus.

title: Design · Signs
text: `app/static/signs.svg` carries 25 counting signs and 4 pictograms, two families with two rules. A **counting sign** is 24×24, fill only, `currentColor`. It is repeated to show quantity (more signs, never a bigger sign), so it has to read at `--sign-floor`, 12 px, and tile in a row of ten without fusing. At that size the one reliable difference is solid mass against hollow ring. A **pictogram** (`pix-air`, `pix-heat`, `pix-land`, `pix-coast`) is 15×11, drawn once at hero size beside the issue it names, and never repeated. An issue with no pictogram has none. Distinctness is measured: every pair is rasterised at 12 px and compared cell for cell, and over 90% identical fails unless the layer records it as an open item. Two pairs are recorded and wait for a redraw: O7 (`prov-cached` against `prov-example`, 93.7%) and O12 (`cell` against `prov-example`, 93.9%).

title: Design · Motion
text: Every motion is named after the datum that drives it. A motion with no datum behind it is deleted: nothing counts up, and nothing eases between two readings. | token | datum | value | |---|---|---| | `--motion-reading-fade` | a reading lands | `120ms` | | `--motion-reading-pulse` | a reading lands | `3s` | | `--motion-ring-closed` | a person answered | `320ms` | | `--motion-meter-fill` | a stack arrives | `40ms` per bracket cell | | `--motion-day-curve-step` | the day curve steps | `3600s`, once an hour | | `--motion-satellite-year` | the year changes | `4s` per frame, no tween | | `--motion-land-change-yoy` | the datum changes once a year | `0s`, so it does not animate | | `--motion-mark-float` | learn mode is on | `3.2s`, 4 px | | `--motion-asking` | the node has not answered yet | `until-data` | | `--motion-asking-hold` | the loading state is also a reading | `3s`, the shortest time it is held | The doors add one token the layer does not carry yet, `--motion-replay-loop: 30s`, defined in `doors.html`: a replayed window of 6 or 24 hours takes 30 s, on Node's flow and on the Wall's walk. Only transform and opacity move. One `requestAnimationFrame` loop drives the whole page; surfaces subscribe to it, and it stops when the tab is hidden or nobody is subscribed. Time and scale move in steps: there is no place between resolution 7 and 8, so nothing morphs. `--motion-asking` is a word, not a duration: the loading state lasts as long as the node takes to answer. `--motion-asking-hold` puts a floor under it so the list of what the page asked can be read. Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` one block sets every timed token to `0s`, `--motion-asking-hold` included, and every surface has to read frozen. The doors' clock never starts. `--motion-asking` is not restated there, so the loading state still happens and stops moving. No page uses SVG `<animate>`, because reduced motion reaches CSS animation and not SMIL.

title: Design · Refusals that hold at every stage
text: - No raw readings leave the instance that recorded them. - No cell is upgraded from `mock` or `partial` to `live` by aggregation. - No agent dispatches without a human row in `actions`. - No layer requires a cloud provider to function. - No scale is skipped: a city aggregator is built from nodes, not declared from above. On the doors these close the Node door, "What this node will not do, at any stage", each in plain words beside a link to where it can be checked. On the classic dashboard they are the care label, drawn as signs in Measure beside the funnel. The longer form is [Architecture](architecture.md); what leaves the machine, and how coarse, is [Sharing and security](sharing.md).

title: Design · What is unsettled
text: The theme carries 12 open items on 11 tokens, each written into the CSS as an `OPEN:` comment at the token it affects: `--land-opacity`, `--cells`, `--prov`, `--cell-water-opacity`, `--state-pilot-opacity`, `--wall-line-opacity`, `--sign-floor` (two items), `--num-face`, `--motion-reading-pulse`, `--motion-day-curve-step` and `--motion-ring-closed`. They are values set by eye, on one screen or in one room, and not measured since. The list lives in `planetai-design/references/planetai-layer.md`.

title: Design · Where this leads
text: [The dashboard](dashboard.md) is where these rules are read by a person at the page, and [Wall mode](wall.md) is the dark register for a screen read from three metres.

title: Developing and contributing
text: This page is for the person who changes the node itself: a new adapter, a rule, a pack, a fix. A household updates by running `planetai update` and cannot review what arrives, so every change here passes the gates, a review and CI before it merges, and a release is signed before any node gets it. The repository is [`fabcity/planetai-node`](https://github.com/fabcity/planetai-node). The code is Apache-2.0 today and moves to AGPL-3.0-or-later once every contributor has consented ([the decision](../../docs/decisions/2026-09-25-licence.md)); the documentation is CC BY 4.0. By opening a pull request you agree to those terms.

title: Developing and contributing · Ways to help
text: Run a node and report. The most useful contribution is [Install](install.md) failing on your machine. Open an issue with the "Node problem" template, which asks for the output of `make health; docker compose ps; docker compose logs app | tail -50`. Never paste `.env`. Add a sensor or a source. An adapter is one function returning `(sensors, readings)`, and the contract is on [Sensors](sensors.md). Test it against a saved payload from the real device before you open a pull request, and set `local` and `indoor` to what is true, because every rule depends on them. Write a rule, a cell or a pack: [Packs](packs.md). A pack for one place is a wild pack in its own repository, listed at [fabcity/planetai-wild-packs](https://github.com/fabcity/planetai-wild-packs), and does not come here as a pull request. The 25 packs in `packs/` are core, and a wild pack joins them by promotion. Start from a core pack of the same kind, say in the README where the thresholds come from and which place you wrote for, and make the rule end in something a person does.

title: Developing and contributing · What will not be merged
text: Anything that makes a node depend on a cloud service to function: reference data from public APIs is fine, a control plane is not. A third container without a trigger written in [`SPEC.md`](spec.md) §6. Raw readings leaving the node: hourly means, cells and model updates may go, raw never. Rules that fire on indoor sensors as if they were ambient, which is what `NOT s.indoor` in a rule is there to prevent.

title: Developing and contributing · Run a node from your clone
text: Develop on a machine with git, and keep the node you test on separate from the one a household relies on. The CLI runs on Apple's Python 3.9 with the standard library only, and nothing runs pip on a node's host; what the app needs is in its image. ```bash git clone https://github.com/fabcity/planetai-node && cd planetai-node ./install.sh --name dev --lat -8.8 --lon 115.1 # your own coordinates; no sensor needed make health ``` The installer runs in the checkout and builds the app image from `app/`. With no sensor the node still fills itself with 92 days of free global data for its coordinates, so there is something to read as soon as `make health` answers. After you change the code, rebuild and restart the app with `docker compose up -d --build app`, and watch it with `make logs`.

title: Developing and contributing · Before you commit
text: ```bash cp tools/hooks/pre-commit .git/hooks/ # once make lint make test git commit -s ``` The hook refuses a commit that stages `.env`, anything under `.git/`, `backups/` or a `*.before-update` file, a diff that carries a Telegram bot URL, a `…TOKEN=` or `…API_KEY=` value or a real database password, and `.DS_Store`, `__pycache__` or `.pyc` files. Then it runs `make lint` and `make test`. `make lint` runs every gate this repository has: shell syntax, SQL, the CLI's Python 3.9 compatibility, the docs against the code, the registry, the dashboard, the wire formats, the theme, the vendored libraries, the rules, and an import of the app. [docs/DEVELOPING.md](../../docs/DEVELOPING.md) says what each gate exists for. Some gates need extra packages on the dev machine (`pyyaml`; `sqlglot` for the rules; `markdown` for the docs site; the app's `requirements.txt` for the import check), and a gate whose package is missing says it skipped. CI installs them all, so nothing skips there. `make test` runs `tests/all`: 91 offline suites, one line each with a count at the end. It exits non-zero when a suite fails, when a check skipped that nobody declared, or when the list and the count disagree. A new suite needs its own line in `tests/all` and the count raised, or it never runs. `-s` adds the `Signed-off-by:` line of the Developer Certificate of Origin: you are saying you wrote the change or have the right to contribute it. If an agent writes your commits, tell it to use `-s` too. Two habits help. Test the file itself, never a copy of the code typed into the test, because the copy hides the bug. And before you trust a new gate, break something on purpose and watch it fail.

title: Developing and contributing · Open a pull request
text: Work on your own branch, and in a worktree of your own if you keep several. `tools/session.sh preflight` before you start tells you where `main` is, how far your branch is from `origin/main`, the open pull requests and whether CI is green on main. `tools/session.sh land` before you stop runs `make lint` and `make test` in full and stops on uncommitted or unpushed work. Give the pull request a line under `## Unreleased` in `CHANGELOG.md`, written for the person running a node: what changed for them. A pull request that changes what a node runs (`app/`, `bin/`, `packs/`, `config/`, `presets/`, `init.sql`, the installers, `docker-compose.yml`) fails CI without one; a change that truly needs none carries the label `no changelog`. Schema changes go in `init.sql` additively, so a node updates in place. A new feature, setting or command also needs a place a household would look (a Set up row, a line on the page that uses it) and a page or section here; say in the pull request where both are (AGENTS.md, "Anything new is visible"). Most changes need one maintainer's review. `init.sql`, the contracts in `SPEC.md`, `install`, `install.sh`, `update.sh` and `bin/planetai` need two, because those are what a household runs without reading. `GOVERNANCE.md` says who merges what. How a merged change is tested on a node and gathered into a release is in [docs/WORKFLOW.md](../../docs/WORKFLOW.md).

title: Developing and contributing · What CI checks
text: | workflow | when | what it runs | |---|---|---| | `lint` | every push and pull request | `make lint` and `make test` on Ubuntu with Python 3.12, and the visual gate on macOS (a pull request from a fork gets no secrets, so the visual gate does not run there) | | `install smoke` | every push and pull request | the install a stranger runs, from a tarball built from this commit: no terminal, no prompt, no `sudo` and no `brew`, and `make health` answers. Then a second run, a removal and a fresh install, on Ubuntu 22.04, Linux Mint, Arch and Debian on arm64 | | `changelog` | every pull request | a change to what a node runs carries a line under `## Unreleased`, or the `no changelog` label | | `sweep` | once a day | `tools/sweep.py`, which files what it finds (a release with no CHANGELOG heading, a site behind main) into one pinned issue |

title: Developing and contributing · Looking at the page
text: `python3 tools/shots.py` renders every fixture in Now, on the Wall and in Network at four widths into `docs/design/shots/`, with every request answered from disk. It fails on a page error, a component that drew its guard box, a page that scrolls sideways or a request the fixture should not have made. It needs Chromium from a sibling `planetai-design` checkout (`PLANETAI_DESIGN_REPO`) and is not a gate. The dashboard's frozen visual language and the checks against it are in `docs/design/LANGUAGE_GAP.md`.

title: Developing and contributing · This documentation
text: The pages under `docs/site/`, and the pages of `docs/` and the root that the sidebar lists, are rendered by `tools/build_docs.py` into `planetai.fab.city/docs`: ```bash pip install markdown # on the dev machine only python3 tools/build_docs.py --check # what make lint runs: the map, every link, every anchor make docs # build_learn.py, then build_docs.py --out ../planetai/docs python3 tools/build_docs.py --single /tmp/docs.html # everything on one page, for review ``` `docs/site/STYLE.md` is how the pages are written. `make lint` checks what can be checked mechanically: the commands, settings, paths and endpoints a page names exist, every command, MCP tool, route, setting and `pack.yaml` field the code has is on its page (`check_docs.py`), every link and anchor lands (`build_docs.py --check`), and the learn spans are still there. Whether a sentence is still true is not mechanical. Every page carries `<!-- checked: vX -->`, the release it was last read against, and lint holds that to the newest release in `CHANGELOG.md`, so a release cannot pass lint until every page has been read for it (`skills/release-docs/SKILL.md`). A change that alters what a page describes changes the page in the same commit. The dashboard's learn mode quotes short spans of some pages, through `app/static/learn.json`. If you move one on purpose, update `MARKS` in `tools/build_learn.py` in the same change and run `make learn`; `make lint` fails until the marks and the pages agree.

title: Developing and contributing · Releases
text: A merge is not a release: a node gets a change only in a signed tarball. Maintainers cut releases with `tools/release.sh <version>` and the Foundation's signing key (`PLANETAI_SIGNING_KEY`), after the CHANGELOG section is written, pushed and green in CI. It runs `make lint` and `make test`, tags, pushes, and then `tools/ship.sh` builds the tarball, signs it with `ssh-keygen -Y sign -n planetai-node`, verifies it against `tools/allowed_signers`, rebuilds the docs site from the same commit and publishes both. `make released` afterwards says whether the site serves what is on `main`. The steps in order are in [docs/WORKFLOW.md](../../docs/WORKFLOW.md), the key and its rotation in [docs/SIGNING.md](../../docs/SIGNING.md), and what a node checks before it installs an update on [Sharing and security](sharing.md#signed-updates).

title: Developing and contributing · Layout of the repository
text: ``` app/ main.py (api, loops) · db.py (the pool, q()) · auth.py (tokens, share levels) · channels.py (notify) basemap.py · geo.py · machine.py · household.py · presence.py (route groups moved out of main.py) sources.py (adapters) · index.py (cells, ρ) · packs.py · settings.py registry.py (the source registry) · report.py · agent.py (MCP) · tool_classes.py · agent_loop.py (the bot) events.py · events_pg.py · events_wire.py · actions.py (the alert-event engine, its store, its /issues block and the action it chooses) requires.py (which node a pack needs) · fundamentals.py (the sources every node needs) · learn.py (what it learns) ask.py (the dashboard's ask pane) · bootstrap.py · ground.py · issues/ · static/ (the dashboard) bin/planetai the operator CLI packs/ the twenty-five core packs, some with their own routes.py; see Packs config/ rules.yml (two domain-blind rules, trust's three) · channels.yml · mosquitto · grafana data/ sources/ (the pinned registry) · strings/ · env_defaults.yml · frozen_layer.txt · platform_floors.yml · mac_ceilings.yml skills/ setup-node · troubleshoot-node · connect-agent · publish-to-index · preflight · land · write-a-pack · release-docs tools/ the gates, hooks, bundle, ship and release scripts, session.sh, sweep.py, sync_registry.sh, build_docs.py tests/ offline suites docs/ the pages; docs/site/ the ones written for this site; design/ the visual language and its reviews presets/ bali · barcelona · boston · santiago · delhi · menorca ``` A tarball node carries none of `tests/`, `.github/`, `docs/design/`, the `tools/check_*` gates, or the bundle and release scripts; `tools/bundle.sh` leaves them out.

title: Developing and contributing · Where this leads
text: The parts a contributor most often adds are [a sensor](sensors.md) and [a pack](packs.md). What a change may send off the machine is on [Sharing and security](sharing.md).

title: Federation and the Index
text: This is the part that joins the network. With a parent set, a house becomes one cell in a district's picture without its readings leaving the house: every hour it sends up hourly means and the timestamps of its alerts, and nothing else. A node at a house and an aggregator for a district run the same code with different sources, different rules and a different parent, which is how the architecture can say "a city aggregator is built from nodes, not declared from above" ([Architecture](architecture.md), §7). A child pushes two things to its parent, `POST /aggregates` and `POST /events`, and every node answers `GET /cells`. What the Index cells are, and the words `live` and `partial`, are on [Concepts](concepts.md).

title: Federation and the Index · Parent and child
text: ![Home nodes push to a district parent; only a pilot's city node writes to the Index](img/federation.svg "Every hour a child sends hourly means and alert times, and nothing else.") To make one node the child of another: 1. On the parent, set `AGGREGATE_TOKEN`: `planetai config set AGGREGATE_TOKEN <a long random string>` (`openssl rand -hex 16` makes one). Until it is set, both routes answer 403 `this node accepts no children: set AGGREGATE_TOKEN in .env and give it to them`. The token lets a child push and read nothing; a child reads its parent only as a stranger on that network would (see [Sharing](sharing.md)). 2. On the child, set `PARENT_API_URL` and `PARENT_TOKEN`: `planetai config set PARENT_API_URL http://<parent>:8080`, with the parent's tailnet hostname, then `planetai config set PARENT_TOKEN <the parent's AGGREGATE_TOKEN>`. Each answers `<KEY> is now …, on this node, within 20 s`. 3. Wait for the first pushes. The child posts to `/aggregates` two minutes after its app starts and to `/events` half a minute after that, then each every hour, with `Authorization: Bearer <PARENT_TOKEN>` and its `NODE_SCALE`. A child that was already running pushes on its next hourly turn, and `planetai restart` brings the first push to two minutes. In `planetai logs` the child says `pushed <N> hourly rows to parent`, and `pushed <N> alert events to parent` when it raised an alert in the last 36 hours. A wrong token shows as `push to parent failed:` with a 401. On the parent the child's sensors appear as `<child>/<sensor_id>` with `kind='child'`, in the parent's custody, so they count toward a `live` cell. The house's raw readings are still at home. A parent never sees a child's raw rows, its room names, its people, its sentences or its coordinates. ### POST /aggregates The last two hours of `readings_1h`, the node's hourly means, for its own sensors and its children's only (custody), leaving out every channel whose role is `private`. A peer's station and a model sampled at the node stay home: the parent would count them as its own. ```json {"schema": "aggregates-v0", "node": "bayu-ungasan", "scale": "community", "rows": [{"bucket": "2026-09-16T05:00:00+00:00", "sensor_id": "sc-19880", "metric": "pm25", "mean": 12.4, "min": 9.1, "max": 17.0, "n": 12, "indoor": false}]} ``` The parent keeps each `mean` as one reading on the child's own hour, under the sensor `<child>/<sensor_id>` with `source='child'`, `kind='child'`, `cadence='PT1H'` and `local=FALSE`. Custody is generated as `kind='child' OR (local AND kind<>'peer')`, so those rows count toward a `live` cell. The metric keeps its own name, so the parent's pack SQL matches it. `indoor` is kept on the parent's sensor row, so an indoor kit stays out of outdoor means there too. `min`, `max` and `n` travel but the parent does not store them. A child's sensors have no coordinates at the parent. The push sends the hour in progress and, an hour later, the same hour complete; the parent keeps the later mean. ### POST /events The last 36 hours of alerts, as timestamps only: ```json {"schema": "events-v0", "node": "bayu-ungasan", "scale": "community", "rows": [{"alert_id": "812", "rule": "air-quality/indoor_pm25_high", "level": "act", "kind": "air-quality", "raised_at": "…", "responded_at": "…", "acted_at": "…", "measured_at": null}]} ``` `kind` is the pack prefix of the rule id, so the pack is the domain tag. `responded_at` and `acted_at` are the first `acknowledged` and `acted` rows in the child's ledger. `measured_at` is the first posted `measured` row, and it is null in practice, because the node derives `measured` from a rule's silence after an act and `POST /actions` takes only `acknowledged`, `acted` and `decided` for an alert. The push is read from `alerts`, so a `decided` row is not sent, and neither is an answer to an alert event. The window is 36 hours because an alert raised yesterday can be answered today; the parent upserts on `(child, alert_id)`, so the row is updated when its timestamps change. A row without `alert_id` or `raised_at` is skipped. There is no text, actor, sensor, note or ratio in it. The parent computes [ρ](rho.md) itself, over its own act-level alerts and its children's pooled together, because a mean of ten ratios is not the ratio of the pooled counts. The Measure funnel under `/rho` stays the node's own: children push no stages, so a pooled funnel would have a hole where each child's `measured` should be. ### Versions on the wire Both bodies carry a `schema` key, and a receiver never refuses on it. A body with no `schema` is read as `-v0`; one with a value the node does not know is read for the fields it recognises, and the rest are dropped. Either case is logged once per value. So a parent one release behind keeps accepting a child one release ahead.

title: Federation and the Index · Cells: `fci-cells-v0`
text: Every node exposes `GET /cells`: the Fab City Index cells it can compute from what it holds, one row per cell, in the shape of an `FCI Observations` row, with counts from [the source registry](sources.md): ```json {"city": "bali", "cell": "Environmental|Community", "value": 11.8, "unit": "µg/m³ PM2.5 (24h mean, sensors in this node's custody)", "source": "planetai-node · pack:air-quality", "observed_at": "2026-09-16T06:00:00+00:00", "state": "live", "notes": "this node's own sensors and its children's hourly means; indoor and outdoor kept separate by the rules · <have>/12 hourly buckets", "registered": 2, "adapter": true, "reviewed": 2, "candidate": 1, "capable": 2} ``` `reviewed`, `candidate` and `capable` are counted from each registry entry's `feeds_cells`. `registered` carries the `reviewed` count, and `adapter` is true when `capable` is above 0. [The source registry](sources.md) says how an entry gets each label. `state` is provenance and travels end to end, and it is never upgraded on the way ([Architecture](architecture.md), §7). At a parent, `live` needs in-custody measurement at the parent's own rung from at least two sensors, and from at least two children where there are children; otherwise the core demotes the claim to `partial`. One child reporting is one household's kitchen. A cell with no source is absent, not zero. Aggregation of cells stops at Region ([Architecture](architecture.md)). Bioregion and Planet publish context downward as boundary conditions and are never rolled up.

title: Federation and the Index · Publishing to the Index
text: One node per pilot writes to the Index, and a home node never does. A pilot city has one City-tier node, run by the partner accountable for that city's numbers, and it is the only node in that city whose cells reach the Index's spine. Every other node, at a home, a lab, a classroom or a community centre, computes its own cells, shows them on its own dashboard, and passes them no further. That keeps readings where they were made and puts one identified operator per city behind what the Index publishes. The writer, `cells-ingest`, lives with the Index's own code, outside this repository. `docs/SPEC_custody.md` and `skills/publish-to-index` describe it: it refuses to run without `FCI_PUBLISHER=1` and a per-pilot write token issued by hand. Nothing in the node publishes, and `SHARE_LEVEL` has nothing to do with it; sharing is who on your own network may read the node, and publishing is a separate act, gated by the tier and a token issued to a person. To publish: 1. Confirm the node is the pilot's City-tier node. 2. Run `planetai cells --json` and read every row's `state`. 3. If a row is wrong, fix the source or the pack, never the label. 4. Write to **info@fab.city** with the node's name, the city and that output. The Index's own methodology, sources and cells are at [index.fab.city](https://index.fab.city). A source a pack reads has to be an entry in [`awesome-fabcity-data`](https://github.com/fabcity/awesome-fabcity-data) first; the copy every node carries is described on [the source registry](sources.md).

title: Federation and the Index · The node directory
text: `registry.json` in the repository is the node directory: `name, scale, operator, place, cell, lat, lon, sources, parent, since, contact`, where `cell` is the node's resolution-8 H3 cell and `lat`/`lon` are that cell's centre, never the house. Adding a node is a pull request, and approval is a merge. It lists two nodes, `bayu-ungasan` (node #1, in Ungasan) and `larsbcn` in Barcelona. Every node reads the file from the repository's `main` once an hour and serves it at `GET /nodes`, with only the name, place, scale, operator, `since` and cell, and each point rounded to one decimal; `contact`, `sources` and `parent` stay in the file. The Node door and the phone's walk draw the nodes from it. `UPDATE_CHECK=off` reads nothing. A registry service with a signed handshake comes back when pull requests stop scaling, roughly thirty nodes or a second operator organisation, with its trigger written in [`SPEC.md`](spec.md) §6. > **Note.** This file is not the source registry. `data/sources/` is the network's list of what can be > measured; `registry.json` is the list of nodes.

title: Federation and the Index · Peers and places
text: An observatory the node does not run, such as Bali Air Dispatch or a city's own portal, is a source. Its readings enter through an adapter or a pack, flagged `local=FALSE` and credited. A `kind='peer'` row, another node's numbers shown for context, reaches no cell, no custody count, no aggregate and no alert, whatever its coordinates say. Nothing writes `peer` rows yet: listening to other nodes as peers is proposed and not built. A `kind='facility'` row is the other kind of row that is not a measurement. The `make` pack writes one per fab lab within reach: a place with a name and a point, no readings, never in custody, a cell or an alert. It is how the node can say where somebody could go and make or fix something (see [Packs that ship](packs-reference.md#make)).

title: Federation and the Index · Not built: identity and discovery
text: Two specifications describe what the network would add next. Neither is built. [`docs/SPEC_identity.md`](../SPEC_identity.md) is about identity. Today every child of a parent shares one `AGGREGATE_TOKEN`, and the child's name is `body["node"]`, a string the child declares about itself, so any child holding the district's token can push readings under a sibling's name or rewrite a sibling's ρ rows. The spec gives each node an Ed25519 key generated in the app container at first boot, makes the node id the public key, has the parent keep a `children` table filled by one enrolment command, signs the bytes on the wire, and retires the shared token after one release. The two body shapes would not change. [`docs/SPEC_discovery.md`](../SPEC_discovery.md) is about discovery. A node that chooses to be discoverable would answer what `GET /presence` already returns: its name, a coarse H3 cell (resolution 3, about sixty kilometres across), its version and its kind. On the tailnet the host would read the peer list and the node would ask each peer's `/presence` once an hour; on radio, the Reticulum bridge already announces the same body. Being discoverable gives nobody access: `SHARE_LEVEL` still decides who may read what, and nothing discovered enters `sensors`, `cells` or any count.

title: Federation and the Index · The commons
text: The daily export (`GET /export?day=`, written nightly to `exports/<node>/`, `schema: export-v0`) is what a parent, the Index, a researcher or the commons should receive: hourly mean, min, max and count per sensor and metric, the cells, the first line of each alert, ρ, what the household offers (`offers`, while the things pack is on), and the centre of the node's resolution-8 cell in place of its coordinates. Your own sensors are named by role (`indoor-1`, `outdoor-2`) instead of by id. There are no raw rows, no tokens and no chat ids, and CC BY 4.0 is stated in the file as `licence`. Each source's own attribution is in its sensor's `meta` on `/sensors`, not in the export. `planetai ipfs` pins the export on IPFS; the database and its dumps never go there.

title: Federation and the Index · The refusals
text: No raw readings leave the instance that recorded them. No cell is upgraded from `mock` or `partial` to `live` by aggregation. No agent dispatches without a human row in `actions`. No layer requires a cloud provider to function. No scale is skipped: a city aggregator is built from nodes, not declared from above. Peers never roll up and never drive an alert or a report line. Exact place never leaves; a coarse cell may, and says how coarse. Exactly one node per pilot writes to the spine.

title: Federation and the Index · Where the network is
text: We run node #1, `bayu-ungasan`, in Kuta Selatan, Bali, at community scale, with Smart Citizen kits and the Bali Air Dispatch ring. Node #2 runs in Menorca. Stage 1 of the architecture, a district aggregator receiving hourly means from five nodes over the tailnet, begins when five nodes have been alive thirty days with at least one `acted` row each.

title: Federation and the Index · Where this leads
text: A node that shares a summary upward can also be asked questions by an agent, under the same rule that nothing dispatches without a person: [Agents](agents.md), then the [MCP tools](mcp.md) and the [bot](bot.md).

title: First ten minutes
text: The install ends with a node that reads your place and has nobody to tell. In the next ten minutes you add the rest of the loop: a channel to your phone, one alert that goes all the way through, a person's answer recorded against it, and the first value of [ρ](rho.md), the share of act-level alerts somebody answered. After that the node can measure whether anybody acted on what it said, which only this layer can do.

title: First ten minutes · 1. See that it is reading
text: ```bash planetai status ``` ``` node <name> <version> schema <schema> up <h>h <m>m polls <n> readings <n> last poll <time of the last poll> errors none sensors none of yours yet (models only) reference <n>: <the first four public stations and models it reads> alerts 0 so far rho not yet measured (0/0 act-level alerts answered, 30d) ``` The angle brackets are this node's own figures. `polls` goes up by one every `POLL_SECONDS` (300), and `errors none` means every source answered. With a Smart Citizen kit configured, `sensors` names it. **Now there is:** sense. The poll loop is running and the models for your coordinates are in the database.

title: First ten minutes · 2. Connect Telegram
text: ```bash planetai telegram ``` Make a bot with **@BotFather** (`/newbot`) and paste its token when asked. Then open a chat with your bot and send it any message, because a bot cannot start a conversation; the command waits up to two minutes for it. When it worked: ``` ● token works. Your bot is @<yourbot> ● found your chat: <chat id> ● sent you a hello ● the node is restarting with Telegram on. Try: planetai test-alert ``` Your phone shows "<name> is connected. Alerts will arrive here." The command writes `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` and `TELEGRAM_CHAT_IDS` to `.env` and to the running node. For more people, comma-separate their chat ids in `TELEGRAM_CHAT_IDS`. Once the bot answers messages ([step 6](#6-talk-to-it)), a chat that is not in that list is told once that the node answers its household only, with its own chat id to add. **Now there is:** a channel. An alert has somewhere to go that a person will see.

title: First ten minutes · 3. Prove the whole path
text: ```bash planetai test-alert ``` ``` A rule that always fires has been added. The node checks rules every minute. Waiting...... ● it fired. Alert #12 is in the log and on your phone. Now close the loop, which is the part the Index measures: planetai act 12 ``` The command writes a temporary pack with one act-level rule that always fires, waits up to ninety seconds for it, and removes the pack as soon as its alert appears, so the phone gets one test message. The message says: "Test alert from your node. If you can read this, the whole path works: rule to message to you. Record it with `planetai act <id>`." A quiet node is not a working node until this has happened once. The API has its own test alert too, `POST /test-alert`. **Now there is:** act. A rule fired, the alert is in `alerts`, and it went out on every channel the node has.

title: First ten minutes · 4. Close the loop
