text: Reads this node's own AirGradient ONE and Open Air monitors on the household's WiFi, each host in `AIRGRADIENT_HOSTS` at `http://<host>/measures/current`, never through AirGradient's cloud. PM2.5 is the EPA 2021 correction of the raw Plantower value, which is kept beside it as `pm25_raw`. CO2, temperature, humidity, PM1, PM10 and the TVOC and NOx indexes are stored as the monitor gives them. | | | |---|---| | Kind | code, on whenever a host is listed (`switch: [AIRGRADIENT_HOSTS]`) | | Domain | `air` | | Requires node | `>=0.83.0` | | Sources | `environmental/community/airgradient` | | Needs | the monitors' own addresses on this node's network | | Rules and cells | none: `air-quality` and `heat` decide what the readings mean | The sensor ids are `ag-<serial>` and the source is `airgradient`. The monitors take the node's own coordinates, and `SENSOR_INDOOR=1` marks them as indoors. This was a core adapter until v0.16 dropped it from the poll by accident, while the setting and the installer's `--airgradient` stayed; it reads again as a pack from 22 October 2026. On `planetai update`, a node that lists its packs in `PACKS_ENABLED` and has `AIRGRADIENT_HOSTS` set gets `airgradient` added to the list.

title: Packs that ship · purpleair
text: Reads this node's own PurpleAir sensors on the household's WiFi, each host in `PURPLEAIR_HOSTS` at `http://<ip>/json?live=true`; use the IP, the `.local` name is unreliable. PM2.5 is the EPA 2021 correction of the mean of the two laser channels, with the raw mean kept as `pm25_raw`, and a gap between the channels larger than 5 µg/m³ and 70% of the reading is stored as `channel_disagreement`, because one laser is failing. Temperature is converted from °F, not corrected, and pressure from hPa to kPa. | | | |---|---| | Kind | code, on whenever a host is listed (`switch: [PURPLEAIR_HOSTS]`) | | Domain | `air` | | Requires node | `>=0.83.0` | | Needs | the sensors' own addresses on this node's network | | Rules and cells | none: `air-quality` and `heat` decide what the readings mean | The sensor ids are `pa-<sensor id>` and the source is `purpleair`. A sensor that reports its own coordinates keeps them; otherwise it takes the node's. Like `airgradient`, it was a core adapter that v0.16 dropped from the poll, and it reads again as a pack from 22 October 2026, added to a listed `PACKS_ENABLED` on update.

title: Packs that ship · home-assistant
text: Publishes this house's own sensors to Home Assistant as entities, one device per physical sensor, and the node's latest alert as a text sensor, over MQTT discovery, retained. The node publishes and Home Assistant automates; it never addresses a device. Setting it up is on [Channels](channels.md#home-assistant). | | | |---|---| | Kind | code, run by its own switch (`switch: HA_DISCOVERY`); `hooks.py`, no `adapter.py` | | Domain | none: it carries what the node stores and sends | | Requires node | `>=0.83.0` | | Needs | the MQTT broker (`MQTT_HOST`), which `planetai homeassistant` sets up | | Rules and cells | none | It hears the node through two hooks: `on_readings` after every batch the node stores, and `on_alert` with every alert it records. `HA_DISCOVERY` is still declared by the core, so Set up keeps marking it as a setting that changes what leaves the machine; a pack cannot declare that of a key yet. It was core code until 22 October 2026. On `planetai update`, a node that lists its packs in `PACKS_ENABLED` and has `HA_DISCOVERY=1` gets `home-assistant` added to the list, so it keeps publishing.

title: Packs that ship · nearby
text: This pack reads the ring, other people's air sensors around the node as `bali-air-dispatch` stores them. One kit cannot tell a fire in the lane from a haze over the whole island, and the ring can. It says when the bad air is only here, when it is everywhere, and in the report when there is no ring worth the name. | | | |---|---| | Kind | code: its rules are data, and it ships scripts | | Domain | `air` | | Requires node | `>=0.40.0` | | Metrics | `pm25`, `pm25_raw`, `pm10`, `pm1`, `temp`, `humidity` | | Scales | community | | Sources | `environmental/community/bali-air-dispatch` | | Needs | the `bali-air-dispatch` pack on; at least two public outdoor stations within `BAD_RADIUS_KM`; for `only_here`, a local outdoor sensor | | Cells | none: `live` means measured here, and `air-quality` already has `Environmental\|City` as `partial` over these same stations | | Attribution | Bali Air Dispatch, baliairdispatch.com, and the network named in each row's `source` | The ring is every sensor with `sensors.source='baliairdispatch'` that is not local, is outdoor and has reported in the last 120 minutes. ### Rules | rule | level | cooldown | fires when | |---|---|---|---| | `only_here` | act | 2880 | the ring has at least 2 stations and a local outdoor sensor's 1-hour mean is at least 10 over the ring's 75th percentile and more than 1.6 times the ring's median | | `everywhere` | info | 2880 | the ring has at least 2 stations and its median is over 35.5 | | `alone` | (report) | | the ring has fewer than 2 stations or the nearest is more than 10 km away; puts `stations` and `nearest_km` in the report | `only_here` asks the node to clear the top of the ring by 10 µg/m³. Node #1's neighbours in clean air sit 4 to 15 km apart and differ by about 9 µg/m³, so a rule that waited for the ring to agree with itself would never fire; this way a wide ring asks for a bigger excursion and a tight one fires sooner. 35.5 is the EPA line `air-quality` uses. ### Scripts - `planetai run nearby stations`: every station in the archive, its distance, and `included` or `excluded: <reason>`, from the same function the adapter uses. - `planetai run nearby status`: the ring now, who is reporting, how far, how long ago. - `planetai run nearby verify`: every exclusion fires, nothing external is stored as `local`, the ring recomputes. Exit 1 on failure. - `planetai run nearby backfill [days]`: each station's hourly PM2.5 history. Asked for, never scheduled. ### Settings The pack declares no `env:` of its own. The ring's settings are `bali-air-dispatch`'s (`BAD_*`, above), and its scripts read them too. One more is read by `backfill`: | setting | default | meaning | |---|---|---| | `BAD_BACKFILL_DAYS` | `0` | history to pull on `backfill` when no number is given | ### What it does not know The pack has no adapter and no `channels.yml`: the fetch and the channels are `bali-air-dispatch`'s, and a second fetch would put every station in the node twice. Outside Bali the same three rules would need an OpenAQ v3 backend behind the same shape, and there is none yet.

title: Packs that ship · season
text: `nearby` asks where the bad air is right now, across space; `season` asks across time whether this week is worse than the weeks before it. It is two SQL rules and a script, with no fetch of its own, reading the ring `bali-air-dispatch` stores. Written for Bali, from the archive's daily record since January 2025. | | | |---|---| | Kind | code: its rules are data, and it ships a script | | Domain | `air` | | Requires node | `>=0.40.0` | | Metrics | `pm25` | | Scales | community | | Sources | `environmental/community/bali-air-dispatch` | | Needs | the `bali-air-dispatch` pack on and 68 days of the ring in this node's own database. `planetai run nearby backfill 90` fetches that depth once | | Cells | none, for the same reason as `nearby` | | Settings | none of its own; the `BAD_*` settings shape the ring | | Attribution | Bali Air Dispatch, baliairdispatch.com, and the network named in each row's `source` | The comparison is paired: each ring station's last 7 days against its own preceding 60, and the median of those differences. A station counts only if it holds at least 4 days in the week and 20 in the baseline. The archive grew from 2 stations with usable daily rows to 79 over its record, so an unpaired comparison would measure which networks joined and not what the air did. ### Rules | rule | level | cooldown | fires when | |---|---|---|---| | `turning` | info | 4320 | at least 3 stations pair, the median paired step is 8 µg/m³ or more, and the median of the week is 20 µg/m³ or more | | `record` | (report) | | at least one station pairs: `stations`, `week`, `usual`, `step` and `baseline_days`, whether or not the line was crossed | +8 µg/m³ is the top of an ordinary week in the record: the paired step's 90th percentile was +8.2 across Bali. The week must also reach 20 µg/m³, because a step from 6 to 14 changes nobody's afternoon, and three paired stations is the floor for saying anything. ### Scripts - `planetai run season window`: every paired station, its week, its baseline and the step. The summary line runs the pack's own `record` rule, so the audit cannot drift from the report. ### What it does not know It is not a climatology. The same weeks last year held two stations, so a year-over-year comparison does not exist yet, and the message says "its own last two months", never "normal for this time of year". A node that has held the ring for under four weeks pairs nothing, and `record` returns no row.

title: Packs that ship · insight
text: Three rules that turn the node's own history into sentences: a digest for the report, how well the node's sources agree, and the shape of the week. It is all SQL, since Postgres has `corr()` built in, and nothing leaves the machine. | | | |---|---| | Kind | data | | Domain | `cross-domain` | | Requires node | `>=0.9.0` | | Scales | community | | Needs | nothing beyond what the node holds; `rhythm` needs a local outdoor `noise` sensor | | Scripts | none | | Cells | none: how the node's sources agree is not a fact about the place | | Settings | none; to change the cadence, copy the folder and change `cooldown_minutes` | ### Rules | rule | level | cooldown | fires when | |---|---|---|---| | `digest` | (report) | | inside (`n_in`), outside (own outdoor sensors, else the 3 nearest public), modelled (CAMS), `day_mean`, `day_peak` and `trend` (rising, falling or steady: the last 3 hours against the prior 3, ±3). A row only when inside is not NULL | | `agreement` | info | 1440 | 7 days of hourly indoor, outdoor and model give at least 48 indoor and 48 outdoor hours; reports `r_in_out`, `r_out_model`, `r_in_model`, `shield`, `model_bias`, `filtered_pct` | | `rhythm` | info | 1440 | the week's worst and best outdoor hours (local time), and the loudest hour from a local outdoor `noise` sensor, in `quiet_hr` | ### What it does not know A node with no local outdoor noise sensor gets no `rhythm` alert, because the SQL joins a `loud` CTE built from those readings. The rule names no cause for the bad hours, because the one kit with a noise sensor showed the loud hours were the clean ones. The README's pooled correlations (r = 0.55 indoor to outdoor) are kept for the record; measured pairwise, one indoor kit against one outdoor kit 1.3 km apart gives r = 0.20, and the pairwise figure is the one to use.

title: Packs that ship · cold-start
text: Makes a node useful on day one with no hardware: a modelled air line, today against 40 years of climatology, and once a sensor arrives, how far it sits from the model. The README calls it a scaffold, to delete when your own sensors carry the story. | | | |---|---| | Kind | data | | Domain | `cross-domain` | | Requires node | `>=0.3.0` | | Scales | community, planet | | Sources | `environmental/planet/open-meteo`, `environmental/planet/nasa-power` | | Needs | the `BOOTSTRAP` step on first start (92 days of CAMS hourly history while `air-quality` is on, NASA POWER monthly normals), the core's `open-meteo` adapter and the CAMS model the `air-quality` pack reads. All free, key-free, global | | Scripts | none | | Settings | none | | Cells | none: nothing here measures your place | The rules read `observations`, the view where models and portals land. ### Rules | rule | level | cooldown | fires when | |---|---|---|---| | `modelled_air_today` | info | 10080 (`long_cooldown_ok`) | a `cams-point` / `pm25_model` observation exists. The daily reports carry the model reading, so this is weekly | | `hotter_than_normal` | info | 4320 | `om-point` / `temp_model` differs from `power-point` / `temp_norm` for this month by more than 3 °C | | `sensor_vs_model` | info | 10080 | the 24-hour mean of local outdoor PM2.5 differs from CAMS by more than 15 µg/m³ | ### What it does not know The README reads a big gap in `sensor_vs_model` as the local signal a global model cannot see, and not as a sensor fault. Seeing that signal is the reason to run a node at all.

title: Packs that ship · forecast
text: Official and model weather for this point over the next day, wind direction and rain, as context for reading the node's own air. It fetches and does not predict, and it never sends an alert. BMKG, Indonesia's meteorological agency, is the source that is on by default; Open-Meteo works anywhere. | | | |---|---| | Kind | code | | Domain | `weather` | | Requires node | `>=0.40.0` | | Metrics | `fc_temp`, `fc_humidity`, `fc_wind_speed`, `fc_wind_direction`, `fc_cloud`, `fc_rain`, `fc_lead_hours`, `fc_temp_gap`, `fc_wind_speed_gap` | | Scales | community | | Needs | `PACKS_ALLOW_CODE=1`; network to `api.bmkg.go.id` and `api.open-meteo.com`; correct node coordinates; for BMKG, a village code | | Cells | none: a forecast is not measured here | | Attribution | BMKG must be named inside the application and is, on the card and in the export; Open-Meteo is CC BY 4.0, free tier non-commercial | ### Rules | rule | level | cooldown | fires when | |---|---|---|---| | `ahead` | (report) | | the next 24 hours from `readings` of `kind='model'` with `source IN ('forecast-bmkg','forecast-om')`: `wind_kmh`, `wind_from_deg`, `rain_mm`, `rain_from`, `lead_hours` | No rule here may grow a level or a message, and a test holds it to that. A forecast is wrong often, and wrong about tomorrow; there is nothing a household does at 9 pm because of rain predicted for tomorrow that it would not do by looking out of the window. ### Scripts - `planetai run forecast verify`: the `adm4` code resolves to somewhere near the node (province, regency, district, village and distance printed; past 10 km the card says so), units are as documented, BMKG's `analysis_date` is under 18 hours old. Exit 1 on failure. - `planetai run forecast fetch`: fetch now instead of waiting for the poll; writes to `sensors` and `readings`. - `planetai run forecast status`: the next day's wind, rain and temperature, and when it was issued. - `planetai run forecast windfield`: refresh the wind field now. Refuses unless `FORECAST_OPENMETEO=1`. ### Settings | setting | default | meaning | |---|---|---| | `FORECAST_BMKG` | `1` | poll BMKG: 3-hourly, three days, no key. `ws` is km/h, `wd_deg` is where the wind comes from, `tp` is rain in mm for the step | | `FORECAST_BMKG_ADM4` | empty | the Permendagri village code for this point, such as `51.03.05.2002` for Ungasan, Kuta Selatan. Without a code the pack logs one line and idles | | `FORECAST_OPENMETEO` | `0` | poll Open-Meteo, hourly, anywhere. Off because its free tier is non-commercial only, which is the operator's decision | | `FORECAST_POLL_HOURS` | `6` | how often the pack asks, whatever `POLL_SECONDS` is; a stamp in `out/forecast.last` keeps it across restarts and failures. Both publishers update a few times a day, and Open-Meteo's free tier is 10,000 calls a day per IP with each wind-field point counting as one | | `FORECAST_WIND_N` | `8` | points a side of the wind field: 8 × 8 | | `FORECAST_WIND_KM` | `30` | half-width of the wind field's square, in km | It also reads `NODE_LAT` and `NODE_LON`. ### What it does not know A forecast is often wrong, and the pack keeps it apart from what the node measures. Every channel in `channels.yml` is `role: derived`, `comparable: false` (sources `forecast-bmkg`, `forecast-om` and `forecast-gap`), and the `fc_` prefix is a second guard. Each value is stored at its valid time with `fc_lead_hours` beside it. Open-Meteo publishes no model run time, so its rows say `fetched`, not `issued`. With both sources on, `forecast-gap` records how far apart they are on temperature and wind for the same hour. With Open-Meteo on, each fetch also keeps the next day's hourly 10 m wind over the node's square as `out/ground/wind.json`, served at `GET /ground/wind` for the map. It asks with `cell_selection=nearest`, because the default moves a sea point to the nearest land cell, up to 12 km off. The field reaches no cell, alert or report.

title: Packs that ship · coast
text: Waves, swell and sea-surface temperature at the nearest ocean grid cell, every poll, from Open-Meteo's Marine API, which needs no key and works anywhere. It was written at Kuta Selatan, where the nearest cell is 5 km off the Bukit; a calmer sea such as Barcelona's would set the thresholds lower. | | | |---|---| | Kind | code | | Domain | `coast` | | Requires node | `>=0.10.0` | | Metrics | `wave_height_m`, `wave_direction`, `wave_period_s`, `swell_height_m`, `swell_period_s`, `sea_surface_temp` | | Scales | bioregion | | Sources | `environmental/bioregion/open-meteo-marine` | | Needs | `PACKS_ALLOW_CODE=1`; network to Open-Meteo Marine; an ocean cell within `COAST_MAX_KM` | | Scripts | none | | Attribution | Open-Meteo Marine API (CC BY 4.0), model data from Copernicus Marine / MeteoFrance MFWAM | The adapter writes one sensor, `marine-point`, with `source='open-meteo-marine'`, `kind='model'`, `scale='bioregion'`, `local=False` and cadence `PT1H`. The API snaps to the nearest ocean cell however far it is, so the adapter measures the distance and raises if it is over `COAST_MAX_KM`; a node in Ubud does not get the weather of a sea it cannot see. ### Rules | rule | level | cooldown | fires when | |---|---|---|---| | `heavy_swell` | info | 720 | `swell_height_m` is at least 2.5 and `swell_period_s` at least 12, the combination that means strong currents on exposed beaches | | `sea_warm_anomaly` | info | 1440 | the current sea-surface temperature is at least 1.0 °C above its own mean over days 7 to 60 back | ### Cells | cell | unit | state | min_buckets | what the SQL counts | |---|---|---|---|---| | `Environmental\|Bioregion` | sea surface temperature, 7d mean, °C (nearest ocean cell) | partial | | 7-day mean of `sea_surface_temp` on `marine-point`. Never `live`: it is a model | ### Settings | setting | default | meaning | |---|---|---| | `COAST_MAX_KM` | `30` | refuse to report if the nearest ocean cell is further away than this, in km | ### What it does not know The values are a wave model's at the nearest ocean grid cell, which may be kilometres off your beach, and the thresholds are set for the Bukit's coast. The wild `posidonia` pack reads this pack's `sea_surface_temp`, and without `coast` on it has nothing to read.

title: Packs that ship · surface-heat
text: How hot the ground in this node's own H3 resolution-8 cell got against the land 1 to 3 km around it, from Landsat's surface temperature at 30 m, and how warm the ground stays at night, from MODIS at 1 km. It reads once a day from Microsoft Planetary Computer, with no account. Nothing in it is specific to Bali. | | | |---|---| | Kind | code | | Domain | `heat` | | Requires node | `>=0.81.0` | | Metrics | `lst`, `lst_ring`, `lst_delta`, `lst_pctile`, `lst_night`, `lst_day` | | Scales | city | | Sources | none in `pack.yaml` yet; the registry entries are `environmental/city/landsat-c2-surface-temperature` and `environmental/city/modis-lst-mod11a1` | | Needs | `PACKS_ALLOW_CODE=1`; network to planetarycomputer.microsoft.com and its blob storage, once a day: about 1.5 MB the first day, half a megabyte on a day with a new Landsat scene | | Scripts | none | | Cells | none: a satellite retrieval of the ground is not measured here | | Attribution | Landsat courtesy of the U.S. Geological Survey, MODIS from NASA LP DAAC, both public domain, read through Microsoft Planetary Computer | The adapter writes two sensors, both `kind='model'`, `scale='city'`, `local=False`: `surface-cell` (`source='landsat-lst'`) from the newest clear Landsat 8/9 Collection 2 scene, and `surface-modis` (`source='modis-lst'`) from MOD11A1 and MYD11A1 v061. Every reading is stamped with the satellite's pass, not the poll. A scene counts when at least `SURFACE_HEAT_MIN_CLEAR` of the cell's land and of the ring's is clear in `QA_PIXEL`; water is on neither side. It adds no library: it reads only the few tiles of each Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFF around the node, with HTTP range requests, and remembers a scene in `out/surface-heat/state.json`. Its `readouts:` add three lines to the heat issue: the cell's ground temperature, the cell minus the ring, and the ground at night. Its `sections:` entry, `surface-heat` (stage observe, `wall: true`), shows four: those three and the ring's own. ### Rules | rule | level | cooldown | fires when | |---|---|---|---| | `ground` | (report) | | the last pass's `seen_at`, `ground_c`, `around_c`, `hotter_than_around_c`, `percentile_in_ring`, and `air_c` from the house's own outdoor sensor within half an hour of the pass, else the weather model's, with `air_from` saying which | ### Settings | setting | default | meaning | |---|---|---| | `SURFACE_HEAT_RING_KM` | `3` | the outer edge of the ring, in km; it starts at 1 km | | `SURFACE_HEAT_MIN_CLEAR` | `0.5` | the share of the cell's land, and of the ring's, that must be clear for a scene to count | ### What it does not know A ground temperature is the skin of roofs, roads and canopy. A roof at 45 °C is not a room at 45 °C, which is why the pack has no alert and no cell. Landsat gets one clear look every one to three weeks, at about 10:30.

title: Packs that ship · earth
text: The node's own copy of Google's AlphaEarth Satellite Embedding layers for its square of the planet, and the year-over-year per-pixel change computed here from them: cosine distance at 10 m. The node downloads them once, on command, keeps them as files and compares them with arithmetic. It says something changed, never what. | | | |---|---| | Kind | code | | Domain | `land` | | Requires node | `>=0.33.0` | | Metrics | `land_change_yoy`, `land_change_since_2017`, `years_cached` | | Scales | city | | Sources | `environmental/city/alphaearth-satellite-embedding` | | Needs | `PACKS_ALLOW_CODE=1`; `planetai packs install` for `rasterio` and `numpy` (`pip:`); network to `storage.googleapis.com` on the first fetch only. No key, no account, no cloud project. Disk: 64 MB per year cached, 576 MB for all nine | | Attribution | "The AlphaEarth Foundations Satellite Embedding dataset is produced by Google and Google DeepMind. CC BY 4.0.", carried with every derivative | The adapter writes `earth-point` (`kind='model'`, `scale='city'`) and reads only what is already cached under `out/earth/<node>/`: `<year>.npy`, `meta.json`, `change_<A>_<B>.png` and `.json`, `year_<YYYY>.png`. Nothing is downloaded on a poll. The directory is matched on the point and radius in its `meta.json`, so one written under an earlier `NODE_NAME` is adopted as it stands; `planetai run earth status` names any that no longer match and deletes nothing. ### Rules None. A threshold that fires in Kuta Selatan, where the land is being built on, also fires in Boston every year for reasons nobody there can act on: snow and leaf-off between two annual composites. A season cannot yet be told from a bulldozer, and the node does not send messages a household would ignore. ### Cells | cell | unit | state | min_buckets | what the SQL counts | |---|---|---|---|---| | `Environmental\|City` | land change: mean per-pixel cosine distance between consecutive annual AlphaEarth embeddings (0 = unchanged) | partial | 1 | the latest `land_change_yoy` observation on `earth-point` | It stays `partial`: the node did the arithmetic, but the input is a model's description of a place, which nobody here could repeat as a measurement. `air-quality` also has an `Environmental|City` cell, and `/cells` lists both. ### Scripts - `planetai run earth fetch [year ...] [--force]`: every year the dataset has (or `EARTH_YEARS`); `--force` re-reads a cached one. About 103 MB and 150 seconds per year, roughly 22 minutes for all nine, so run it from a shell and not over MCP. - `planetai run earth change [A B | --all] [--force]`: the two latest consecutive cached years, any two, or every consecutive pair plus the oldest-to-newest span. Read the span first, then the years. - `planetai run earth frames [--refit]`: one grey picture of the place per cached year for the card to animate, the first principal component of the embedding (not photographs). `--refit` redoes the projection, which a moved square needs and a new year does not. - `planetai run earth status`: years, bytes, comparisons, what the cell reports. - `planetai run earth verify`: seven checks, the dataset's claims against the files (unit-length vectors after de-quantising) and whether the reading landed. - `planetai run earth similar [year] [--out FILE]`: every pilot in `presets/` compared with the others and with its own tile. A regional search (one UTM tile, about 82 km a side). ### Settings | setting | default | meaning | |---|---|---| | `EARTH_RADIUS_M` | `5000` | half-width of the square around the node, in metres. 5000 is a 10 km square: 64 MB on disk and about 103 MB pulled, per year | | `EARTH_YEARS` | empty | which years to fetch, comma separated. Blank means every year the dataset has (2017 to 2025) | It also reads `NODE_LAT`, `NODE_LON`, `NODE_NAME`, `PACK_OUT` and `DATABASE_URL`. Write `VAR=value` in `.env` with no space after `=`: `VAR= value` is read by the shell as a command. ### What it does not know `CHANGED = 0.15`, at the top of `packs/earth/change.py`, is the one number in the pack that was chosen; at node #1 it sits at about the 99th percentile of a consecutive-year comparison. The number does not compare between places: for 2024 to 2025 the mean is 0.0414 in Kuta Selatan, 0.0404 in Boston, 0.0164 in Barcelona and 0.0151 in Santiago. Change the coordinates or the radius and `fetch` re-reads every cached year; a correction under 1% of the radius (never less than 25 m) is recorded as `point_drift_m` and leaves the cache alone.

title: Packs that ship · terrain
text: Where the next day's rain goes around the node. It reads its own square of Copernicus DEM GLO-30 once, on command, fills the hollows (priority-flood) and routes water downhill (D8), with numpy and a heap and no hydrology library. Each poll multiplies the ground that drains through the node's point by the next 24 hours of forecast rain. Nothing in it is specific to Bali, and it has no threshold to tune. | | | |---|---| | Kind | code | | Domain | `water` | | Requires node | `>=0.76` | | Metrics | `terrain_upslope_ha`, `terrain_upslope_near_ha`, `terrain_hollow_m`, `rain_24h_mm`, `water_24h_m3` | | Scales | city | | Sources | `environmental/planet/copernicus-dem-glo30` | | Needs | `PACKS_ALLOW_CODE=1`; `rasterio` and `numpy` (`pip:`, the same as `earth`); network to `copernicus-dem-30m.s3.amazonaws.com` (or `-90m`) on the fetch only, about half a megabyte for 10 km. No key. The `forecast` pack for the rain | | Cells | none: a surface model is not measured here | | Attribution | "produced using Copernicus WorldDEM-30 © DLR e.V. 2010-2014 and © Airbus Defence and Space GmbH 2014-2018 provided under COPERNICUS by the European Union and ESA; all rights reserved", and the licence's no-liability sentence, carried with every row | The adapter writes `terrain-point` (`kind='model'`, `scale='city'`, `local=False`). The three terrain rows carry the fetch's own timestamp; `rain_24h_mm` and `water_24h_m3` are stamped on the hour. The rain is `fc_rain` summed over the rows timestamped in the next 24 hours, from one source only, BMKG if it has rows, else Open-Meteo: adding both would double it. `water_24h_m3` is that rain on the upslope area, as if none of it soaked in. The pack ships the `water` issue (`packs/terrain/issue.yml`): context, four readouts, no line and no hero, so it never leads. Add `water` to `NODE_ISSUES` to draw it. ### Scripts - `planetai run terrain coverage`: which elevation this point would use, before anything is downloaded: your own file, GLO-30, GLO-90 where the 30 m tile is not public (25 tiles in the Caucasus on AWS), or none. - `planetai run terrain fetch`: read the square, fill, route, keep `out/terrain/<node>/terrain.json`. Run it again only when the node moves, the radius changes or the DEM changes. - `planetai run terrain verify`: five checks, including that every land cell drains to the window's edge or the sea after the fill, and that rows from this fetch reached the database. ### Settings | setting | default | meaning | |---|---|---| | `TERRAIN_RADIUS_M` | `5000` | half-width of the square, in metres. Water from further uphill than this is not counted | | `TERRAIN_DEM_PATH` | empty | a GeoTIFF of your own (a drone survey, a national LiDAR), used instead of Copernicus | | `TERRAIN_DEM_LICENCE` | empty | that file's licence, in words. Read on every poll: blank means the node computes from the file and sends no rows | ### What it does not know GLO-30 is a surface model: roofs and canopy are in the heights, and a 30 m pixel is a street block, so the pack speaks at region distance and never for the yard. It does not know the soil, the drains or the gutters. There is no wetness index and no percentile: on a filled pixel the index is mostly its slope clip, and a percentile gives every square a wettest tenth. At node #1 the house's own pixel drains 0.09 ha and the largest flow within 60 m drains 0.6 ha. The AWS copy is the 2021 release; the newer Copernicus Data Space copies are licensed for non-commercial use, and the pack does not read them.

title: Packs that ship · earth-engine
text: What the land within a kilometre of the node did last year, from Google Earth Engine's public catalog: tree, built, crop and water fractions (Dynamic World), annual median NDVI (Sentinel-2, clouds masked) and the latest night-lights radiance (VIIRS). Computed in Earth Engine and stamped mid-year, so a daily fetch inserts nothing new after the first. It is the worked example of a code pack with a dependency and a credential. | | | |---|---| | Kind | code | | Domain | `land` | | Requires node | `>=0.10.0` | | Metrics | `tree_frac`, `built_frac`, `crop_frac`, `water_frac`, `ndvi_median`, `night_lights` | | Scales | bioregion | | Needs | `PACKS_ALLOW_CODE=1`; `planetai packs install` for `earthengine-api` (`pip:`); a Google Earth Engine project (free for research and non-commercial use) and a service-account key mounted read-only at `config/ee-key.json` | | Rules | none; land change is the `earth` pack's | The adapter writes `ee-point` (`source='earth-engine'`, `kind='model'`, `scale='bioregion'`), and until it is configured the pack logs one line and idles. To set it up: 1. Register an Earth Engine project. 2. Create a service account with Earth Engine Resource Viewer and Service Usage Consumer (and Resource Writer for timelapse images). 3. Copy its JSON key to `config/ee-key.json` on the node. 4. Run `planetai packs install`, then `planetai restart`. 5. Run `planetai run earth-engine verify`; every step it names should pass. ### Cells | cell | unit | state | min_buckets | what the SQL counts | |---|---|---|---|---| | `Environmental\|Bioregion` | tree-cover fraction within 1 km (Dynamic World, last complete year) | partial | | the latest `tree_frac` reading on `ee-point` | ### Scripts - `planetai run earth-engine verify`: library, settings, key file, credentials, a real query, the datasets. Names the step that failed. - `planetai run earth-engine timelapse [--years a,b,c | --n 4 --gap 5] [--km 2] [--px 1024] [--source landsat|sentinel] [--lat --lon] [--dry-run]`: annual-median frames of clear pixels; Landsat by default (the only archive reaching 2010 with one instrument family), Sentinel-2 from 2016 at 10 m. PNGs and a side-by-side page land in `out/`. - `planetai run earth-engine basemap [--months 12] [--dry-run]`: the median of every clear Sentinel-2 pass over the last twelve months, built in the node's own Earth Engine project and kept as tiles at zoom 8 to 15 in `out/ground/imagery.mbtiles`, served at `GET /ground/imagery`. Earth Engine learns the two squares once, and the script says so before it runs. ### Settings | setting | default | meaning | |---|---|---| | `EE_PROJECT` | empty | the project id, such as `planetai-node-472103`, and not the service account's 21-digit number; Earth Engine reports that mistake as "project not found". Blank reads it from the key file | | `EE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT` | empty | blank is fine; the key file names it | | `EE_KEY_FILE` | `/app/config/ee-key.json` | the JSON key, copied to `config/ee-key.json` on the node. `config/` is mounted read-only | | `GROUND_SAT_WIDE_KM` | `60` | `basemap`: half-width of the wide context square, in km. The close square is `place`'s `GROUND_RADIUS_KM` | ### What it does not know Dynamic World is a classifier, and a kilometre around a house is mostly other people's land, so the cell is `partial` always. The Earth Engine land-change score that used to live here and the per-pixel distance in `earth` measure different things and did not agree, so only `earth`'s is kept. The adapter's own comments say it has not yet run against a live account.

title: Packs that ship · place
text: What is around the node, from OpenStreetMap, kept in PostGIS on the node and summarised once a month: buildings and how much ground they cover, shops and warungs, schools, clinics, temples, roads, green, and the walk to the nearest of each. It describes structure and change, and says nothing about behaviour. | | | |---|---| | Kind | code | | Domain | `place` | | Requires node | `>=0.26.0` | | Metrics | 22: `buildings`, `built_share`, `commercial_share`, `businesses_per_km2`, `poi_food`, `poi_retail`, `poi_education`, `poi_health`, `poi_worship`, `poi_lodging`, `poi_services`, `roads_km`, `green_share`, `nearest_school_m`, `nearest_health_m`, `nearest_market_m`, `nearest_worship_m`, and the satellite half `sat_buildings`, `sat_confidence`, `osm_building_coverage`, `sat_buildings_yearly`, `sat_height_m_yearly` | | Scales | community | | Sources | `economic/community/openstreetmap` (the registry files OpenStreetMap once) | | Needs | `PACKS_ALLOW_CODE=1`; `planetai packs install` (`pip:` `earthengine-api`); network to the Overpass API; PostGIS in the node's database image. For the optional Open Buildings half, the `earth-engine` pack's credentials | | Attribution | © OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL, via Overpass; Google Open Buildings V3 and Temporal v1 (CC BY 4.0) via Earth Engine | The adapter writes `place-point` (`kind='map'`, `scale='community'`) and creates the tables `place_features`, `place_runs`, `place_yearly` and `place_buildings_sat` after `CREATE EXTENSION postgis`. The first poll fetches everything within `PLACE_RADIUS_M` from Overpass, later polls recompute from what is stored, and every `PLACE_REFRESH_DAYS` it fetches again. It also notices a moved node (more than 1% of the radius, never less than 25 m) and refetches, clearing the satellite footprints and yearly series of the old circle. ### Rules | rule | level | cooldown | fires when | |---|---|---|---| | `place_around` | info | 43200 (`long_cooldown_ok`) | the `place-point` observations have `buildings > 0`: one message a month describing the circle | ### Cells | cell | unit | state | min_buckets | what the SQL counts | |---|---|---|---|---| | `Economic\|Community` | businesses per km² within the radius | partial | 1 | the latest `businesses_per_km2` observation on `place-point` | Business density stands in until a fab lab's machine log or a market's stall count exists, which is why the cell says `partial`. ### Scripts - `planetai run place refresh`: force a fetch from Overpass, so edits to the map reach the node within minutes. - `planetai run place gaps`: the mapping briefing, with untyped buildings, empty categories, named places without hours and unnamed streets, written to `out/place-gaps.md` for a mapping afternoon at the lab. - `planetai run place verify`: PostGIS, OpenStreetMap, Earth Engine and Open Buildings, each step named; it names the mismatch after a move. - `planetai run place basemap [--only vector|drone] [--dry-run]`: keeps a map of the place on the node's disk, in `out/ground/`, served at `GET /ground/*`: OpenStreetMap vector tiles cut from Protomaps' daily build, in three rings to zoom 15, with the label fonts, and any OpenAerialMap drone mosaic (CC BY 4.0) that crosses the drone ring. Protomaps and OpenAerialMap learn the square once, and the script says so before it runs. `planetai run place satellite` also shows in the script list, because `satellite.py` is a non-adapter `.py` in the folder. It is a module the adapter imports, not a command. ### Settings | setting | default | meaning | |---|---|---| | `PLACE_RADIUS_M` | `1000` | radius around the node to describe, in metres | | `PLACE_REFRESH_DAYS` | `30` | how often to re-fetch from OpenStreetMap | | `GROUND_RADIUS_KM` | `12` | `basemap`: half-width of the street-level square, in km | | `GROUND_DRONE_RADIUS_KM` | `4` | `basemap`: the ring a drone mosaic must cross, in km | | `GROUND_DRONE_MAXZ` | `18` | `basemap`: the finest zoom kept for a drone mosaic | It also reads `OVERPASS_URL` (default `https://overpass-api.de/api/interpreter`) and, for Open Buildings, `EE_KEY_FILE`, `EE_PROJECT` and `EE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT`. ### What it does not know A zero means unmapped, and every message and label says so: a circle with no school may only be a circle where nobody has mapped one. If the map is wrong about your place, fix the map, and never from Google Maps or Google imagery. With the `earth-engine` credentials in place, the monthly refresh also fetches Google Open Buildings V3 footprints (confidence at or above 0.65) and the Temporal dataset's yearly building count and mean height for 2016 to 2023; `GET /history?sensor_id=place-point&metric=sat_buildings_yearly` is the series. After a move it takes `planetai restart`, `planetai run place refresh` and a dashboard reload.

title: Packs that ship · make
text: Where somebody can go to make or fix something: the active fab labs nearest the node, from the Fab Lab Network directory, with what each one can do. It names the place and stops there: nothing in the code hands a job to a workshop. | | | |---|---| | Kind | code | | Domain | `make` | | Requires node | `>=0.64.0` | | Metrics | none | | Scales | community | | Sources | `economic/community/fablabs-io`, `economic/community/fablabs-network-data-archive` | | Needs | `PACKS_ALLOW_CODE=1` and `MAKE_ENABLED=1`; network to `gitlab.fabcloud.org` (the default) or `api.fablabs.io`; `NODE_LAT` and `NODE_LON` | | Rules and cells | none: `rules.yml` is comments only and there is no `cells.yml` | `MAKE_ENABLED` ships as `0`, and the pack has its own switch because an empty `PACKS_ENABLED` means every pack. Set `MAKE_ENABLED=1` in `.env`, then `planetai restart`. `planetai doctor` says which state the node is in: off, with the reason; `make: <n> fab lab(s) within 50 km · fablabs.io @ <snapshot> · read <date>`; or `make: no fab lab within 50 km of this node yet`. It stores one `sensors` row per active lab inside `MAKE_RADIUS_KM`, a `facility` with no readings; the row and its `meta` are on [Data schema](schema.md). `meta` never holds an email or a telephone number, although most upstream records carry them. A facility reaches no metric, cell or alert, and is never in custody. Near the end of the report, after what happened and before the to-do lines, it adds one sentence: ``` Nearest place to make or fix something: <lab>, <km> km (<up to three capabilities>). ``` It is in Indonesian and Spanish too, capability names included (`laser cutting`, `pemotongan laser`, `corte láser`). A lab under 0.05 km away prints as `<0.1 km`. The same sentence travels in `GET /issues` as `asks.where`, and the dashboard draws it in Act, under the record of what was asked and answered. With the pack off, the dashboard shows the help text the node publishes for `MAKE_ENABLED`. ### Settings | setting | default | meaning | |---|---|---| | `MAKE_ENABLED` | `0` | the pack's own on-switch. Read the licence note below first | | `MAKE_RADIUS_KM` | `50` | how far to look for a lab, in km | | `MAKE_SOURCE` | `archive` | `archive` reads the Fab Foundation's dated monthly snapshots at `gitlab.fabcloud.org/fl-management/fablab-network-data`; `live` reads `api.fablabs.io/0/labs.json`, whose own root page says it has been removed | | `MAKE_SNAPSHOT` | empty | which dated snapshot to read, such as `2026.07.31_labs.json`. Blank takes the newest and logs that it did. A pin makes every node on it answer the same way | | `MAKE_REFRESH_DAYS` | `30` | how often to re-read. The archive is monthly | One read is about 5.3 MB and the publisher ignores every query parameter, so the pack checks staleness before it fetches, and a node that already has its labs does nothing. ### What it does not know Active labs with no coordinates cannot be placed; the adapter counts them and logs the number on every read. > **Careful.** The directory is not openly licensed. Each lab keeps copyright in its own record (fablabs.io > Terms of Use §8.1), no data licence is published, and §7.4 and §7.5 restrict bulk collection and commercial > use. Fab City Foundation decided that PLANETAI may read it and accepted responsibility for that, pending a > Terms of Use clause. That decision covers the Foundation and not each node's operator, who is a separate > party to those terms. The full reading is in `data/sources/data/economic/community/fablabs-io.yaml` and > `packs/make/README.md`. If that matters to you, leave this pack off.

title: Packs that ship · fire
text: Fires that satellites saw near the node in the last day, from NASA FIRMS: how many, how far, in which direction, and whether they lie where the wind is coming from. It says when a fire is near, when one is upwind, and, only when the air outside is rising too, that smoke is probably arriving. | | | |---|---| | Kind | code | | Domain | `air` | | Requires node | `>=0.81.0` | | Metrics | `fires_local_24h`, `fires_region_24h`, `frp_local_mw`, `frp_region_mw`, `fires_nearest_km`, `fires_nearest_bearing`, `fires_local_upwind`, `fires_region_upwind`, `fires_upwind_km`, `fires_upwind_bearing`, `fire_wind_from_deg` | | Scales | bioregion | | Sources | `environmental/bioregion/nasa-firms` | | Needs | `PACKS_ALLOW_CODE=1` and `FIRE_ENABLED=1`; network to `firms.modaps.eosdis.nasa.gov`; `NODE_LAT` and `NODE_LON` | | Scripts | none | | Cells | none | | Attribution | NASA FIRMS, VIIRS 375 m active fire detections from NOAA-20, NOAA-21 and Suomi NPP, distributed by LANCE; NASA data are CC0 | It is off unless `FIRE_ENABLED=1` because of the bandwidth. Without a key it reads FIRMS's public regional file per satellite whenever that file changed, 1 to 2 MB a satellite for South East Asia, and the 7-day file once at first start; it asks with HEAD first, at most every `FIRE_POLL_HOURS`, and an unchanged file writes no rows. The region file is `SouthEast_Asia` or `Europe` when the whole regional ring fits it, else `Global`. With `FIRMS_MAP_KEY` (listed under `secrets:`) it asks the keyed area API for the ring's box instead. The adapter writes one sensor, `firms-fires` (`source='firms'`, `kind='model'`, `scale='bioregion'`, `local=False`, no coordinates), and every channel is `derived`. Counts are burning places, one per ~445 m cell a day however many satellites saw it, with low confidence dropped. Upwind is within 45° of where the wind comes from, by the node's own wind: a local kit, then the core Open-Meteo point, then `fc_wind_direction` bounded `ts <= now()`. Its `sections:` entry, `fire` (stage observe, `wall: true`), shows fires nearby, in the region and upwind, and the nearest fire's distance and bearing; it stays out of `/issues` until the node holds a row of it. ### Rules The rules are not kinded, so they send the same way on every `ALERT_ENGINE`. Each message gives the place as a distance and a compass direction from the house. The thresholds were written from one day of FIRMS at Kuta Selatan (`thresholds:` in `pack.yaml`). | rule | level | cooldown | fires when | |---|---|---|---| | `fire_near` | info | 1440 | at least one fire in the local ring | | `fire_upwind_near` | warn | 720 | at least one fire in the local ring is upwind | | `smoke_arriving` | act | 1440 | 25 or more burning places upwind in the regional ring, and outdoor PM2.5 (outdoor sensors, else CAMS) over the last 2 hours past the WHO line of 15 µg/m³ and half again its level of the 6 hours before | 25 is about half of everything the 150 km ring held on the day the pack was written. It is a first guess and has not been calibrated. ### Settings | setting | default | meaning | |---|---|---| | `FIRE_ENABLED` | `0` | the pack's own on-switch | | `FIRE_LOCAL_KM` | `25` | the local ring, in km: burning near enough to smell | | `FIRE_REGION_KM` | `150` | the regional ring, in km: smoke that travels. Singapore may want 500 | | `FIRE_POLL_HOURS` | `3` | how often to ask, in hours | | `FIRE_SATELLITES` | `noaa-20,noaa-21` | any of `noaa-20`, `noaa-21`, `suomi-npp`, one file each | | `FIRMS_MAP_KEY` | empty | optional, a secret: the keyed area API instead of the public files | ### What it does not know A small rubbish fire is usually below what a 375 m pixel sees, and cloud hides fires, so an empty ring does not mean clean air.

title: Packs that ship · open-data-health
text: Turns a CKAN portal's maintenance state into a `Governance|City` cell: how much of a city's open data was touched in the last 90 days, since a portal nobody updates is an archive. It was written from the Index registry, which lists four CKAN portals under `governance|city`. | | | |---|---| | Kind | data | | Domain | `governance` | | Requires node | `>=0.3.0` | | Scales | city, region | | Sources | `governance/city/open-data-bcn`, `governance/city/analyze-boston`, `governance/city/datos-gob-cl`, `governance/city/bali-satu-data` | | Needs | the core `ckan` adapter, with `CKAN_PORTALS` set in `.env`; a CKAN portal with a public `package_search` endpoint | | Scripts | none | | Settings | none of its own; the `ckan` adapter reads `CKAN_PORTALS` | ### Rules | rule | level | cooldown | fires when | |---|---|---|---| | `portal_gone_stale` | warn | 10080 | a `kind='portal'` observation of `datasets_fresh_pct` is under 10 | ### Cells | cell | unit | state | min_buckets | what the SQL counts | |---|---|---|---|---| | `Governance\|City` | % of published datasets updated in the last 90 days | partial | | mean of the latest `datasets_fresh_pct` per portal, over portals read in the last 7 days | | `Governance\|City` | open datasets published | partial | | sum of the latest `datasets_total` per portal, over portals read in the last 7 days | ### What it does not know The 10% line is a guess until someone watches a real portal for a quarter and corrects it. The dataset count says little; the share touched in 90 days says whether anyone is home. Socrata and ArcGIS portals would need their own adapters, and the cell SQL would stay the same.

title: Packs that ship · thingdata
text: Reads one or more ThingData servers, the reuse-city repair-knowledge protocol, and turns each catalogue into observations: how many things are described, how many have a repair guide or story, and whether anyone is still writing. It was written against the reference implementation's source and has not met a deployment yet. | | | |---|---| | Kind | code | | Domain | `repair` | | Requires node | `>=0.10.0` | | Metrics | `things_total`, `guides_total`, `stories_total`, `things_documented_pct`, `knowledge_fresh_90d_pct` | | Scales | city, region | | Needs | `PACKS_ALLOW_CODE=1`; a ThingData server with the v0.1.3 public read API (`GET /api/v1/{things,guides,stories,relationships}`, no auth) | | Scripts | none | | Attribution | ThingData Protocol server (reuse-city), github.com/reuse-city/thingdata-server | The adapter writes one sensor per server, `thingdata-<slug>`, with `kind='portal'`, `local=False`, the scale from `THINGDATA_SCALE`, cadence `P1D` and no coordinates. There is no count endpoint, so it pages the whole catalogue, 100 rows a request, and refuses above `THINGDATA_MAX` instead of reporting a truncated total. A thing counts as documented when a guide or story names it, or a relationship from one points at it. The freshness figure is the share of guides and stories written or revised in the last 90 days. With `THINGDATA_INSTANCES` blank the pack idles. ### Rules | rule | level | cooldown | fires when | |---|---|---|---| | `repair_commons_quiet` | warn | 10080 (`long_cooldown_ok`) | a `kind='portal'` observation of `knowledge_fresh_90d_pct` is under 10 | The 10% line is the guess `open-data-health` makes about portals, carried over unchanged. ### Cells | cell | unit | state | min_buckets | what the SQL counts | |---|---|---|---|---| | `Economic\|City` | % of catalogued things with a repair guide or story | partial | | mean of the latest `things_documented_pct` per server, over servers read in the last 7 days | | `Economic\|City` | repair guides and stories published | partial | | sum of the latest `guides_total` and `stories_total` per server, over servers read in the last 7 days | The cell keys are literals and say City. A node whose server covers a region should edit both to `Economic|Region`, as the comment in `cells.yml` says. ### Settings | setting | default | meaning | |---|---|---| | `THINGDATA_INSTANCES` | empty | the servers to read, `slug=url`, comma separated. Blank, the pack idles | | `THINGDATA_SCALE` | `city` | the scale of what those servers cover, `city` or `region` | | `THINGDATA_MAX` | `5000` | refuse to count a collection larger than this | ### What it does not know ThingData entities carry no coordinates, so a server three continents away counts the same as the one down the road. The pack cannot tell whether a guide is any good, whether anyone followed it, or whether a thing was repaired.

title: Packs that ship · things
text: The things this home keeps and the ones it offers: `GET /things`, `POST /things`, `PATCH` and `DELETE /things/{id}` (the admin token only) and `GET /offers` (every share level, by the household's choice). One row per thing, with how often it is used, whether it works and whether it is offered; three private counts per class (`stock`, `idle`, `repair`) written as readings on the node's own survey sensor whenever one changes, so a readout, a rule or a cell can use them and nothing sends them. An offer is a public line at the node's res-8 cell, with a link to the node's Telegram bot, which passes one message on to the household. | | | |---|---| | Kind | code: `routes.py`, no adapter | | Domain | `things` | | Requires node | `>=0.83.0` | | Shares | `/offers` on every level (`share: {"off": [/offers]}`) | | Rules and cells | none yet | Core until 24 October 2026. The `things` table stays in `init.sql`, and the private role on the counts stays declared by the core, so a node that switches this pack off keeps its readings private and loses no row. With the pack off, `/things` and `/offers` answer 404 and the daily export carries no offers. On `planetai update`, a node that lists its packs in `PACKS_ENABLED` gets `things` added, because every node had it.

title: Packs that ship · eyes
text: The pictures a household takes of its own place, and what is in them: `POST`/`GET /captures`, `PATCH`/`DELETE /captures/{id}`, `GET /captures/{id}/file`, `POST /captures/{id}/describe` and `GET /species`. A picture is cleaned on arrival (its location kept as a cell, never a point) and kept on its own disk. The image model on this house's own network describes it as findings in the flows classes, the model's until a person confirms one. With `SPECIES_MATCH` on, a finding's scientific name is asked of GBIF, and two weekly reads say whether this country lists it as introduced or invasive (GRIIS) and how many open records others have made in the node's seven cells. | | | |---|---| | Kind | code: `routes.py` and two weekly jobs (`check_griis`, `check_others`), no adapter | | Domain | `species` | | Requires node | `>=0.83.0` | | Needs | a disk for the pictures; the image model on the house's network; `api.gbif.org` with `SPECIES_MATCH` on | | Rules and cells | none: a finding is the model's until a person confirms it | Core until 24 October 2026. The `captures` table stays in `init.sql` and the pictures stay where they are; the three settings stay the core's, because two of them change what leaves the house. With the pack off, the routes answer 404, the Data door says so, and the weekly reads do not run. On `planetai update`, a node that lists its packs in `PACKS_ENABLED` gets `eyes` added, because every node had it.

title: Packs that ship · example-cooking-hours
text: The worked example: don't shout about indoor PM2.5 during normal cooking hours, say it once, after. It has two files, `pack.yaml` and `rules.yml`, and no README. | | | |---|---| | Kind | data | | Domain | none declared in `pack.yaml`; `docs/PACKS.md` places it under the `air` issue | | Requires node | `>=0.1.1` | | Scales | community | | Needs | a local indoor PM2.5 sensor | | Scripts | none | | Settings | none | | Cells | none: it is an example of a rule | ### Rules | rule | level | cooldown | fires when | |---|---|---|---| | `post_cooking_summary` | info | 1440 | between 20:00 and 23:59 local time, a local indoor sensor's 15-minute PM2.5 mean is over 35.5; one row per sensor with its `peak` | ### What it does not know Cooking hours are fixed in the SQL, 20:00 to 23:59, and the pack cannot tell cooking from any other source of indoor smoke at that hour. The comment on its `kind: data` line explains the distinction for every pack: data means rules and cells only, and code means the folder ships `adapter.py`; the loader now counts any `.py` file.

title: Packs that ship · Where this leads
text: A pack that reads an outside source names it in `sources:`, and that id has to be an entry in the network's registry first. The entries nobody has written a pack or an adapter for yet are listed on [the source registry](sources.md); how to write the one your place needs is on [Packs](packs.md).

title: Packs
text: A pack is how a place teaches its node what to watch and what to say about it. The core names no metric: what `pm25` means, which line matters in this house, and the sentence a person should read at 9 pm are all written in a pack. A data pack is SQL and words. A code pack also fetches, adding a source the core does not read. There are two tiers: | | core | wild | |---|---|---| | lives in | `packs/` in the node's repository, twenty-five of them | its author's own repository, or a folder in [fabcity/planetai-wild-packs](https://github.com/fabcity/planetai-wild-packs) | | reaches a node | with every release | `planetai packs add` | | checked by | the node's `make lint` and tests, on every commit | the wild-packs repository's CI, against the node's `main`, every week | | kept by | the node's maintainers | its author | What the core packs do is on [Packs that ship](packs-reference.md). This page is the contract as `app/packs.py` reads it, how to add a wild pack, and one small data pack built step by step. ``` packs/<id>/ pack.yaml id, name, description, version, requires, domain, sources:, pip:, env:, secrets:, switch:, share:, footprint:, readouts:, sections: rules.yml alerts: SQL that returns rows, one message per row; or a contribution to the report cells.yml Index cells: SQL that returns one `value` issue.yml the dashboard issue this pack ships, read while the pack is on (see Issues) channels.yml what the pack's own metrics ARE: ambient, enclosure, device_health, derived, index, private adapter.py a new source; its presence makes this a code pack hooks.py on_readings and on_alert, what the pack does with what the node stores and sends; MQTT_TOPICS and on_mqtt, what it reads off the broker; also code routes.py the pack's own HTTP routes, mounted at start for a core pack and 404 while it is off; also code *.py scripts, run with `planetai run <pack> <script>` README.md where the thresholds came from, which place they were written for, what the pack does not know ```

title: Packs · Add a wild pack
text: 1. **Run `planetai packs add <id>`** with an id from the wild list, such as `posidonia`, or `planetai packs add <owner>/<repo>[/<folder>][@<ref>]` for any pack on GitHub. The node fetches the commit, pins it, and prints `● <id>: added, a data pack, from <source> at <commit>`. It warns when the pack is not on the list, or is listed and not yet reviewed, and when it is a code pack. Then it adds any settings the pack declares to `.env`, as `planetai packs install` does. 2. **Run `planetai restart`, then `planetai packs`.** The pack is under `wild:` with where it came from, the commit and the day it was added, and which of its scripts an agent may run. Run `planetai packs add` again to update it. To remove it, delete `packs/<id>` and restart. A wild pack never replaces a core pack or a folder you put there by hand.

title: Packs · How packs load
text: Every folder under `packs/` with a `pack.yaml` is a pack, in sorted order. `PACKS_ENABLED` filters that list: blank means every pack, otherwise a comma list of ids. The loader reads the folders on every pass, and `packs/` is mounted into the app container, so a folder you add is seen within a minute without a restart. A folder that `planetai packs add` put there carries a `.wild` file beside its `pack.yaml`; any other folder counts as core. A pack is a code pack if its folder has any `.py` file. The loader sets `kind` from that and ignores the `kind:` line in `pack.yaml`. An adapter or hooks runs with the node's privileges and network access, so it runs only with `PACKS_ALLOW_CODE=1`: read it first. Without that setting the node logs `pack <id> ships code; set PACKS_ALLOW_CODE=1 to run it (read <path> first)` and loads the pack's rules and cells anyway. Because blank `PACKS_ENABLED` means every pack, a pack that must stay off by default has its own setting. `make` waits for `MAKE_ENABLED=1`, because it reads a directory that is not openly licensed, and `fire` for `FIRE_ENABLED=1`, for the bandwidth; both also need `PACKS_ALLOW_CODE=1`. `bali-air-dispatch` names `BAD_ENABLED` as its `switch:`, and a core pack with a switch runs its adapter and hooks when the switch is `1`, without `PACKS_ALLOW_CODE`; `air-quality`, `home-assistant`, `smartcitizen`, `airgradient` and `purpleair` have one too. A `pack.yaml`, `rules.yml`, `cells.yml` or adapter that does not parse is logged and skipped, and the rest of the node carries on. Every installed pack's `env:` keys, enabled or not, appear in Set up → Packs with their help text and default. Rule ids are namespaced `<pack>/<id>`; the core's rules in `config/rules.yml` keep the ids written there.

title: Packs · Your first data pack
text:
Five steps, each with something to check. The pack watches temperature, because most kits report it. If your sensors do not, pick a metric they do report and change `temp` in both files. **1. See what your node measures.** Run `planetai sensors`. The rows marked `yours` are the ones a rule written with `local` will read. A pack teaches the node about readings it already holds; it adds no sensor. **2. Make the folder.** In the node's directory (`~/planetai` on an installed node), create `packs/my-room/pack.yaml`: ```yaml id: my-room name: My room description: How warm the rooms this node measures have been, as one alert a day and one Index cell. version: 0.1.0 requires: { node: ">=0.72.0" } domain: heat ``` Within a minute `planetai packs` lists it under `loaded now:`, in `core:`, as `my-room data How warm the rooms…`. If it does not appear and `PACKS_ENABLED` is not blank, add `my-room` to that list. `domain: heat` puts the pack's alerts under the heat issue on the dashboard. **3. Teach it one thing to say.** Create `packs/my-room/rules.yml`. The line is set low on purpose, so it fires now and you see the whole path; step 5 moves it. ```yaml - id: room_warm level: info cooldown_minutes: 1440 sql: | SELECT sensor_id, name, mean_1h FROM stats WHERE local AND metric = 'temp' AND mean_1h > 20 message: en: "🌡️ {name} has averaged {mean_1h:.1f} °C over the last hour.

👉 Open a window on the shaded side, or switch on a fan." id: "🌡️ Suhu rata-rata {name} {mean_1h:.1f} °C selama satu jam terakhir.

👉 Buka jendela di sisi yang teduh, atau nyalakan kipas angin." es: "🌡️ {name} ha promediado {mean_1h:.1f} °C durante la última hora.

👉 Abre una ventana del lado de la sombra, o enciende un ventilador." ``` Rules run every 60 seconds. Run `planetai status`: under `alerts` it prints the time and the start of your message, with your sensor's name and its last hour filled in. That row is in the `alerts` table under the id `my-room/room_warm`, and it will not repeat for that sensor for 1440 minutes. At the default `ALERT_LEVEL=act` an `info` alert is recorded, shown on the dashboard and carried by the next report, and interrupts nobody (see [Alerts](alerts.md)). If nothing appears, `planetai logs | grep my-room` shows `rule my-room/room_warm failed: …` with Postgres's reason. **4. Say which Index cell it becomes.** Create `packs/my-room/cells.yml`: ```yaml - cell: "Environmental|Community" unit: "°C (24h mean, sensors in this node's custody)" state: live min_buckets: 12 notes: "my-room: every temperature channel in custody, hourly means, last 24 h" sql: | SELECT avg(mean) AS value FROM readings_1h r JOIN sensors s USING (sensor_id) WHERE s.custody AND r.metric = 'temp' AND r.bucket > now() - interval '24 hours' ``` Run `planetai cells`. A new `Environmental|Community` row carries your value, its state and your unit. `planetai cells --json` shows the full row, with `source: "planetai-node · pack:my-room"` and a note ending in `<have>/12 hourly buckets`. The state reads `partial` until the node holds 12 hourly buckets from sensors in its custody and enough of those sensors report (see [Cells](#cells)). A row like this, a mean with its provenance, is the only form in which a place's measurements reach the Fab City Index (see [Federation](federation.md)). **5. Move the line to your place.** Change `20` in the SQL to the temperature this room should not pass, and say in a `README.md` where that number came from. To make it an alert that asks for something, set `level: act`, keep `cooldown_minutes` at or under 2880, add `watch: {metric: temp, over: <the same number>}` so the node can time how long an action took to work, and add `{line}` to the message so it names the line. The cooldown still counts from the `info` alert of step 3, so the first `act` alert comes once those 1440 minutes have passed with the room still over the line. Then a 🔴 message reaches Telegram if it is connected, the heat issue's state is `act`, and the lead's last line counts the alert (`1 alert open · in Decide` when it is the only one). What a person records against it counts in [ρ](rho.md). On a checkout of the repository, `python3 tools/check_rules.py` (it needs `sqlglot`) parses every pack against `init.sql` and prints `55 rules and cells check out against init.sql`, two more with your folder added. A `{placeholder}` the SQL does not return is refused here and named; on a running node the same mistake sends the raw template, braces and all.

title: Packs · Fields in pack.yaml
text: | field | used for | |---|---| | `id` | the pack's name; defaults to the folder | | `name` | what a person calls it; the Packs card in Set up shows it, and falls back to `id` | | `description` | shown by `planetai packs` and `GET /packs` | | `kind: data` | `data` or `code`; the loader overwrites it: `code` when the pack ships any `.py` file (an adapter, hooks or a script), `data` when it ships none | | `version: 0.1.0` | the pack's own version, returned in `GET /packs`; nothing compares it | | `requires: {node: ">=0.76"}` | the node versions the pack loads on. A node outside the range does not load it, says so once in its log, and lists it under "not loaded" in `planetai packs`. Declare at least `>=0.76` for `readouts` or `sections`, which an older node ignores without a word | | `domain` | which dashboard issue the pack feeds (`air`, `heat`, `land`, `coast`, …). A cross-domain pack's rules are claimed one by one in an `issue.yml`. A pack that reaches no issue, is not one of the domains outside them (`weather`, `place`, `governance`, `repair`) and ships an alert no issue claims fails `tests/test_issues.py`. See [Issues](issues.md) | | `sources: [environmental/community/bali-air-dispatch]` | the registry ids of the data sources it reads. `make lint` runs `tools/check_registry.py`, which fails and names any id that is not an entry in the registry the node carries. See [The source registry](sources.md) | | `pip: [earthengine-api]` | libraries `planetai packs install` builds into the image, once, as the union of the lists of the packs this node loads (every folder, when the node is down) | | `footprint:` | where the pack's word reaches, drawn on the page as the cells that cover it: `key`, `name`, `what`, the `setting` that holds the radius with its `default` and `unit` (`km` or `m`), `shape` (`circle` or `square`), `base_res`, and `native_m` when the source has a grain of its own (earth's 10 m). Read while the pack is on; coast, earth and place declare one | | `share: {open: [/path]}` | the paths this pack's `routes.py` serves that join the `open` share list, or with `"off"` (quoted, since YAML reads a bare `off` as false) every share level. A wild pack's are ignored. `forecast`, `nearby`, `earth` and `earth-engine` declare `open`, `things` declares `"off"` | | `env: ["# comment", "KEY=default"]` | settings `planetai packs install` appends to `.env` under a dated marker when the key is absent; a comment line travels with the key under it. No space after `=` | | `secrets: [CAMERA_WYZE_BRIDGE_TOKEN]` | which of its `env` keys are secrets. Set up and the agent's `settings_get` mask them once saved, like the node's own tokens; a key not listed here is shown to anyone holding the admin token | | `switch: BAD_ENABLED` | the pack's own on-switch, usually one of its `env` keys. A core pack that names one runs its `adapter.py` and `hooks.py` when the switch is `1`, without `PACKS_ALLOW_CODE`; a wild pack still needs the flag. It may be a list of keys, on when any is set and not 0 (`smartcitizen`: `[SC_USER, SC_DEVICES, MQTT_HOST]`). Set up draws any pack's `…_ENABLED` key as a switch | | `stations: {source, prefix, radius, box, url, attribution}` | a network of other people's stations the pack reads, for "Air stations nearby", `GET /nearby` and the ring on the map. `box` (south, north, west, east) is where the network has stations; `radius` names the key that sets how far the ring reaches | | `agent_scripts: [verify]` | which of a wild pack's scripts a connected agent may run through `run_pack_script`. Leave it out and none do; a core pack's are all open, and `planetai run` runs every script either way. No agent can run `adapter.py` as a script | | `readouts: {air: [ … ]}` | numbers the pack adds to an issue, in the shape an issue file uses; shown in Figures, and in the sentence of a context issue. It adds and never replaces. See [PACKS.md](https://github.com/fabcity/planetai-node/blob/main/docs/PACKS.md#readouts-on-an-issue) | | `sections: [ … ]` | a band the pack declares on the dashboard as data, drawn with the page's own readout cards. See [A dashboard section](#a-dashboard-section) | | `needs: [api.bmkg.go.id]` | hosts the pack reaches, for people to read | | `author`, `attribution` | who wrote it and answers for it; the licence line a source asks to be credited with | | `metrics: [pm25, pm10]`, `scales: [community, city]` | what it measures and at which scales, for a reader choosing a pack. No code reads either: the channels a pack really produces are in `channels.yml`, and the cells it fills in `cells.yml` | | `thresholds: US EPA / WHO 2021` | one line on where its numbers come from; the README says the rest |

title: Packs · Rules
text:
YAML only. A rule's SQL runs every 60 seconds as the read-only role `planetai_ro`: every table but `settings`, and no writes, so a rule cannot read a token into an alert or change a row. Postgres does the maths, `corr()` included. The first rule in `packs/air-quality/rules.yml`, with its message shortened: ```yaml - id: indoor_pm25_high level: act cooldown_minutes: 120 watch: {metric: pm25, over: 35.5} sql: | SELECT sensor_id, name, mean_15m FROM stats WHERE local AND indoor AND metric = 'pm25' AND mean_15m > 35.5 message: en: "😷 The air inside at {name} is unhealthy right now … {line} µg/m³.

…

Run the purifier if you have one. …" id: "😷 Udara di dalam {name} sedang tidak sehat … {line} µg/m³.

…

Nyalakan pembersih udara kalau ada. …" es: "😷 El aire dentro de {name} no es saludable ahora mismo … {line} µg/m³.

…

Enciende el purificador si tienes uno. …" ``` | field | required | meaning | |---|---|---| | `id` | yes | becomes `<pack>/<id>` | | `sql` | yes | one `SELECT`; every returned row is a candidate alert. A `sensor_id` column keys the cooldown; without one the row is the node's | | `level` | no (`info`) | `info`, `warn` or `act`; see [Alerts](alerts.md#levels) | | `cooldown_minutes` | no (60) | per rule and sensor, checked against `alerts`. An `act` rule may not exceed 2880, the window after which the node counts a silent rule as cleared; `tests/test_share.py` fails a slower one | | `long_cooldown_ok: true` | when cooldown > 20160 | tells the lint a cooldown over a fortnight is deliberate | | `watch: {metric, over}` | no | the indicator and the line the rule is about, so `GET /effect` can time how long after an action the reading came back under it, and `{line}` in the message prints it. The lint fails if the metric or the number is missing from the SQL. Leave it out where the rule fires on a relation between two readings | | `name` | no | what the household calls the alert in a learning ("unhealthy air inside"). Without one, the alert is named by its issue's `alert:`, then by its id | | `line: {value, label}` | no | the line the report names when it says whether the reading came back under it after the alert; `label` is whose line it is (`line_epa`, `line_who`), a key of the report's own words. The test fails if the number is not in the SQL | | `message` | unless `contributes` | a string or `{en, id, es}`, filled with the row by `str.format`; a `None` renders as a dash | | `contributes: report` | instead of `message` | never sent; the first row lands in the report bundle under the rule's id | | `kind`, `issue` | no | makes the rule the event engine's. `kind` is `ahead`, `unusual`, `spike`, `sustained` or `danger`; `issue` (default the issue the pack ships in its `issue.yml`, else the pack's id) is the story its rows fold into. Every row must carry `value`, `line` and, optionally, `over` (false for a row inside the margin, which keeps an open event open and never opens one). Under `ALERT_ENGINE=rules` the rule is skipped; under `shadow` and `events` it writes no `alerts` row. See [Alerts](alerts.md#the-event-engine) | The node picks `message[ALERT_LOCALE]` and falls back to `en`. Every shipped rule carries all three languages, and every `{placeholder}` in every language must be a column the top-level `SELECT` returns, or `{line}` with a `watch:`. End a message with a paragraph that starts with 👉 and says what a person does; the classic dashboard's Decide card shows it as "what this node suggests" (see [Alerts](alerts.md#what-an-alert-says)). A rule that treats indoor sensors as ambient will not be merged, which is what `NOT s.indoor` is for. `make lint` runs `tools/check_rules.py` (with sqlglot) over every rule and cell. Besides the limits in the table, it refuses unknown tables and columns, a cell without a `value`, and a rule with both a message and a contribution or with neither, which could fire and reach nobody. What a rule may read: | table or view | what it holds | |---|---| | `stats` | `sensor_id, metric, indoor, local, kind, scale, lat, lon, name, last, last_ts, silent_minutes, mean_15m, mean_1h, mean_24h`: the last 24 hours, sensors only | | `readings_1h` | hourly `mean, min, max, n` over all history; a filter on `bucket` reads only the hours it asks for | | `recent_15m` | quarter-hour means of the last 24 hours, with `apparent` | | `usual_by_hour` | each room's own median, p75 and p90 for each local hour, from the fourteen complete days before today | | `observations` | the latest value per slow source | | `readings`, `sensors`, `channel_roles` | the raw tables | The node's own position and time zone are Postgres settings: `current_setting('planetai.lat')`, `current_setting('planetai.lon')`, `current_setting('TimeZone')`. `NODE_TZ` is the session time zone, so `date_trunc('day', ts)` means the household's day. A contributor has no level, no cooldown and no message: ```yaml - id: digest contributes: report sql: SELECT round(avg(mean_1h)) AS inside FROM stats WHERE local AND indoor AND metric='pm25' ```

title: Packs · Cells
text: ```yaml - cell: "Environmental|Community" unit: "µg/m³ PM2.5 (24h mean, sensors in this node's custody)" state: live # live | partial | mock min_buckets: 12 notes: "your own outdoor and indoor kits, hourly means, last 24 h" sql: SELECT avg(mean) AS value FROM readings_1h r JOIN sensors s USING (sensor_id) WHERE s.custody AND r.metric='pm25' AND r.bucket > now() - interval '24 hours' ``` `state` is provenance. `live` means measured here; `partial` means derived, from a model or a portal, whatever its quality. Never claim `live` for a model. The core demotes `live` to `partial` when the in-custody hourly buckets in 24 hours are fewer than `min_buckets`, or when too few in-custody sensors report (two where the node has children or is above community scale, one otherwise), and appends `have/need hourly buckets` to the note. A `NULL` value leaves the cell out, so absent is never zero. The cell's source is recorded as `planetai-node · pack:<id>`, and the core adds one cell of its own, `Governance|<Scale>` = [ρ](rho.md). Each row also carries `registered`, `reviewed`, `candidate`, `capable` and `adapter` from [the source registry](sources.md), where `registered` means `reviewed`.

title: Packs · Channel roles
text: A pack that adds a metric says what it is, keyed on `(source, metric)`: ```yaml - { source: forecast-om, metric: fc_wind_speed, role: derived, comparable: false, unit: "km/h" } ``` Roles are `ambient`, `enclosure`, `device_health`, `derived`, `index` and `private`, defined on the [sensors](sensors.md) page. The core's `config/channels.yml` is read first; a pack may not redeclare a pair the core already claimed, and the duplicate is logged and dropped. A pack that adds no metric may ship `channels.yml` as `[]` to say so.

title: Packs · Code packs: adapters
text: `adapter.py` has `fetch(hc) -> (sensors, readings)`, the same contract as `app/sources.py`, and runs only as described under [How packs load](#how-packs-load). Dependencies and settings go in `pack.yaml`. `planetai packs` lists what is loaded and says when a dependency or a setting is missing, and `planetai packs install` adds the missing `env:` keys to `.env` and rebuilds the image once with every pack's `pip:` list. A pack that needs a key or a service must log once and return nothing when it is missing. `packs/earth-engine` is the worked example: a dependency, a credential, several remote datasets, and it idles until configured. `packs/make` is a code pack that stores places rather than numbers.

title: Packs · Scripts
text: Things you ask for rather than things that run on a schedule: ```bash planetai run # lists every script with its first line planetai run earth change --all # the land change for every consecutive year pair this node has cached planetai run nearby stations # every station in the ring, with the reason for each exclusion planetai run place gaps # a mapping brief: what is undrawn within the kilometre planetai run season window # every paired station, its week, its baseline, the step ``` They run inside the app container, where the dependencies are, with `PACK_OUT=/app/out`. `out/` is the one writable path, and what they write there is yours to send anywhere. Every `*.py` in a pack except `adapter.py` and `hooks.py` is listed, so a helper module shows up too (`place/satellite.py` does).

title: Packs · A dashboard section
text: Any pack, wild or core, can declare a section in its `pack.yaml`, as data. The node reads each readout's latest row and serves the section in `GET /issues` under `sections` (a core pack's section only once a row of it exists). The page draws it as a band in its stage on Now, with the pack's name beside the title, using its own readout cards and no code from the pack: ```yaml sections: - id: sg-air # unique on the page: lowercase letters, digits and hyphens stage: observe # observe · decide · act · measure title: { en: Singapore air, from NEA, id: Udara Singapura, dari NEA, es: Aire de Singapur, de NEA } order: 40 # optional, default 50 wall: true # optional: each reading is also a column on the wall readouts: - { metric: psi, sensor_id: nea-psi, unit: PSI, dp: 0, label: { en: NEA PSI, id: PSI NEA, es: PSI de NEA } } ``` A declared section draws readout cards only. A stack, a series or a row needs script, and script on this page is for core packs only: it reads the same browser storage the admin token is kept in, so a pack's own script would hold admin rights on every node that installed it. A core section registers one object with the page contract: ```js window.PAI.register({ id: 'meshtastic', // required, unique; the band's DOM id pack: 'meshtastic', // required stage: 'observe', // required: observe · decide · act · measure title: 'The mesh in this house', // required render(ctx) { … }, // render or lead is required; captions belong here, explanations do not order: 41, // within the stage, lower first (default 50) level: 'advanced', // default; 'simple' keeps it in simple mode on Historical and Network (simple on Now draws no sections) needs: ['H3.radio.mesh'], // dotted paths off window; absent → one honest line, never a blank learn: ['states'], // learn marks this section carries controls(ctx) { … }, // optional control strip wall(ctx) { … }, // what this section contributes to the wall notes(ctx) { … }, // [{ id, label, text }]: the explanations, gathered at the foot of the page }); ``` A section may not invent a fifth card kind (readout · stack · series · row), colour a state by hue, print a numeral without `data-num`, or put its explanation in its body. A scripted section lives inline in `app/static/dashboard.js`, because the node serves its static files from a fixed allowlist, so it comes with the pack's promotion to core. The page itself is on [Dashboard](dashboard.md).

title: Packs · Sharing one
text: Do not fork the node to write a pack for your city. Make a repository that is the pack folder, develop it in `packs/<id>` on your own node, and run `python3 tools/check_rules.py` from the node's folder. Say in the README where the thresholds come from and which place you wrote for: thresholds for Kuta Selatan are not thresholds for Barcelona. A source the pack reads has to be an entry in the registry first, so `sources:` can name it. To let other nodes find it, add one entry to `packs.json` in [fabcity/planetai-wild-packs](https://github.com/fabcity/planetai-wild-packs) by pull request.
