Its README lists the fields, anyone may be listed, and an entry is marked `listed` until a maintainer has read it (for a code pack, its adapter) and marks it `reviewed`. Any node then installs it with `planetai packs add <owner>/<repo>`. The same repository can host the folder for you if you would rather not keep a repository of your own. A pull request to the node's repository is for promotion to core. A reviewer asks that the pack is useful beyond the place it was written for, or is the reference for a pilot city; that its data is openly licensed and its README says under which licence; that it has offline tests registered in `tests/all`; and that a maintainer agrees to keep it. The issue a new domain declares is explained on [Issues](issues.md).

title: Packs · Packs nobody has written yet
text: Each of these would fill a gap the node has today. Take the one whose sensor you own and whose decision you face. | pack | what it would watch | Index cell | what it needs | |---|---|---|---| | classroom | CO₂ over 1,200 ppm for 20 minutes: open the windows | `Social\|Community` | a CO₂ sensor the node reads (the `airgradient` pack reads an AirGradient monitor's, see [Packs that ship](packs-reference.md#airgradient)) | | outage | grid up and down, as outage hours | `Economic\|Community` | a smart plug on the broker | | water | turbidity, TDS and tank level: is the well safe, will the tank last to the rain | `Environmental\|Community` | a DIY probe on an ESP32, over MQTT | | lab machines | hours run, jobs, material in and out | `Economic\|Community` | a fab lab's job log, from Fabman or a CSV | | open-data portals | the Socrata and ArcGIS portals of cities such as Barcelona and Boston | `Governance\|Region` | nothing but the portal | | noise | school-hours rules on sound levels | | a Smart Citizen kit, which already reports noise | Smaller ones, an afternoon each: tides, pollen, procurement latency from public tender data (TED, ChileCompra, LKPP), and a pack that is only messages translated into another language.

title: Packs · Where this leads
text: A pack reads what the node already holds. When the thing your place needs measured is not held yet, the next page is [the source registry](sources.md): what the network has filed as measurable at each pillar and scale, which of it any code reads, and which is waiting for somebody to write the adapter.

title: The report
text: The report is the node telling the household what the ground is doing, in their language, on a schedule. The node writes it itself, with SQL against its own tables, so a node with no model reachable anywhere still gets it. With the `make` pack on, it can also name the nearest workshop where somebody could make or fix something. `app/report.py` holds both halves: `bundle()`, every number the node has about the window, and `sheet()`, the report written from it.

title: The report · When
text: `REPORT_EVERY` takes 3, 4, 6, 8, 12 or 24. Each divides 24, so the rhythm does not walk round the clock, and anything else falls back to 6. `REPORT_ANCHOR` is the local hour it counts from (0 to 23). The defaults are 6 and 6: 06:00, 12:00, 18:00 and 00:00 where the node is. `planetai report every 12` and `planetai report at 7` change it without a restart, and so does the dashboard's Set up view. The rules loop checks once a minute. In the first twenty minutes of a due hour it writes the report, and the `reports` row for that local hour is the lock, so a container that restarts inside the window does not send twice. A report due inside quiet hours is written and stored with `held_quiet` and not sent; the next report to go out folds every held hour in and opens with "Overnight and this morning." A node that was off for a week reports the last two days (the window is capped at 48 hours).

title: The report · Read one now
text: 1. **Run `planetai report`.** The node writes a report at once and sends it. The terminal prints the text, then ` written by node, sent.`, and Telegram, when it is connected, receives the same text. `written by node` means the node wrote every sentence itself, from its own tables, with no model. With no admin token in `.env` it stops at `no ADMIN_TOKEN in .env; run planetai ui`. 2. **Run `planetai report last`.** It prints the last report's text and one line under it, `<date> <time> · <hours> hours · written by node`, with `· HELD for quiet hours, folded into the next one` when quiet hours kept it back. Before any report it prints `no report yet; the first one lands at the next due hour`. A report you ask for does not move the scheduled ones.

title: The report · The four parts
text: Plain text in `ALERT_LOCALE` (English, Bahasa Indonesia or Spanish), each part a sentence or two, an empty part left out, and written to stay under a hundred words. There is one sign, the headline's, and a line is always named with its owner and its unit, never as a bare number. 1. **The headline, in words.** Heat first, if an open act-level alert comes from the `heat` pack or the event engine has sent a heat event that is still open: "dangerously hot" only at `heat_danger` or a danger event (feels like 40 °C or more), otherwise "🌡️ It is hot inside." Else the worst indoor PM2.5 against 35 (unhealthy) and 15 (the clean line), said as unhealthy, middling or clean. Else that there is no sensor inside yet, so what follows is the district and not the rooms. No number in it. 2. **What happened, per room, with the local time.** Heat, at most two rooms: "In Kids and Living Room it has felt past this house's heat line, 35 °C feels-like, since 14:47." (an `unusual` event is "hotter than usual", never past the line). Then each act alert with a threshold, one sentence per room, at most two: "Kitchen went past the US EPA's unhealthy level, 35.5 µg/m³, at 15:00; it is back under now." or "…, and is still past it." The lines are the rules' own: the US EPA's unhealthy level (35.5), its level unhealthy for everyone (55.5), the WHO line (15). Then up to two rooms whose window was unusual: "Studio was more humid than usual.", "The air in Kitchen was dirtier than usual." Then one clause only the models know, if its rule is loaded and crossed: a heavy swell, or the European air model (CAMS) putting the district past the US EPA's unhealthy level. 3. **The one thing to do.** When the node knows one, [the nearest place to make or fix](#the-nearest-place-to-make-or-fix) comes first. Then a room still over its line, a sensor gone quiet, or the first failing health check, in the household's words ("A sensor has gone quiet: Kitchen."), never the admin's fix and never a source refusing (the dashboard's Running section names those). Or "Nothing needs doing before the next report." 4. **The invitation.** "Ask me anything about the air, the heat or the sea." Always last: the morning memory goes above it.

title: The report · The nearest place to make or fix
text: When the bundle holds a `facility` row, the third part opens with one line before the to-do, so a person reads what happened first and only then where somebody could act on it: ``` Nearest place to make or fix something: {lab}, {distance} km ({up to three capabilities}). ``` The distance reads `<0.1` for a node inside a lab, and the capabilities are in the report's language. The row comes from the `make` pack, which is off unless both `MAKE_ENABLED=1` and `PACKS_ALLOW_CODE=1` are set, and which stores only the labs within `MAKE_RADIUS_KM` (50) that publish coordinates. The same line is offered on the alerts in `GET /issues`, as `asks.where`. The line adds to the hundred words. > **Careful.** The Fab Lab Network directory the pack reads is not openly licensed: each lab keeps copyright in its > own record, and no data licence is published. Fab City Foundation's permission to read it covers the Foundation, > not each node's operator. Read [packs/make/README.md](../../packs/make/README.md) before turning it on, and leave > it off if that matters to you.

title: The report · Two numbers behind it
text: **Notability** is the window's mean for a sensor and metric against the mean of the same local hours on each of the previous seven days, in standard deviations of that baseline. It is null until three days exist, so a node in its first three days claims nothing. It decides which two places get a sentence in part 2, which is how the report can say "The air in Kitchen was dirtier than usual." without anyone reading a chart. **Trend** compares the second half of the window with the first, against a step per metric: 3 µg/m³ for PM2.5, half a degree for temperature, and 5% of the window's range for a metric with no step of its own.

title: The report · The bundle
text: Everything the sheet was written from, as one JSON document, SQL only, most of it run as the read-only role: | key | what it holds | |---|---| | `meta` | node, locale, local time, window, held hours | | `series` | per sensor and metric: min, max, mean, n, trend, notability, the usual value and how many baseline days | | `observations` | sea, weather, satellite air, place, land, with yesterday's value | | `now` | the `stats` view | | `alerts` | the alerts in the window | | `open_act` | unanswered act alerts of the last 24 hours, at most five | | `open_events` | the event engine's open act events that were sent, with their rooms (on `ALERT_ENGINE=events` only) | | `sensors_quiet` | the house's own sensors that have gone quiet, never a survey such as the things it keeps | | `rho` | ρ now and a week ago | | `previous` | the last sent report | | `cells` | the Index cells, with what changed | | `rules`, `health` | the loaded rules, the health checks | | `facility` | the nearest lab, or null | | `<pack>/<rule>` | the first row of every pack's `contributes: report` rule | On `ALERT_ENGINE=events`, `alerts` and `open_act` leave out the rows the replaced packs record without sending, so the report tells what reached the household. A contributor may not use a name the bundle owns (`RESERVED` in `app/report.py`); one that tries is skipped and logged. The bundle is trimmed to 64 kB by dropping the least notable series first. `GET /report/bundle?hours=` returns it behind the read-only or admin token, and the MCP tool `report_bundle` reads it too. Any number in a sentence about the node must come from here. No sentence of the report says ρ; a ρ sentence is proposed in `docs/SPEC_rho.md` and not built.

title: The report · A model in the path
text: This version ships without one, and the schema is ready for it. Every report row carries `sheet` (always the node's own text), `text` (equal to `sheet` until a model rewrites it), `depth` (`sheet` today; `brief`, `standard` and `deep` reserved), `rung` (`node` today; `local`, `remote` and `online` reserved) and `fallback_reason`, for a model's text that is refused because it invented a number, timed out, or had no agent. `REPORT_DEPTH` takes `auto`, `brief`, `standard` or `deep`, and changes nothing yet. When a model comes it is handed the bundle and the sheet, anything it writes is checked against the numbers in them before it goes out, and the sheet is what the node falls back to.

title: The report · Delivery
text: The report goes to Telegram with its own sign and no other, and to Home Assistant's *latest alert* entity. The mesh and Reticulum do not carry it. The first report sent each day that finds yesterday's diary entry written carries, in Telegram only, the house's memory, between the to-do and the invitation: yesterday's entry, last week's on a Monday, last month's on the 1st and last year's on 1 January, then each learning whose status changed that day (now holding, weakening or gone), in its own sentence. `LEARN_PUSH` sets it: `all` (the default), `week` (only the week, month and year) or `off`. The memory is never in the stored report, `/report/latest`, the bundle, Home Assistant or the mesh, which other people and machines can read. `reports.memory` says which report carried it, so a restart does not send it twice, and whatever does not fit in one Telegram message is left for `/learned`. | | | |---|---| | `GET /report/latest` | the last report, always with the same keys: `schema` (`report-v0`), `id, ts, due_local, window_hours, depth, rung, text, sent, held_quiet, fallback_reason`, and `note`, which is null when a report exists and "no report yet; the first one lands at the next due hour" when none does. Open at `SHARE_LEVEL=open` | | `GET /report/bundle?hours=` | what it was written from; read-only or admin token | | `POST /report/now` | write one now and send it; admin token. Written without a `due_local`, so the scheduled one still happens | | `planetai report` · `report last` · `report every N` · `report at H` · `report level act`, `warn` or `info` | the same from the command line; `level` sets `ALERT_LEVEL`, what may interrupt between reports | | `report_latest` · `report_now` · `report_bundle` | the same over MCP |

title: The report · The digest on the page
text: `GET /issues` carries a second summary, separate from the report: `digest`, four sentences, one per stage (observe, decide, act, measure), in English, Bahasa Indonesia and Spanish. It also carries `simple`, the paragraph simple mode draws on Now (the house's own stations and the nearest others, the oldest open alert, how the last 30 days of asking went), and `prompts`, the ask pane's questions, the first three of which it opens with. Every figure in them is one the page already draws further down, and the node writes them. On a node whose alert engine is `shadow` or `events` the open alerts they count leave out the heat and air alerts, because an event stands for them. The measure sentence reads "Of the {acts} alerts here that asked for something, {answered} have been answered, and the usual wait was {median} minutes." It is not ρ: it counts the Act stage's ledger, where an alert is answered once it has an `acted` or `measured` row, and ρ has its own window and its own query in `app/index.py`.

title: The report · Contributing to it from a pack
text: A rule with `contributes: report` and no message is never sent. Its first row lands in the bundle under the rule's id, where the sheet may read it and a model may quote from it. Five ship: | contributor | what it puts in the bundle | |---|---| | `insight/digest` | inside, outside, modelled, the day's mean and peak, the trend | | `nearby/alone` | a ring of fewer than two stations, or none within 10 km | | `forecast/ahead` | wind and rain for the next day | | `surface-heat/ground` | the ground's temperature in the node's cell at the newest clear Landsat pass, against the land around it, beside the house's own outdoor air at the same half hour (else the weather model's) | | `season/record` | this week's PM2.5 around the node against the usual: each Bali Air Dispatch station's last 7 days against its own preceding 60, the median of the differences, and the station count, whether or not it crossed a line | How to write one is on [Packs](packs.md).

title: The report · Where this leads
text: Between reports the node speaks only when a reading crosses a line: [alerts](alerts.md) is how it asks, and [channels](channels.md) is where the asking reaches people.

title: ρ: the loop closed
text: ρ (rho) is the share of the node's act-level asks (alerts and events it sent, and its children's alerts) that a person answered within 24 hours. It is the node's `Governance` cell in the Fab City Index, counted from the answers people give, each one a row in the `actions` table. Once the node has asked ([alerts](alerts.md)) and heard back ([channels](channels.md)), ρ and the numbers beside it say how often asking worked, how long the answer took, and whether the condition stopped afterwards.

title: ρ: the loop closed · The definition
text: Over the last 30 days: ``` ρ = act-level asks whose first acknowledged-or-acted answer came within 24 hours ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── act-level asks that were sent ``` with `median_minutes`, the median time from the ask to that first answer, among the ones answered within 24 hours. `index.rho()` computes both. An ask is one of three things: | ask | counted from | answered by | |---|---|---| | an act-level `alerts` row | its `ts` | an `acknowledged` or `acted` row in `actions` with its `alert_id` | | an act-level event the event engine sent | its first sent `open` or `escalate` message | an `acknowledged` or `acted` row with its `event_id` (Done or Not now, on Telegram or the dashboard) | | a child's act-level alert, pushed up to this node | its `raised_at` | the earlier of its `responded_at` and `acted_at` | Only what was sent is asked. On `ALERT_ENGINE=events` the event engine speaks for the heat and air-quality packs, and from its first sent message on, their `alerts` rows are written and never sent, so ρ leaves them out and counts the event once instead. Packs the engine does not replace still send through rules and count as alerts. On a `rules` or `shadow` node every act-level alert counts. A node with no children has an empty `events` table, so the third row adds nothing. ![ρ: of the act-level asks sent, the share that got an answer within 24 hours](img/rho.svg "The first acknowledged or acted answer stops the clock. The figures are an example.") > **Gap in v0.90.0.** A child pushes every `alerts` row to its parent, the unsent ones included, and none of its > events. A parent's pooled ρ therefore counts a child on `ALERT_ENGINE=events` the old way. `GET /rho` on node #1, an events node: ```json {"window_days": 30, "days_ago": 0, "alerts_act": 157, "acted": 13, "rho": 0.083, "median_minutes": 73, "funnel": {"stages": {"asked": 157, "acknowledged": 2, "acted": 13, "measured": 6}, "latency_minutes": {"acknowledged": null, "acted": 438, "measured": null}, "measured_derived": true, "measured_window_minutes": 2880, "self_only": true}} ``` Of 157 asks in 30 days, 13 were answered within 24 hours, and among those 13 the median answer came 73 minutes after the ask. `rho` and `median_minutes` are `null` when there is nothing to divide. `days_ago` moves the whole window back; the report's bundle uses 7 to carry what ρ was a week ago. `planetai status` and `planetai act` print ρ, and the `status` MCP tool carries it. The dashboard's *Whether it worked* section draws it as "{closed} of {total} alerts answered · median {n} min", and the classic wall as its row of rings. The doors' Wall does not show it.

title: ρ: the loop closed · Read it on your node
text: 1. **Run `planetai status`.** Its `rho` line reads, for example, `rho 0.083 (13/157 act-level alerts answered, 30d)`. Before the first act-level ask it reads `rho not yet measured (0/0 act-level alerts answered, 30d)`. 2. **Ask the node for the whole record.** `curl http://<node>:8080/rho` (at `SHARE_LEVEL=open`, or with `-H "Authorization: Bearer <token>"` and any of the node's tokens) returns the document above. `alerts_act` and `acted` are the two counts the `status` line divides. 3. **Close one loop and look again.** `planetai act <id> "<what you did>"` ends with `rho is now <ρ> (<acted>/<alerts_act> alerts answered, median <n> min)`. If the alert was raised less than 24 hours ago and nobody had answered it yet, `acted` has gone up by one, and so has the node's `Governance` cell.

title: ρ: the loop closed · Stages
text: `actions.stage` is one of six: | stage | meaning | written by | in ρ | |---|---|---|---| | `acknowledged` | somebody saw it | `POST /actions`, the bot's Not now | yes | | `decided` | somebody said what would be done | the dashboard's Decide form, `POST /actions` | no | | `acted` | somebody did the thing | the dashboard's *I did this* and Done, `planetai act`, `/act` on Telegram, `act <id>` over LXMF, the MCP `act` tool, `POST /actions` | yes | | `measured` | the condition stopped | derived in the funnel (below); `POST /actions` refuses it | no | | `settings` | a setting was changed, with no alert | the node, on `PUT /settings` | no | | `dismissed` | *Doesn't fit*, said of an event's advice | `POST /actions` with an `event_id` | no | An event's three answers (`acted`, `acknowledged`, `dismissed`) carry an `event_id` and no `alert_id`. ρ and the funnel count them; `GET /effect` joins `actions` to `alerts` on `alert_id`, so no event's answer is in it. See [Alerts](alerts.md#the-event-engine). For ρ, `acknowledged` and `acted` both count as an answer. On the dashboard only `acted` and `measured` close an alert. There is no cap of one action per alert; the clock stops at the first answer. A `decided` row counts in neither ρ nor the funnel. The Act stage's ledger (*What was decided, and by whom*) marks an act that had a decision recorded against the same alert beforehand as *decided first*. `DECISION_REQUIRED` is under [Answering an alert](alerts.md#answering-an-alert).

title: ρ: the loop closed · The funnel
text: `GET /rho` carries `funnel`: this node's own asks of the same 30 days, counted at four stages (asked, acknowledged, acted, measured), with the median minutes between consecutive stages. Its `acted` is the literal stage, so it will not match ρ's `acted`, which also counts an acknowledgement. It leaves out the children, whose `events` rows carry no stages (`self_only: true`), and it leaves out the unsent rows the same way ρ does. `measured` is derived from silence: an alert with an `acted` row, whose rule the node still evaluates, and which that rule did not raise again on the same sensor for `MEASURED_WINDOW_MIN` (2880 minutes, 48 hours) after the act. The window is longer than every act-level rule's cooldown, so silence across it means the condition stopped being true. That says whether, never when, so `latency_minutes.measured` is always `null`. A retired rule is left out, because a rule that can never fire again is silent whatever happened. An event has no derived `measured`; only a posted row would count for it.

title: ρ: the loop closed · What worked, per rule
text: `GET /effect` asks the same question per rule over the node's whole record (365 days by default): how many acts there were (`acted`) and how many were followed by the condition stopping (`cleared`, derived as `measured` is). A rule that declares `watch: {metric, over}` also gets `measured` (acts after which that sensor's hourly mean came back under the line), `already` (acts made when it was already back), and the median `hours` to recovery. Four rules declare one: `air-quality/indoor_pm25_high` (`pm25` over 35.5), `air-quality/outdoor_pm25_high` (`pm25` over 55.5), `heat/heat_stress_now` (`apparent`, the feels-like temperature, over 35) and `heat/heat_danger` (over 40). Every other rule answers `hours: null`, because it fires on a relation such as inside worse than outside, where there is no line to come back under. The dashboard draws it as *Which of these worked*. It is elapsed time, not an effect. A window opened at 21:00 and air that cleared at 03:00 may be the window or may be the night, and the node cannot tell.

title: ρ: the loop closed · What ρ does not measure
text: ρ counts answers, it says nothing about the place. The funnel's `measured` and `GET /effect` are the node's evidence about the place, and both say that a condition stopped, never that the act stopped it. A second number read from the place's own recovery (ρ_observed, with a `recovery:` block in the rules) is proposed in `docs/SPEC_rho.md` and not built: no rule carries a `recovery:` block, and `rho()` still counts `acknowledged` as an answer, which the spec would change.

title: ρ: the loop closed · Where it goes
text: - **The Index.** `GET /cells` adds `Governance|<Scale>` with ρ as its value once there has been any act-level ask in 30 days: `partial` until five have been answered, `live` from then. - **A parent.** Every hour the node posts its alerts of the last 36 hours to the parent's `/events` as timestamps only (`raised_at`, `responded_at`, `acted_at`, `measured_at`, the rule, the level, the pack), never the text, the actor, the sensor or a ratio. `measured_at` is filled only from a posted `measured` row, so a parent receives `null` there. The parent computes ρ under its own definition. - **The export.** The daily CC BY 4.0 export carries `rho` as `index.rho()` returns it when the export is written, the rolling 30-day figure. - **The report.** The bundle carries ρ now and a week ago; no sentence of the report says it.

title: ρ: the loop closed · Recording an action
text: From another machine `POST /actions` needs `ACT_TOKEN` or `ADMIN_TOKEN`; from loopback (the node's own MCP tools, a shell in the container) it needs none. A browser is never loopback. The body is `{"alert_id": 12, "stage": "acted", "actor": "made", "note": "closed the windows"}`, or `event_id` in place of `alert_id` for an event. `actor` is cut at 80 characters and `note` at 500, and an unknown alert or event is a 404. | way in | actor | when no note is given | |---|---|---| | the dashboard's *I did this* | the name typed in the form | the form will not post; it needs the act or admin token Set up holds | | `planetai act <id> [note]` | `$(whoami)` | writes `acted` | | Telegram `/act <id> <words>` | `<AGENT_NAME>/telegram` | writes nothing; the bot asks "What did you do about it?" | | the MCP `act` tool | its `agent` argument | refuses, and refuses placeholders such as `acted`, `done` or `ok` | | `act <id> [note]` over LXMF | `lxmf:<hash>` | writes `acted (via reticulum)` | The note should be what the person said. The MCP tool and the Telegram bot will not write a row without one, the terminal and the radio fill in a placeholder, and `POST /actions` takes any note. `GET /actions` lists every answer with its stage, actor and note, and answers only a token or the machine itself. `planetai snapshot` leaves the notes out of the file it writes. The invariants ρ depends on are on the [federation](federation.md) page: peers never roll up and never drive an alert, the note on an action and the chat ids never leave the node at any sharing level, state is never upgraded by aggregation, and exactly one node per pilot writes to the Index's spine.

title: ρ: the loop closed · Where this leads
text: The node now senses, asks, hears back and measures. Extend it with [packs](packs.md), which add rules, cells and sources for a domain, and the [source registry](sources.md). [Sharing](sharing.md) and [federation](federation.md) are how ρ travels up to a district, as timestamps and nothing else.

title: Data schema
text: Everything the node knows sits in one Postgres database, `planetai`, on the machine itself. A pack's rules and cells are SQL written against the tables and views on this page, and a person debugging a node at 9 pm reads the same ones with `psql`. The raw readings live in `readings` and stay here: "No raw readings leave the instance that recorded them" (ARCHITECTURE.md). What goes up to a parent is `readings_1h`, the hourly means, and the timestamps in `alerts` and `actions`. `init.sql` is the whole schema, and it is written to be run twice: `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`, `ALTER TABLE … ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS`, and `DROP VIEW` then `CREATE VIEW`. Postgres runs it on its own only when the data volume is first created, so `update.sh` applies the same file to the existing database on every update, and `planetai restore` applies it after a restore. There are no other migration files. Schema changes are additive by rule (SPEC §5): no dropped columns, no renames, no destructive migrations, which is what makes a rollback a `git checkout <tag>` and a restart instead of a restore. The one column ever dropped is `events.cleared_at`, which nothing had written. `schema_version` records where a node is, and `/health` reports it. `init.sql` holds 18 tables, 4 views, 1 materialized view, 1 trigger and 1 role, and the `place` pack adds four tables of its own.

title: Data schema · Tables
text: ### `sensors` One row per thing that produces readings, and per place the node was told about. | column | type | meaning | |---|---|---| | `sensor_id` | text, primary key | `<source>-<upstream id>`: `sc-19880`, `bad-pa-46949`; a child's as `<child>/<sensor_id>`; a fab lab's as `lab-<slug>`. Never reassigned | | `source` | text | the adapter that wrote it, for example `smartcitizen`, `airgradient`, `purpleair`, `meshtastic`, `open-meteo`, `open-meteo-cams`, `nasa-power`, `ckan`, `child` (a child's push), `contributor` (a `POST /readings` that names no source), `things`, or a pack's (`fablabs-io` for `make`, `baliairdispatch` for `bali-air-dispatch`) | | `name` | text | the place, as the person named it: the `room` when the household set one, else the platform's name | | `room` | text | the household's word for where the sensor is, set with `PATCH /sensors/{sid}`; a trigger makes it the `name` whatever writes the row | | `source_name` | text | the platform's own name, kept while a `room` stands in for it | | `lat`, `lon` | double | position; rounded before it leaves for a reader without a token | | `indoor` | bool | measures a room; never in an ambient average | | `local` | bool | the person's own **and** within `LOCAL_RADIUS_M` of the node | | `kind` | text | `sensor` · `portal` · `model` · `survey` · `child` · `peer` · `facility`, as `init.sql` lists them; the `place` pack also writes `map` | | `scale` | text | `community` · `city` · `region` · `bioregion` · `planet` | | `cadence` | text | ISO 8601 duration: `PT5M`, `PT1H`, `P1D`, `P30D`, `P1Y` | | `meta` | jsonb | free-form. A reader of `/sensors` without a token gets only `licence`, `attribution`, `model`, `dataset`, `network`, `note`, `corrected`, and for a `facility` row ten more keys that describe the lab | | `custody` | bool, generated | `kind = 'child' OR (local AND kind <> 'peer')`. The only thing a cell may count | The one `survey` row is `things:<node>`, the counts of the things a home keeps. Nothing writes `peer`; it is named in `init.sql` and in the `custody` expression. A facility has no readings. `kind = 'facility'` is a place with a name and a point, and the `make` pack writes it: with `MAKE_ENABLED=1` it stores each active lab within `MAKE_RADIUS_KM` as one row, `sensor_id` `lab-<slug>`, `source` `fablabs-io`, `local` false, `scale` `community`, `cadence` `P30D`. Its `meta` holds `slug`, `capabilities`, `kind_name`, `city`, `country_code`, `distance_km`, `url`, `registry_slug`, `snapshot`, `fetched` and `attribution`. No `readings` row is written for it, so it is in neither `stats` nor `observations`; `/issues` reads it straight from `sensors`. Because `local` is false, `custody` is false, and a fab lab can never make an Index cell say `live`. ### `readings` | column | type | | |---|---|---| | `ts` | timestamptz | a UTC instant | | `sensor_id` | text → `sensors` | | | `metric` | text | lowercase, no unit in the name | | `value` | double | | Unique on `(sensor_id, metric, ts)`, so polling twice is harmless; indexed `(sensor_id, metric, ts desc)` and on `ts` alone. ### `alerts` | column | | | |---|---|---| | `id` | bigserial | the number a person answers | | `ts` | timestamptz | when the rule fired | | `rule_id` | text | `<pack>/<id>`, or a bare core id | | `sensor_id` | text | the row's sensor, or `node` | | `level` | text | `info` · `warn` · `act` | | `text` | text | the filled message | | `event_id` | bigint → `alert_events.id` | the event the alert fed. Nothing writes it yet, so it is null on every row | Indexed `(rule_id, sensor_id, ts desc)` for the cooldown check. An alert never clears, it only cools down; an [alert event](#alert-events) is the row that opens and clears. ### `actions` The ρ instrument: what happened after an alert, one row per answer. | column | | | |---|---|---| | `ts` | timestamptz | | | `alert_id` | bigint → `alerts.id` | null for `settings` rows and for the answers to an alert event | | `event_id` | bigint → `alert_events.id` | set only on an answer to an event, from `POST /actions` with an `event_id`; null on every other row | | `stage` | text | checked: `acknowledged` · `acted` · `measured` · `settings` · `decided` · `dismissed` | | `actor` | text | who: the name typed on the dashboard, the login name from `planetai act`, `lxmf:<hash>` from the radio bridge, an agent's name, or the `X-Agent` of a settings change | | `note` | text | in the person's words | The six stages do different things, and two of them are never posted by a person. | stage | written by | what it moves | |---|---|---| | `acknowledged` | `POST /actions` | ρ, and `/alerts.acted_at` | | `acted` | `POST /actions` | ρ, `acted_at`, and closes the alert | | `decided` | `POST /actions` | Nothing. It records that somebody said what they would do: it is not in ρ or the funnel and closes no alert | | `dismissed` | `POST /actions` with an `event_id`, never with an `alert_id` | Nothing. It is *Doesn't fit*, said of an alert event's advice | | `measured` | nothing | `POST /actions` refuses it. The node derives `measured` from an `acted` alert whose rule stayed silent on the same sensor for 2880 minutes; see [ρ](rho.md). A `measured` row already in the table still counts | | `settings` | `PUT /settings`, `planetai config set`, the `settings_set` tool | Nothing in ρ; it records who changed which keys | An `acknowledged` or `acted` row with an `event_id` answers an alert event. On `ALERT_ENGINE=events`, ρ and its funnel count each event the engine sent at act level once, answered by such a row; the rows of the packs the engine replaced are left out from its first sent message on. `GET /effect` and the push to a parent read only rows with an `alert_id`. With `DECISION_REQUIRED=1`, `POST /actions` refuses an `acted` row for an alert that has no `decided` row yet. The table itself does not enforce that. ### `reports` | column | | | |---|---|---| | `id`, `ts` | | | | `due_local` | timestamptz | the local due hour; the row is the scheduler's lock. Null for `POST /report/now` | | `window_hours` | int | | | `depth` | text | `sheet` on every row; `brief` · `standard` · `deep` are reserved | | `rung` | text | `node` on every row; `local` · `remote` · `online` are reserved | | `text` | text | what was sent. Both writers put the sheet here, so it equals `sheet` | | `sheet` | text | the node's own six parts, always | | `sent`, `held_quiet` | bool | a report due in quiet hours is written with `sent` false and `held_quiet` true, and folded into the next | | `fallback_reason` | text | why `text` is the sheet and not a model's. Nothing writes it yet | | `cells` | jsonb | the Index cells at the time of the report | | `memory` | bool | it carried the morning memory on Telegram; one report a day does | ### `events` ρ from below: one row per child alert, pushed hourly by children to `POST /events`. | column | | | |---|---|---| | `child`, `alert_id` | text, primary key together | | | `rule`, `level`, `kind`, `scale` | text | `kind` is the pack prefix | | `raised_at`, `responded_at`, `acted_at`, `measured_at` | timestamptz | timestamps only: no text, no actor, no sensor | | `received_at` | timestamptz | | `measured_at` is null in practice: a child fills it from posted `measured` rows, and `POST /actions` does not take one. The parent's funnel in `/rho` is computed from its own alerts only, and says so with `self_only: true`. ### `alert_events` The alert-event engine's stories ([Alerts](alerts.md#the-event-engine)): one row per issue per house, from the first candidate over its line to the all-clear. Written only under `ALERT_ENGINE=shadow` or `events`, and empty under `rules`. It is called `alert_events` because `events` is the parent's ledger above. | column | | | |---|---|---| | `id` | bigserial | | | `issue`, `kind`, `level` | text | the issue (`heat`, `air`), the highest kind seen (`ahead` · `unusual` · `spike` · `sustained` · `danger`), the highest level | | `opened_at`, `last_seen_at`, `last_sent_at`, `cleared_at` | timestamptz | `cleared_at` is null while the event is open; an open event clears after 30 minutes with no candidate | | `peak` | double | the highest value seen | | `rooms`, `places` | text[] | the sensors' names, and where each was (`inside`, `outside`) | | `ever_sent` | bool | whether any message for it went out; an all-clear is sent only if so | | `action_id` | text | the action the last message carried | | `told_kind`, `told_peak`, `told_level`, `told_held`, `last_emitted_at` | | what the last message said, sent or held, so a restart does not forget where the escalation was | ### `event_messages` Every message the engine decided, sent or held. | column | | | |---|---|---| | `id`, `ts` | | | | `event_id` | bigint → `alert_events.id` | | | `reason` | text | checked: `open` · `escalate` · `clear` | | `kind` | text | the event's kind when this was decided; `danger` is never counted against the daily ceiling | | `sent` | bool | in `shadow`, what would have been sent | | `held` | text | why not: `quiet` · `ceiling` · `level`; null when sent | | `mode` | text | `shadow` or `events` | | `text` | text | the message as rendered, or null when it could not be | | `action_id` | text | the action it carried; null for an all-clear or when none was chosen | ### `channel_roles` What each `(source, metric)` is, written at every start from `config/channels.yml` and every pack's `channels.yml`: `role` (`ambient` · `enclosure` · `device_health` · `derived` · `index` · `private`), `comparable`, `unit`, `reference` and `declared_by`. A `private` reading is used on the page, by rules and by cells, and never in the export, a parent's aggregates, the report bundle or an agent's read. ### `settings` `key`, `value`, `updated_at`: the runtime overlay over `.env`, written from Set up, `planetai config set`, `PUT /settings` and the `settings_set` tool. The rules' role cannot read it, and its rows are left out of every dump, so a saved token never travels. ### `schema_version` `version`, `applied_at`; one row per schema step: 0.4, 0.14, 0.20 to 0.23, 0.50 to 0.52, and 0.54 to 0.61. There is no 0.53 row; the alert-event tables are created without one. An up-to-date node reports `0.61` at `/health`. ### `release_notices` `version`, `told_at`: one row per release the node has told its household about, so a restart or the hourly re-check never sends "a new version is out" twice for the same one (`UPDATE_CHECK`). Written by `check_release()` in `app/main.py`; nothing else reads it. ### `captures` The pictures a household keeps ([`docs/SPEC_eyes.md`](../SPEC_eyes.md)): `id`, `ts` (when it was taken), `received_at`, `kind` (`microscope` · `phone` · `camera` · `drone` · `balloon`), `cell` (H3 res 10), `lat` and `lon` (the exact point, or null), `outside` and `at_home` (both computed once on arrival), `actor`, `note`, `file` (a name inside `CAPTURES_DIR`, never a path), `sha256` (unique), `bytes`, `mime`, `meta` (the household's key: value lines) and `analysis` (what the image model found, null until described). Written by `/captures`, the eyes pack's routes. The file is in `CAPTURES_DIR`, never in the database. Revoked from `planetai_ro`, and in no export, aggregate or push. ### `household` Who is in the house ([`docs/SPEC_learn.md`](../SPEC_learn.md)): one row (`id` = 1), `people` (yes or no for `older`, `under5`, `lungs`, `pregnant`, `outdoor`) and `updated_at`. Written only by `PUT /household`. Revoked from `planetai_ro`, and named by no export, push or report. ### `digests` The node's diary: `scale` (`day` · `week` · `month` · `year`) and `period_start` (the primary key together), `label`, `text`, `numbers`, `written_at`, and `tsv`, a generated full-text vector of label and text with a GIN index. `check_learn()` writes them in the first hour of each local day, for every completed period not yet kept, oldest first; `numbers.v` says which version wrote a row, and a row written by an older version is written again once. Never deleted. Revoked from `planetai_ro`, and named by no export, push or report. ### `learnings` What the node learned: `kind` and `key` (the primary key together), `issue`, `metric`, `status` (`too_early` · `holding` · `weakening` · `gone`), `statement`, `numbers`, `n`, `scope` (`house` · `place`), `first_seen`, `checked_at`, and `status_since`, the local day its status last changed, which the morning memory reads to name what changed that day. `check_learn()` writes them once a day; a row is replaced, never deleted. Revoked from `planetai_ro`, and named by no export, push or report. ### `things` What a home keeps ([`docs/SPEC_inventory.md`](../SPEC_inventory.md)): `id`, `added_at`, `class`, `name`, `count`, `used` (`weekly` · `monthly` · `yearly` · `never`), `condition` (`works` · `needs_repair` · `broken`), `offer` (`no` · `lend` · `give`), `capture_id` and `note`. Written by `/things`, the things pack's routes. Revoked from `planetai_ro`, so no pack SQL reads it, and named by no export or push. Its counts per class reach `readings` as the private `stock.<class>`, `idle.<class>` and `repair.<class>`. ### `readings_1h_done` The finished hours behind the `readings_1h` view: `bucket, sensor_id, metric, mean, min, max, n`, one row per sensor, metric and hour. The app fills it from `readings`, the last 26 hours every hour and the whole table on start and once a day. Read `readings_1h`, never this table: the view adds the hours this table has not got to yet. ### Pack tables The `place` pack creates `place_features` (OpenStreetMap features with a PostGIS geometry), `place_runs`, `place_yearly` and `place_buildings_sat` (Open Buildings). Tables a pack creates inherit the read-only role's `SELECT` through default privileges.

title: Data schema · Views
text: | view | rows | columns | |---|---|---| | `readings_1h` | hourly means over all readings: the finished hours from `readings_1h_done`, and the rest grouped live from where that table ends, so it is complete even when the table is behind | `bucket, sensor_id, metric, mean, min, max, n` | | `stats` | one per (sensor, metric), last 24 h, `kind='sensor'` only | `sensor_id, metric, indoor, local, kind, scale, lat, lon, name, last, last_ts, silent_minutes, mean_15m, mean_1h, mean_24h` | | `observations` | the latest row per (sensor, metric) for `kind <> 'sensor'` | `sensor_id, metric, value, ts, name, kind, scale, local, cadence, meta` | | `recent_15m` | quarter-hour means of the last 24 h, `kind='sensor'` only, with `apparent` (the no-wind indoor feels-like) derived wherever `temp` and `humidity` share a bucket | `bucket, sensor_id, metric, mean` | | `usual_by_hour` (materialized) | each room's own normal for each local hour, from the fourteen complete local days before today, for `temp`, `humidity`, `pm25` and `apparent` | `sensor_id, metric, hour, median, p75, p90, n` | A rule with a `kind:` reads `recent_15m` and `usual_by_hour`, so it can ask "for how long" and "against what usual" without rebuilding either from raw readings every minute. `GET /issues` reads `usual_by_hour` too, for each issue's `usual`. `usual_by_hour` is created empty, and the app refreshes it at start and hourly in `NODE_TZ`; a rule that reads it before the first refresh fails, is logged, and runs again a minute later. Sensors land in `stats`. Slow sources (portals, models, maps) land in `observations`, which keeps the latest row per source per metric forever, so a retired metric must not be read as this year's answer. A facility lands in neither, because it has no readings.

title: Data schema · The read-only role
text: `planetai_ro` is `NOLOGIN`, has `SELECT` on every table except `settings`, `captures`, `things`, `learnings`, `digests` and `household`, and writes nothing. Every rule and every cell runs as it, one statement at a time with `SET LOCAL ROLE`, so a rule cannot read a token into an alert text or change a row. Grafana's login, `planetai_grafana`, is a member of it, made by the `grafana-role` container and not by `init.sql` ([Grafana](grafana.md)).

title: Data schema · Time and place inside the database
text: The session time zone is `NODE_TZ`, so `date_trunc('day', ts)` and `extract(hour from ts)` mean the household's day and hour; readings themselves are UTC instants. The node's position is available to SQL as `current_setting('planetai.lat')` and `current_setting('planetai.lon')`. The app sets both on every connection it opens. A `psql` session does not go through the app, so there an hour-of-day query answers in the database's own time zone and `planetai.lat` is not set.

title: Data schema · The database image
text: The `db` service runs `imresamu/postgis:16-3.4-alpine`, Postgres 16 with PostGIS 3.4, which publishes `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64` under the same tag. It stays on Alpine because an existing node's data directory was created by musl: opened with a glibc build, the node starts and its text indexes fail an integrity check, with no warning from Postgres. Postgres is published on `127.0.0.1:5432` only. [ARM64.md](../ARM64.md) has the arm64 detail.

title: Data schema · Backups and restore
text: `backup.sh` runs nightly at 03:17 from cron, or on demand with `planetai backup`. 1. It refuses a `BACKUP_DIR` under `/Volumes`, `/mnt` or `/media` that is not mounted, instead of creating a local folder with the NAS's name. 2. It runs `pg_dump` with the `settings` table's rows left out (the table stays in the dump, empty), gzips it to `<node>-<date>.sql.gz`, and keeps it only if it is a valid gzip holding a `readings` table. 3. It deletes dumps older than `BACKUP_KEEP` days (default 30). 4. It writes yesterday's `/export` to `exports/<node>/YYYY-MM-DD.json` when `EXPORT_ENABLED=1` (the default), and adds it to IPFS when `IPFS_PUBLISH=1`. 5. It copies the dumps and exports to `BACKUP_REMOTE` with rclone, if that is set. 6. It writes the time to `LAST_OK` in `BACKUP_DIR`. `planetai restore <dump>` asks you to type the node's name, takes a safety backup with `backup.sh`, stops the app, drops and recreates the database, restores the dump, re-applies `init.sql` and starts the app. It prints the number of readings when it is done. The dump carries no settings rows, so a restored node runs on `.env` until Set up is saved again, and a Telegram bot connected from the dashboard needs `planetai telegram` once more. The database stays on a local disk. SMB and NFS do not honour `fsync` and file locking, and a mount path that is not mounted becomes an empty local folder with the NAS's name. Backups are how the data reaches a NAS, and [Storage](storage.md) says where the copies go.

title: Data schema · Where this leads
text: The rows here reach screens and other nodes through the [API](api.md). A child's hourly push sends `readings_1h` to its parent's `POST /aggregates`, and the timestamps of `alerts` and `actions` to `POST /events`. [Federation](federation.md) is the page for pointing a child at a parent.

title: Sensors and sources
text: This page connects the things that measure your place to the node. Once a sensor of yours is polled, the rules have a room to fire on, and its hourly means can count toward this place's cell in the Fab City Index. Whether they count is decided by two fields on the sensor's row, `local` and `custody`. What the node knows before any sensor exists is on [Before a sensor](before-a-sensor.md).

title: Sensors and sources · Connect a sensor
text: The steps use a Smart Citizen kit, the one sensor the node polls with nothing to install (the `smartcitizen` pack, on as soon as a kit is set). The same checks work for any source on this page. 1. **Tell the node which kit is yours.** `planetai config set SC_DEVICES 19880` (your kit's id), or `SC_USER=<account>` to read every kit on an account. Set up → Sources on the dashboard sets the same keys. The terminal answers `SC_DEVICES is now 19880, on this node, within 20 s`, and from the next poll on the node treats the kit as yours. 2. **Wait one poll.** Polls run every `POLL_SECONDS` (300 by default). `planetai logs` shows a line `smartcitizen: <n> sensors, <n> readings`. A source that fails logs `source smartcitizen failed: …` and the others carry on. Polling twice never stores a reading twice. 3. **Check that it is yours and here.** `planetai sensors` prints one line per sensor: id, `kind`, `yours` or `reference`, `indoor` or `outdoor`, name. `yours` means `local`: the adapter claimed the kit and it stands within `LOCAL_RADIUS_M` (500 m) of the node. A kit on your account 1.2 km away prints `reference`, because it is not this node's measurement of this place. 4. **Check that it may be counted.** `planetai sensors --json` carries `"custody": true` on the same row. Every cell's claim to `live` depends on that field. 5. **Watch it become a cell.** `planetai cells` prints `Environmental|Community` with a value, a state and the unit `µg/m³ PM2.5 (24h mean, sensors in this node's custody)`. The state is `partial` until the node holds 12 hourly buckets from sensors in its custody in the last 24 hours and enough of those sensors (one on a community node with no children, two otherwise), and `live` after that. That row is what a parent node and the Index read. The readings under it never leave the machine. If step 3 says `outdoor` for a kit that is inside, fix it on the Smart Citizen platform. The adapter takes `indoor` from each kit's own `exposure`, and every air rule depends on it.

title: Sensors and sources · Who may be counted
text: `local` is two facts at once. The adapter says whether a sensor is yours, and the node checks whether it is here: `sources.stamp_local` sets `local` to false for any claimed sensor farther than `LOCAL_RADIUS_M` from the node. It only ever narrows. A sensor no adapter claimed never becomes local, whatever its coordinates. A claimed sensor with no coordinates (a radio reaching the node through your own gateway, a purifier on the LAN) stays local, because there is no distance to measure. A node with no coordinates of its own leaves every claim alone. `custody` is a generated column, `kind = 'child' OR (local AND kind <> 'peer')`. No adapter writes it, so it cannot disagree with `local` and `kind`. A child node's hourly means are in custody. A model point, a portal, somebody else's station across the street, a peer's sensor and a fab lab are not, and none of them can make a cell say `live`. A node that aggregates children needs in-custody sensors from at least two children before a cell may say `live`. [Concepts](concepts.md) has the rest of the vocabulary.

title: Sensors and sources · What ships
text: The poll loop asks `sources.enabled()` which adapters to run: the core ones, then every code pack's adapter. Code packs run only with `PACKS_ALLOW_CODE=1`, which ships as `0`. The exception is an official pack that names its own switch: it runs when that switch is on. | source | turned on by | `kind` | `local` | what it reads | |---|---|---|---|---| | Smart Citizen | `SC_DEVICES=19880,…` or `SC_USER=name` (every kit on the account; `SC_EXCLUDE` drops some) | `sensor` | yes, then narrowed by `LOCAL_RADIUS_M` | The public API, no key. Metrics are mapped by measurement name, so SCK 2.1 and 2.3 both work. `indoor` comes from each kit's own `exposure`. No humidity correction: the Seeed HM-3301 is not a Plantower, and the EPA correction was not derived for it. | | Open-Meteo and CAMS | `OPENMETEO_ENABLED=1` (default) | `model` | never | Weather now at the node's coordinates (core), and PM2.5, PM10, O₃, NO₂, dust and UV from the Copernicus model at 11 km, as `cams-point` (the `air-quality` pack, on the same key). Free, no key, anywhere. Never in an ambient average. | | NASA POWER | the first-start bootstrap (`BOOTSTRAP=1`) | `model` | never | Forty years of monthly temperature, humidity and rain normals, as `power-point`. | | CKAN portals | `CKAN_PORTALS=slug=url,…` (five of the six presets name one; `delhi` leaves it blank) | `portal` | never | A portal's upkeep (datasets in total, the share touched in 90 days) for the `open-data-health` pack's `Governance\|City` cell. Scale from `CKAN_SCALE` (`city`). | | Meshtastic radios | `MQTT_HOST` (set by `planetai meshtastic`) | `sensor` | yes | Telemetry from radios through the gateway, on `msh/#`, each reading filed under the radio that measured it. `MESH_INDOOR_NODES=!id,!id` marks the indoor ones. A radio's own temperature, humidity and pressure are its box, not the street. [Radios](radios.md) has the setup and the metrics. The parser also reads a Smart Citizen Kit's `readings/raw`, but a kit cannot send a password and this broker refuses anonymous clients, so kits stay on the cloud path. PM2.5 gets the EPA 2021 correction and the raw value is kept as `pm25_raw`; PurpleAir averages its two Plantower channels first, and stores `channel_disagreement` when they drift apart, because one laser is failing. `SENSOR_INDOOR=1` marks both kinds as indoors.
