title: Sensors and sources · Channel roles
text: One metric means different things from different devices. `config/channels.yml`, and a pack's own `channels.yml`, declare what each `(source, metric)` is, and the node writes the declarations to `channel_roles` at every start. | role | meaning | examples | |---|---|---| | `ambient` | the air, water or land at a place; comparable between sensors there | Smart Citizen `pm25`, `temp`, `noise`; Bali Air Dispatch `pm25`; a radio's `pm25`; a Xiaomi purifier's `pm25`, `temp`, `humidity` | | `enclosure` | the inside of the instrument's own box; never averaged as ambient | a radio's `temp`, `humidity`, `pressure`, `gas_resistance`: a BME680 sealed in a radio reports the box | | `device_health` | the instrument talking about itself | `battery_pct`, `battery_v`, `lora_util_pct`, `lora_channel_pct`, a purifier's `filter_life` | | `derived` | computed by the node from other readings | `open-meteo-cams` `pm25_model`; every `fc_*` forecast metric | | `index` | a vendor's own composite, never pooled with anyone else's | `aqi`, `bme_iaq`, `eco2`, `tvoc_index`, `nox_index` | | `private` | the house's own. The page, rules and cells use it. It stays out of the daily export, a parent's aggregates, the report bundle and every agent's read; `/readings`, `/history`, `/series` and `/sparks` give it to the admin token only, and readouts such as `/stats` to the admin or act token or this machine | a household's inventory counts | `comparable` says whether two sensors' values of a metric may be compared (`pm25_raw` may not). `reference` names the sensing element (`plantower`, `sc`, `bme680`). A role is set for a source and metric pair, so a node whose hardware differs from an adapter's usual shape cannot override it for one device.

title: Sensors and sources · Rules the node inherits
text: Several of these come from Bali Air Dispatch's methodology. 1. **Indoor sensors measure a room.** Never in an ambient average. 2. **Silence is a value that stops changing.** `stats` has `silent_minutes`, which is true per kit and false per channel. Smart Citizen's per-reading timestamp is empty on the kits node #1 reads, so the adapter stamps every channel with one kit-level time at each poll. A channel that has stopped producing new values still gets a fresh timestamp, and its frozen value is stored again under it. That pulls the 24-hour mean toward the frozen number and shrinks its variance, so a dying channel looks steadier. The core rule `trust/channel_dead` (`config/rules.yml`) looks at the value instead. 3. **A daily mean can be one reading.** Check `n` before trusting an aggregate. 4. **Instants are UTC, days are local.** Daily buckets use `NODE_TZ`. Bali's 9 am burning peak vanishes on a UTC day. 5. **Corrected and raw are both stored.** Raw is never overwritten. 6. **Gaps are real.** No fill, no zero, no interpolation. A gap in a series is a gap in the line. 7. **These are not reference instruments.** They are good for patterns and magnitudes, and the node labels them that way. 8. **Sensors in the same place disagree.** Three kits at one address read the same air and one runs about 1.5 times the other two. Collocation is the cheapest calibration a node can run, and most nodes have it by accident. The core rule `trust/peer_disagreement` reads it.

title: Sensors and sources · Where "outside" comes from
text: Your own outdoor sensors; if there are none, the three nearest public references; if there are none, the model. The rules, the report's digest and the dashboard all use this order.

title: Sensors and sources · The EPA 2021 humidity correction
text: Optical PM sensors over-read in humid air, and Bali runs at 45 to 70% RH. `epa_2021_correct(pm_raw, rh)` is the US EPA 2021 Plantower correction: a raw 28 at Bali humidity becomes about 15. Near-zero raw values in dry air lift to 1 or 2, which is a property of the regression and means nothing for health. It is for Plantower lasers (PurpleAir, AirGradient, a DIY PMS5003), and not for Smart Citizen, Xiaomi, IQAir, AQICN or Airly. It lives in the `air-quality` pack, and its callers are the `airgradient` and `purpleair` packs, which borrow it even where `air-quality` is off.

title: Sensors and sources · Siting
text: Mount it three to six metres up, away from a kitchen exhaust, a chimney or a parking spot, in outdoor air sheltered from horizontal rain, and within reach of 2.4 GHz WiFi. Name it after the place: the name becomes the sensor's name on the page and in every message. For the box, the outdoor sensor enclosure is printable, and Fab Lab Bali prints it.

title: Sensors and sources · Thresholds the air rules use
text: | PM2.5 µg/m³ | scale | used for | |---|---|---| | 15 | WHO 2021, 24-hour | the "clean" line everywhere; the floor of `inside_worse_ventilate` | | 35.5 | US EPA, unhealthy for sensitive groups | `indoor_pm25_high`, `outside_worse_keep_shut`, the "moderate" ceiling | | 55.5 | US EPA, unhealthy | `outdoor_pm25_high` | A spike is 2.5 times the day's mean and above 12 indoors or 15 outdoors. It says something changed before anything is unhealthy. Thresholds written for Kuta Selatan are not thresholds for Barcelona, and a pack's README says which place it was written for.

title: Sensors and sources · Adding a source
text: An adapter is one function in `app/sources.py` (an open protocol the core speaks, such as CKAN) or in a pack's `adapter.py` (a source that belongs to a domain, see [Packs](packs.md)), returning two lists: ```python def my_source(hc: httpx.Client, ...) -> tuple[list[dict], list[tuple]]: sensors = [{"sensor_id": "xx-123", "source": "my_source", "name": "...", "lat": .., "lon": .., "indoor": False, "local": True, "kind": "sensor", "scale": "community", "meta": {...}}] readings = [(ts_utc, "xx-123", "pm25", 12.3), ...] return sensors, readings ``` - Readings dedupe on `(sensor_id, metric, ts)`. `sensor_id` is a short source prefix plus the upstream id (`sc-19880`), and it is never reassigned. - Set `local` and `indoor` to what is true. Every rule and every cell depends on them. - `kind` says how the number was produced: `sensor`, `portal`, `model`, `survey`, `child`, `peer` or `facility` (a place with a name and a point, and no number). The `place` pack also writes `map` rows. Only `sensor` rows enter the `stats` view. - Metric names are lowercase with no unit in the name: `pm25 pm25_raw pm10 pm4 pm1 temp humidity pressure aqi gas_resistance noise light eco2 tvoc co2 hcho tvoc_index nox_index`. Units are fixed: µg/m³, °C, %, kPa. The first pack to ship a metric names it. - When its key or service is missing, the adapter logs once and returns nothing. It must never take the node down. Test it against a saved payload from the real device before you open a pull request. Add its metrics' roles to a `channels.yml`, and file the source in [`awesome-fabcity-data`](https://github.com/fabcity/awesome-fabcity-data) so the registry, and with it the Index, knows it exists.

title: Sensors and sources · Where this leads
text: For a sensor that has to stand where there is no WiFi, [Radios](radios.md) is next. Once the node has something of its own to read, the [dashboard](dashboard.md) draws it against the ring and the region, the [report](report.md) says it in sentences every few hours, and [alerts](alerts.md) is where the node starts asking somebody to do something.

title: Sharing and security
text: Read this page before you open the node to anyone else: a wall screen in the house, a phone, a neighbour's network, a parent node. It says what a reader without a token may see, which token opens what, what leaves the machine and how coarse it is when it does, and whose code the node will run. The rule underneath it is the first refusal in the repository: "No raw readings leave the instance that recorded them."

title: Sharing and security · Before you open it
text: 1. Check what listens on your network ([below](#what-listens-on-the-network)). Only the API answers without a password, and what it answers is decided by `SHARE_LEVEL`. 2. Choose `SHARE_LEVEL`. At `off`, the default, a screen with no token sees the dashboard shell and little else. At `open`, anyone on your network reads the whole read API, including the house's usual day ([the notes below](#share-level)). 3. Give each token to the device that needs it and no other, knowing what each one opens ([The tokens](#the-tokens)). 4. Read [what leaves the machine](#what-leaves-the-machine-and-how-coarse). Each line there has the setting that turns it off. 5. To reach the node from outside the house, use Tailscale and nothing else ([Reaching it from elsewhere](#reaching-it-from-elsewhere)).

title: Sharing and security · What listens on the network
text: | port | what | who may use it | |---|---|---| | `8080` (`APP_PORT`) | the API and the dashboard, on every interface | anyone on the network, within `SHARE_LEVEL`; a token for the rest | | `1883` | the MQTT broker, with the `mqtt` profile (`planetai meshtastic`, `planetai broker`) | a client with the broker's user and password; anonymous clients are refused | | `4001` | the IPFS swarm, with the `ipfs` profile | the IPFS network, which sees only the daily export | | `4242` | Reticulum, with the `reticulum` profile | Sideband, NomadNet and other nodes on the LAN or tailnet | | `3000` (`GRAFANA_PORT`) | Grafana, with the `grafana` profile, on loopback unless `GRAFANA_BIND` says otherwise | whoever signs in to Grafana, who reads every table but `settings` ([Grafana](grafana.md)) | Postgres (`5432`), the IPFS API (`5001`, `8085`) and the Reticulum bridge's API (`4243`) bind `127.0.0.1` only. The API is on every interface because the things that read it are on the network: the NAS that pulls backups, the phones and the wall screen, Home Assistant, and an agent's MCP client on the tailnet. A token guards every write and every secret read.

title: Sharing and security · `SHARE_LEVEL`
text: `SHARE_LEVEL` says who on your network may read the node without a token, and it never sends anything anywhere. Change it in Set up, with `planetai config set SHARE_LEVEL open`, or over MCP; it is live within 20 seconds. There are two levels. `cell` and `means` are named in the setting's help and refused until they exist. | level | a request with no token, from another machine, may read | |---|---| | `off` (default) | 10 paths and the static files: `/` and `/ui` (the dashboard shell), `/tester` (the sensor bench, a shell like `/ui`), `/health` with the centre of the node's resolution-8 cell, `/llms.txt`, `/settings` reduced to the layout and the sharing level, the daily CC BY 4.0 `/export`, `/presence`, `/nodes` (the programme's public list of nodes), `/offers` (what the household chose to lend or give), and anything under `/static/`. Everything else is refused with a sentence naming the setting. | | `open` | 39 paths and 5 prefixes: the `off` list, and `/sensors` and `/stats` (the household's own sensors at the point `/health` publishes, the rest to three decimals, metadata cut to the provenance keys), `/observations`, `/alerts`, `/series`, `/sparks`, `/rho`, `/cells`, `/packs`, `/trust`, `/nearby`, `/forecast`, `/earth`, `/earth/change.png`, `/earth/year.png`, `/earth/frame.png`, `/report/latest`, `/readings`, `/reach`, `/shape`, `/effect`, `/history`, `/exports`, `/sources`, the ask pane's `/ask`, `/ask/status` and `/docs/search`, `/geo/cell` without the fields that place a cell relative to the node (`is_node`, `cells_from_node`, `ring_polar`, `children_polar`), `/learned/place` (what the node learned is usual for the outdoor sensors, never the house), and anything under `/exports/`, `/issues`, `/sources/` and `/ground/`. What a wall screen or a phone with no token needs. | A refused request gets 403 and a sentence. For a path that `open` would answer it ends "Set SHARE_LEVEL to open in the dashboard's Set up view to let anything on your network read it." For a path no level opens it ends "No share level opens this one, so it always needs a token from anywhere but the node itself." The dashboard shows the sentence on its refused page. To watch the boundary move: 1. **Ask from another machine at `off`.** `curl http://<node>:8080/rho` answers 403 with `{"error": "this node is set to SHARE_LEVEL=off, so /rho answers only this machine or a request carrying a token. Set SHARE_LEVEL to open in the dashboard's Set up view to let anything on your network read it."}`. The node is up and keeping ρ to itself. 2. **Open it.** On the node, `planetai config set SHARE_LEVEL open` prints `SHARE_LEVEL is now open, on this node, within 20 s`. After those 20 seconds the same `curl` returns the ρ document. Every screen on your network can now read the node without a token, and nothing has been sent anywhere. 3. **Ask for a path no level opens.** `curl http://<node>:8080/actions` still answers 403, with the second sentence. The record of what people did stays behind a token. `planetai config set SHARE_LEVEL off` closes the rest again. Weigh what `open` gives a reader before you set it on a network you share: - `/shape` is the house's usual day: one mean per local hour, indoor against outdoor, over the whole record. It is also a pattern of when the kitchen is in use. - `/issues` carries the alert events with their rooms (under the neutral names below), the stage and time of the last answer, each issue's usual day and an open event's rooms hour by hour. `/issues/days` gives up to 90 days of the hourly series, indoor rooms included. That is the household's rhythm over three months. It never carries the text the node sent, who answered or what they wrote. - `/forecast` and `/earth` carry the node's exact coordinates. [The API](api.md) says what every route returns. `/sources` is on the `open` list because it is a copy of a public registry, the same on every node in a release, and says nothing about the house. ### Rooms and sensor names stay in the house At every level, a screen without a token never reads what the house calls its rooms or its sensors. Every answer it gets has the house's own labels swapped for neutral ones, "Room A" for a room and "Sensor 1" for a sensor's own name, the same on every route, so the page can still tell one room from another. The sentences of past alerts, written under the names of their day, are left out instead. A token reads the real names.

title: Sharing and security · What needs a token at every level
text: These are on neither list: `/place/geojson` (the shape of your building and what is around it), the `/geo/` routes other than `/geo/cell` (each one locates the node), `/machine` and `/storage`, `/settings/raw`, `/settings/phone`, `/backups` and `/backups/<name>`, `/report/bundle`, `GET /aggregates`, `GET /actions` and the whole of `/captures`. So is every write, and `/mcp` checks the admin token itself. Two writes pass the sharing check because their path is on a list for reading, and their handler refuses them instead: `POST /readings` at `open`, and `PUT /settings` at every level. Without the admin token both are refused. `POST /aggregates` and `POST /events`, what a child sends its parent, pass at every level and check `AGGREGATE_TOKEN` themselves. A request from the machine itself is trusted without a token. That means `127.0.0.1` inside the container: the node's own MCP tools and a shell in the container. A browser on the host is not loopback, because it arrives from Docker's bridge, so it is treated as a machine on the network. `GET /actions` is the record of what people did about the alerts: which alert, which stage, who, and the note they wrote. The note is the household's own words about its own house. `planetai snapshot` blanks every note before it writes its file. `/captures` is the household's own pictures. Its routes refuse every token but `ACT_TOKEN` and `ADMIN_TOKEN`, so the read-only `BACKUP_TOKEN` cannot read a picture. The row keeps the exact point, and the file is cleaned of EXIF and GPS. No capture goes into `/export`, `/exports`, `/aggregates`, `/readings` or a parent push. > **Careful.** `GET /actions` and `/place/geojson` have no token check of their own. Any of the three household > tokens opens them: the admin token, the backup token on the NAS and the act token on a phone. Give each knowing it > reads the household's notes and the plan of its building. `AGGREGATE_TOKEN`, which every child node holds as its > `PARENT_TOKEN`, opens neither.

title: Sharing and security · The tokens
text: All travel as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` and are compared in constant time. There is no query-string form. | token | opens | where it comes from | give it to | |---|---|---|---| | `ADMIN_TOKEN` | every write and secret read: `PUT /settings`, `/settings/raw`, `/settings/phone`, `POST /readings`, `/report/now`, `/test-alert`, the whole of `/mcp`, and what `BACKUP_TOKEN` and `ACT_TOKEN` open. Not `POST /aggregates` or `POST /events`, which take `AGGREGATE_TOKEN` only | made by the installer; `planetai ui` prints it | yourself and your agent. Treat it like a password | | `BACKUP_TOKEN` | read-only pulls: `/backups`, `/backups/<name>`, `/report/bundle`. It cannot read `/settings/raw` | made by `update.sh` when blank; `planetai ui` prints it (`planetai storage` says only whether it is set) | a NAS | | `ACT_TOKEN` | `POST /actions` from off the machine: an act, an acknowledgement, a decision or an answer to an alert event (`event_id`). It cannot read a secret or change a setting | `planetai ui` makes it; Set up › This screen shows it to the admin as a QR code for a phone | a phone, the dashboard's forms in a browser you trust, the Reticulum bridge | | `AGGREGATE_TOKEN` | what this node demands on `POST /aggregates` and `POST /events`; unset, the node accepts no children | you set it | your children, as their `PARENT_TOKEN` | | `PARENT_TOKEN` | sent with this node's hourly pushes to `PARENT_API_URL` | your parent's operator | the node itself | Any of the three household tokens (admin, backup, act) passes the sharing check at every level, so each reads the whole read API. The aggregate token does not. Every child holds it, and a child is another household, so it pushes to `POST /aggregates` and `POST /events` and reads only what a stranger reads. Routes with a check of their own then apply it: a backup token cannot change a setting, and an act token cannot fetch a backup. The optional `X-Agent` header names the caller in the audit trail. The dashboard keeps the token it was given in the browser's local storage and sends the admin token first, then the act token. `.env` is mode 600 and never committed. Backups leave out the `settings` table, so a Telegram token saved from Set up never travels to a NAS or a remote. The node never logs the Telegram URL, because the token is in it.

title: Sharing and security · What leaves the machine, and how coarse
text: | what | to whom | how exact | |---|---|---| | the node's position | `/health`, `/export`, and `/sensors` and `/stats` for the household's own sensors, to a reader without a token | the centre of the resolution-8 cell (about 500 m to an edge); this machine or a token gets three decimals | | hourly means and alert timestamps | a parent node, hourly, if `PARENT_API_URL` is set | values and timestamps; never where, never text, never who | | the daily export | anyone (CC BY 4.0) | your own sensors by role (`indoor-1`, `outdoor-2`), no raw rows, no chat ids | | a presence announce | the Reticulum network, every half hour, only with `RETICULUM_PRESENCE=1` | the H3 cell rounded up to `RETICULUM_PRESENCE_RES` (3), with a floor of resolution 6 that no setting goes under | | the node's coordinates | Open-Meteo, for weather and the CAMS air model, with `OPENMETEO_ENABLED=1` | rounded to three decimals for the current weather and the current CAMS reading | | a request for the fab lab directory | gitlab.fabcloud.org (`MAKE_SOURCE=archive`) or api.fablabs.io (`live`), only with `MAKE_ENABLED=1` and `PACKS_ALLOW_CODE=1` | no coordinates: the whole directory comes down and the node works out the distances | | fires nearby | firms.modaps.eosdis.nasa.gov, at most every three hours, only with `FIRE_ENABLED=1` and `PACKS_ALLOW_CODE=1` | the name of a regional file; with `FIRMS_MAP_KEY`, a box `FIRE_REGION_KM` (150) round the node, to three decimals | | the ground's heat | planetarycomputer.microsoft.com, anonymously, once a day, with the `surface-heat` pack on and `PACKS_ALLOW_CODE=1` | the node's own point, unrounded, in each scene search | | a request for the current version | planetai.fab.city, every hour, with `UPDATE_CHECK=on` (the default) | one file. Fab City's host sees this house's internet address and that a node lives there. `off` means the node never asks | | a request for the list of nodes | raw.githubusercontent.com (`registry.json` on the repository's main), every hour, with `UPDATE_CHECK=on` | one file, as above. `off` means the node never asks | | a species name | api.gbif.org, when a plant or animal in an image is given a scientific name, with `SPECIES_MATCH=on` (off by default) | the scientific name only, never the picture or where it was taken. GBIF sees this house's internet address and the names asked | | the country's list of introduced and invasive species | api.gbif.org and the checklist's archive host, weekly, with `SPECIES_MATCH=on` and the `eyes` pack on | which country's GRIIS checklist to read (the country comes from `NODE_TZ`) | | the open records others made nearby | api.gbif.org, weekly, with `SPECIES_MATCH=on` and the `eyes` pack on | the shape of each of the node's seven resolution-8 cells, which places the node to within about 2 km. Only counts come back, from CC0 and CC BY records | | who lives here, in an alert | the household's own Telegram chats, only for an act-level heat or air alert that weighs on someone ticked in Node › What it remembers | one line naming who ("a child under five"), never a name or an age; never over the mesh, Reticulum or Home Assistant, and never in the stored alert text | | the ground's height | copernicus-dem-30m.s3.amazonaws.com, once, only when somebody runs `planetai run terrain fetch` and `TERRAIN_DEM_PATH` is blank | the one to four 1° tiles the square touches, and the parts of them that hold the node's square, `TERRAIN_RADIUS_M` (5000) round it | | the square the node's own map covers | build.protomaps.com and OpenAerialMap (`planetai run place basemap`) or Earth Engine under the node's own project (`planetai run earth-engine basemap`), once, only when somebody runs the command | the tiles, the finest of them `GROUND_RADIUS_KM` (12) round the node; afterwards the node serves the map at `/ground/*` and sends nothing | | the square being looked at | a tile server, per tile, only with `MAP_TILES=on` | the tile's own square; `off` (the default) draws from the node's local copy of OpenStreetMap | | a question to the bot | an online model, only if you gave it a key and changed `AGENT_PREFER` from its default, `private` | the question and the tool results the model asked for | | a question in the dashboard's ask pane | the model Set up names: this machine, one on your network, or an online provider only with `AGENT_PREFER` set to `fallback` or `strongest` | the question and the page's own sentences and numbers, with no position, name or id; the node keeps no transcript | | an offer | anyone, while the `things` pack is on: `GET /offers` at every level, and the daily export | only a thing the household marked lend or give: its class, name, condition and count, at the node's own resolution-8 cell, with a link to the node's Telegram bot. Never a note, a photo, how often it is used or a point | | raw readings | nobody | nothing | | a `private` reading | nobody: not the export, a parent, the report bundle or any agent, and on this machine's raw routes only the admin token | it is used on the page, by rules and by cells; Home Assistant discovery, the household's own automation, still receives it | At `AGENT_PREFER=private`, the default, the ask pane's model is on this machine or your network and the conversation never leaves: a remote model at an address outside your network is not used. An online model is a choice somebody here makes in Set up, and the pane says so on every answer. A remote agent gets the MCP surface instead, which rounds, refuses and audits. See [Ask the node](ask.md). > **Gap in v0.90.0.** The `coast` and `forecast` packs, and the first start's 92 days of CAMS history, send the > node's full-precision coordinates to Open-Meteo; only the weather adapter in `app/sources.py` and the > `air-quality` pack's current reading round them. The > first start also sends them to NASA POWER and OSM Nominatim. The containers run as root.

title: Sharing and security · Signed updates
text: A node runs the code it is sent, so what it trusts is part of its boundary. `install`, and `planetai update` on a node installed from the tarball, download the release, check its published SHA256, and then check an `ssh-keygen -Y` signature against one key: principal `fabcity`, namespace `planetai-node`. The public line is built into `install`, `update.sh` and `bin/planetai`, so a node can check an update before it has one, and it is published in [tools/allowed_signers](../../tools/allowed_signers). The checksum proves the bytes arrived whole. The signature names who built them, with a key that is not on the web server. A download that does not verify is not installed. The node says `this download is not signed by the PLANETAI release key. Nothing was installed and nothing on this machine changed.`, then asks you to try again on a network you trust and to tell us if it happens twice. `planetai version` prints what this node trusts, and `planetai doctor` says whether the last update checked: ``` planetai-node v0.90.0 · a Fab City project · <name> @ <city> updates signed by fabcity SHA256:OrUQK/jsjNjpei1U8B5tyuEWY36/gwYWXrgVF+5ycIY ``` Compare that fingerprint from a machine that is not the node. If they disagree, something replaced the node's copy of the CLI, and the CLI is not the thing to ask. Every release is published twice from the same bytes with the same signature, at `planetai.fab.city/node0/get` and as a GitHub Release, and `PLANETAI_GET` points an install at the second. `PLANETAI_UNSIGNED=1` installs a tarball nobody signed, with a red warning, and the doctor's signature row stays red until a signed update. How to report a security problem is in [SECURITY.md](../../SECURITY.md).

title: Sharing and security · Reaching it from elsewhere
text: Use Tailscale. `planetai mesh` joins the tailnet under the node's name, and your devices reach the node at its MagicDNS name, `<name>.<your-tailnet>.ts.net` (recorded as `MESH_NAME`), with no open port, encrypted by the tailnet. The node has no TLS of its own, so never put it behind a port forward, ngrok or a public reverse proxy. [Networking](networking.md) has the setup, and the self-hosted alternative to Tailscale's coordinator. There is no loopback-only level. On a network the household does not trust, keep `SHARE_LEVEL` at `off` and give tokens only to your own devices; the NAS pull, the phones, Home Assistant and MCP all read over the LAN.

title: Sharing and security · Where this leads
text: With the boundary set, the node can take its place in a district: [Federation](federation.md) is what a child sends its parent and what the parent refuses. To hand the node to an agent without handing it the house, read [Agents](agents.md).

title: The source registry
text: A node measures what its adapters read. The registry is the network's shared list of what could be measured at each pillar and scale, and of the places a person could go to act on it, carried inside every node as a pinned copy. With it the node can say what anyone has filed that this place could measure, and whether any code here reads it yet. A blank adapter column is an adapter nobody has written, and naming the source is how somebody comes to write it.

title: The source registry · Reading it, step by step
text: 1. **List it.** Run `planetai sources`. It prints `registered in awesome-fabcity-data, read from the node:`, then one line per entry: the slug, the status, the first 40 characters of the licence, the pilots, and the code that reads it. By default it shows this node's pilot (`NODE_CITY`) and the `global` rows, 111 entries on a `bali` node; `--all` shows every entry. It ends with the totals: ``` 111 of 283 entries. The last column is the code that reads it. A cell with sources and a blank column is one nobody has written an adapter for yet. across 19 cells: capable 12 / reviewed 17 / candidate 55 capable = live with an adapter. reviewed = live, backed by an adapter or a usable review. candidate = verified, unread. ``` With `--all` it adds `counted nowhere: 8 deprecated, 1 paywalled, 3 planned, 4 stale.` With the containers down it reads `data/sources/index.json` off the disk and says `read from data/sources (the node is not answering)`. The answer is the same either way, because the registry is a file in the release. 2. **Filter it to one cell.** `planetai sources --all --cell 'Social|City'` lists the 13 entries filed for that cell, from the Barcelona electoral sections to the US Census ACS, and the last column is blank on every one. That is a part of the Index no node fills yet, with the sources that could fill it named. The footer says `Social|City: capable 0 / reviewed 1 / candidate 8`; the reviewed entry is `social/city/ine-spain`, whose review found it usable. The counts are the registry's whole count for that cell whatever the other filters, and they come from `feeds_cells`, so they include `social/region/worldpop`, filed under `Social|Region`. The other filters are `--pillar`, `--scale` and `--json`. 3. **Read one entry.** Ask the node for it by slug: ```bash curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $(grep '^ADMIN_TOKEN=' ~/planetai/.env | cut -d= -f2)" \ localhost:8080/sources/environmental/community/bali-air-dispatch ``` The answer is the entry as filed: `"adapter": "pack:bali-air-dispatch"`, `"feeds_cells": ["Environmental|City"]`, `"auth": "none"`, the licence, and notes naming every reader. The same text is in `data/sources/data/environmental/community/bali-air-dispatch.yaml`. A slug that is not in the pin answers 404 and names the pin. 4. **See it on the Network view.** On the dashboard, Network has a section headed **What this place could read, and where it could go**, with three rows. *Registered, and read* shows `pin cd90289 · synced 2026-10-24` (the pin links to the registry on GitHub at that commit), says `283 sources registered; 18 have code on this node that reads them` with the fourteen adapter strings, and draws `18/283`. *What a cell could use* reads `across 19 cells` with `12 capable`, `17 reviewed` and `55 candidate`. *Places to act* counts the 16 act sources by kind and says how many state that no licence is published (4); a fold under it lists all sixteen with each licence as filed. The page fetches `/sources` the first time somebody opens Network, and never before. The registry records that the code exists on node main, not that a given node runs it: an adapter in a pack reads only on a node with that pack on. Up to v0.83.0 it counted `core:airgradient` while the poll loop never called it.

title: The source registry · Three counts per cell
text: The node counts each cell three ways, from the entries it could fill that cell from: | count | what it counts | |---|---| | `capable` | status `live` and an `adapter`: code here reads it | | `reviewed` | status `live` and either an `adapter` or a review whose verdict is `usable` or `usable-with-caveats` | | `candidate` | status `candidate`: verified, and nobody has read it for a real territory | An entry counts against every cell in its `feeds_cells`, and against its own `cell` only when it has no `feeds_cells` key. An entry with `feeds_cells: []` counts in no cell. No `deprecated`, `stale`, `paywalled` or `planned` entry counts anywhere. `capable` is always part of `reviewed`. At `cd90289` that is 12 capable, 17 reviewed and 55 candidate across 19 cells. Of the eighteen entries with an `adapter`, eight say `feeds_cells: []` (`fablabs-io` is one) and two (`airgradient`, `smart-citizen`) feed two cells each, which makes 12. Reviews add five to `reviewed`. The 55 `candidate` entries also make 55, because ten of them feed two cells each and ten feed none. `Governance|City` has 32 entries filed under it and counts capable 4, reviewed 4, candidate 0: the four CKAN portals that `core:ckan` reads.

title: The source registry · One entry
text: The fields a node uses, from the schema at the pin: | field | meaning | |---|---| | `slug` | `pillar/scale/slug`, from the file's path. The id a pack's `sources:` names | | `cell` | the Index key for the entry's own pillar and scale, e.g. `Environmental\|Community` | | `status` | `live` (a named person's review, or code that reads it), `candidate`, `stale`, `paywalled`, `deprecated`, `planned` | | `license` | the licence of the data itself, as free text | | `api`, `auth` | the endpoint, and what a node must hold to call it (`none`, `key-free-rate-limited`, `api-key`, `registration`, `paid`) | | `pilot_relevance` | which pilots it covers: `barcelona`, `boston`, `santiago`, `bali`, `global` | | `adapter` | what in this repository reads it: `core:<function>` in `app/sources.py` or `app/bootstrap.py`, or `pack:<id>`. Absent means no code reads it | | `feeds_cells` | the Index cells a node fills from it, which need not include the entry's own `cell` | | `role` | `observe`, `act`, or both. Absent means `observe` | | `act_kind` | for an act source: `facility`, `equipment`, `design`, `repair`, `material`, `match` or `network` | | `notes` | the long form: quirks, rate limits, and the licence clauses a source turns on | `wired_in_planetai`, the hand-set boolean that `adapter` replaced, is retired upstream: no entry carries it now, and the node reads only `adapter`. `cell` and `feeds_cells` answer different questions. Bali Air Dispatch is filed under `Environmental|Community`, where it publishes its strongest signal, and feeds `Environmental|City`, because its stations are other people's: they fill the public-reference cell, and the in-custody cell is left to the household's own sensors.

title: The source registry · What the node carries
text: The source of truth is [`awesome-fabcity-data`](https://github.com/fabcity/awesome-fabcity-data), one YAML file per source at `data/<pillar>/<scale>/<slug>.yaml`, checked against the schema in that repository's CI. Each node carries a copy at `data/sources/`, mounted read-only into the app container: | path | what it is | |---|---| | `data/sources/REGISTRY_VERSION` | the pin: `sha=cd90289edd506d7a91d897f17f04f03cd7063426`, `short=cd90289`, `synced=2026-10-24`, `entries=283`, and the upstream URL | | `data/sources/data/<pillar>/<scale>/<slug>.yaml` | the 283 entries as filed | | `data/sources/schema/dataset.schema.json` | the schema they are checked against | | `data/sources/reviews/`, `data/sources/cells/` | the reviews filed for entries, and one file for each of the twenty cells | | `data/sources/index.json` | the YAML folded into one JSON list, with `slug` and `cell` taken from each file's path, and a `reviews` list on every entry (`[]` when there are none) | At `cd90289` the 283 entries are 121 economic, 68 governance, 67 environmental and 27 social. By status, 212 are `live`, 55 `candidate`, 8 `deprecated`, 4 `stale`, 3 `planned` and 1 `paywalled`. Eighteen carry an `adapter`, four carry a review, and sixteen are act sources. `app/registry.py` and `bin/planetai` read `index.json`, so the CLI needs no YAML library on the host. The app caches it on the file's modification time, so a re-pin that arrives with `planetai update` is picked up without a restart. The directory is `SOURCES_DIR`, default `/app/data/sources`. Nothing in this repository edits an entry: `tools/check_registry.py` rebuilds `index.json` from the YAML and fails `make lint` if they differ, if a review names an entry the pin does not carry, if a `cells/` file is not named for its own cell, if a pack reads an entry that names no `adapter`, or if an `adapter` names a pack or a core function this tree does not have. The copy is pinned rather than fetched. [`docs/SOURCES.md`](../SOURCES.md) gives the reasons: a node with no uplink answers the same question as one in Barcelona, every node in a release answers it the same way, and a change to what a node believes about the network is a diff somebody reviewed. `tools/sync_registry.sh` takes a commit and refuses a branch or a tag for the same reason.

title: The source registry · Act sources
text: Sixteen entries carry `role: act`: places to go and things to build with. The `make` pack reads the first two. The licence column is a summary; the entry's own `license` and `notes` say it in full. | entry | act_kind | status | read by | licence, in short | |---|---|---|---|---| | `economic/community/fablabs-io` | facility | live | `pack:make` | not open: no data licence published, and the platform's terms restrict mass harvesting and commercial use | | `economic/community/fablabs-network-data-archive` | facility | live | `pack:make` | none published; the records are fablabs.io's, under its terms | | `economic/community/hackerspaces-org` | facility | live | | not stated | | `economic/community/maps-of-making` | facility | live | | not stated | | `economic/community/precious-plastic-community` | facility | live | | not open: the terms reserve database rights; MIT covers the platform code only | | `economic/community/spaceapi-directory` | facility | live | | not stated | | `economic/community/repair-cafe-directory` | repair | planned | | not stated | | `economic/planet/appropedia` | design | live | | CC-BY-SA-4.0 (site default) | | `economic/planet/field-ready` | design | live | | a CERN-OHL variant on 156 of 193 items, while the organisation's site says all rights reserved; unconfirmed | | `economic/planet/okh-losh` | design | planned | | not stated | | `economic/planet/okh-search` | design | live | | Creative Commons, version and variant not stated | | `economic/planet/open-lab-starter-kit` | design | live | | CERN-OHL-W-2.0 on eight of nine repositories; one is GPL-3.0 | | `economic/planet/oshwa-certification` | design | live | | CC-BY-SA-4.0 | | `economic/planet/things-that-work` | design | live | | CC-BY-SA-4.0 for content, MIT for code | | `economic/planet/open-hardware-manager` | match | live | | not stated | | `governance/city/fab-city-pledged-cities` | network | live | | none published; the Foundation's own list | Four name an open licence outright, four say no licence is published or the data is not open, and the other eight state none or one whose variant or scope is unconfirmed. Neither the dashboard nor this page sorts them into open and not open, because that is a judgement about somebody else's terms.

title: The source registry · Elsewhere in the node
text: - **`GET /cells`.** Every row carries `registered`, `adapter`, `reviewed`, `candidate` and `capable`, grouped by `feeds_cells` as above. `registered` carries the `reviewed` count, and `adapter` is true when `capable` is above 0. A cell with registered sources and no adapter has no `/cells` row at all, because a node only emits rows it can compute; `planetai sources --cell` answers that half. - **`planetai doctor`.** One row: `source registry: 283 entries · awesome-fabcity-data @ cd90289 · synced 2026-10-24`. It goes amber when the pin is over 180 days old and red when `data/sources/` is missing. - **Packs.** Every id in a pack's `sources:` must resolve to an entry at the pin, or `make lint` fails and names the id; 18 resolve. The `fire` pack's is `environmental/bioregion/nasa-firms`, a `candidate` filed with `adapter: pack:fire`, `auth: none` (only its area API needs a key) and `feeds_cells: []`: read, and feeding no cell yet.

title: The source registry · The endpoints
text: ### GET /sources Access: open The registry as this node carries it. Query parameters, each optional and combined with AND: `pillar`, `scale`, `pilot`, `cell`, `status` (`live`, `candidate`, `stale`, `deprecated`, `paywalled` or `planned`) and `wired` (`true` or `false`, read from each entry's `adapter`). `GET /sources?wired=false` is every registered source nothing reads. `pilot` also returns the `global` rows, because an entry relevant everywhere is relevant to every pilot. Returns `{registry: {sha, short, synced, entries}, counts, count, sources}`, where `counts` is `{cell: {capable, reviewed, candidate}}` for every cell the registry counts, whatever the filters. Answers 503 when `data/sources` is empty or not mounted. It is open at `SHARE_LEVEL=open` because it is a copy of a public registry, the same on every node in a release, and says nothing about the house. ### GET /sources/{pillar}/{scale}/{slug} Access: open One entry, as filed. A 404 names the pin the node carries and points back at `/sources`.

title: The source registry · Adding a source
text: 1. Open a pull request to `awesome-fabcity-data` with the entry, one pillar and one scale, following its `CONTRIBUTING.md`. The schema allows no key it does not name. Nothing on any node changes yet: the entry is a proposal, and the network decides whether it is a source. 2. Wait for the merge, and keep the merge commit's sha. A pack may name only what the registry has published, and the next step takes a commit and nothing else: a branch or a tag is answered with `x '<ref>' is not a commit sha.` 3. On a development machine, re-pin with `tools/sync_registry.sh <the merge sha>`. It prints the upstream URL, the short sha and the number of entries. 4. Run `python3 tools/check_registry.py` (part of `make lint`). It prints `<n> registry entries @ <short>, <m> pack source ids resolve, <k> adapters name something here` with the new count and pin. If something is wrong it prints `x the vendored registry does not hold` and one line per problem, a sync stopped half-way among them. 5. Commit `data/sources/` and nothing else, with one line in `CHANGELOG.md`. Every release syncs the registry before it is tagged (`docs/NEXT_RELEASE.md`). 6. Only then may a `pack.yaml` name the id in `sources:`. The check then counts one more pack source id; an id it cannot find fails `make lint` with `` `<id>` does not resolve `` and a guess, or `no entry in the registry`. The entry reaches every node in the next release, and `planetai doctor` there shows the new count and pin. To fill a blank adapter column, write the adapter, a function in `app/sources.py` or a code pack (see [Packs](packs.md) and [Adding a source](sensors.md#adding-a-source) on the sensors page), and then set the `adapter` string upstream; once it is re-pinned, `tools/check_registry.py` checks it against this tree in `make lint`. > **Note.** "Registry" names two things here. This page is the source registry, `data/sources/`. `registry.json` > at the repository root is the list of nodes, described on [Federation](federation.md); the node reads it from > `main` every hour and serves it at `GET /nodes`.

title: The source registry · Where this leads
text: The registry is the same list on every node, which is what lets nodes compare what they measure. [Before a sensor](before-a-sensor.md) is what a node reads for its place on the first day, before any sensor of its own. When you are ready to join other nodes, [Sharing and security](sharing.md) decides who on your network may read the node, and [Federation](federation.md) is how a house becomes one cell in a district's picture without its readings leaving the house.

title: Wall mode
text: The Wall is the node on a screen in a living room or a lab, read from about three metres by people who know nothing about air science, and operated by nobody. It shows the moment, what is asked of the house and what the node's model makes of it. It asks nothing itself: an answer belongs where somebody can write one, on Telegram, over the radio or on the dashboard. ``` http://<node>:8080/#wall ```

title: Wall mode · Putting one up
text: 1. **Let the house read the node.** A wall screen carries no token, so it needs `SHARE_LEVEL=open`: `planetai config set SHARE_LEVEL open`, or Set up › Sharing. At `off` the Wall draws one line, "This screen needs sharing turned on.", and never a token form. 2. **Open `/#wall` on the screen.** You should see, in the dark register and inside one viewport, the time and the node's sentence at the top, the map of the stations around the house on the left, and the page for one scale on the right. The bar and the foot of the other doors are gone. 3. **Leave it.** The map walks out from the house by itself, one scale at a time, replaying each scale's day an hour a step. If the screen has reduced motion on, nothing moves: the Wall holds the street at the last hour. 4. **Reload it now and then.** The Wall reads the node when the page opens. > **Gap in v0.90.0.** The Wall does not re-read the node while it stays open: its figures are those of the moment it > was opened, and only the narration is new every ten minutes. Reload the screen, or put the classic wall up instead, > which re-reads on `POLL_SECONDS`.

title: Wall mode · What it shows
text: ![The Wall at the region scale: the sentence, the map and what the satellites see](img/wall.jpg "The Wall on node #1 at the region scale, the fourth of its four.") Nothing on the Wall is smaller than 28 px at 1920×1080, and the type scales with the screen. What did not fit at that size was cut. It reads in one order: - **The time and the sentence**: the headline issue's title as the node writes it, with what is asked now beside it: the node's own sentence, how many things are asked of the house, and "Answer on Telegram, not here.", or "Nothing is asked now." When the node's last poll is more than 15 minutes old, the time says the readings are old. - **The map**: the stations around the house on the node's own map, framed on the scale's H3 cell, with the wind. The house is one mark and a public station a disc, red when it is over the line. A caption under the map says in words what the red discs mean against the house ("This house is under the clean-air line now; 3 stations nearby, in red, are over it"), at the hour the discs show. - **The scale's page**, beside the map (see below). - **The node, thinking aloud**, under the page, only once there is text. The back button, up to four metric chips (only metrics a station on this node reads) and a note naming the model are chrome: hidden until a pointer is over them or the keyboard reaches them, and always shown as 44 px targets on a touch screen. On a phone, a portrait screen or a small TV the two columns stack, the map first.

title: Wall mode · The walk
text: The map walks out from the house in four scales, each framed on its own H3 cell, drawn blue with the smaller cells faint inside it: | scale | H3 resolution | the page beside the map | |---|---|---| | house | 10 | each issue's figure in the house, and the day in the house | | street | 9 | the street's figures, the replayed hour in words ("Air at 19:00: house 7 · street 11 · ring 8 µg/m³"), and the street's day against what the node learned is usual outside at each hour, dotted (`GET /learned/place`) | | ring | 6 | the land within 1 km as a hundred squares by kind (built, trees, crops, water; land cover by satellite), and the places OpenStreetMap maps there, counted. It says when the map tags too few buildings as shops or offices to tell homes from shops | | region | 3 | what the satellites and models see around: fires within 150 km (NASA FIRMS, `fire` pack), the ground's heat at the last clear Landsat pass and at night (`surface-heat`), fine dust over the region (CAMS), the sea's swell, each only where the node reads it, and floods as not watched on this node yet | Each scale holds while its day is replayed, 24 hours in 30 s, then the walk cuts to the next. A new scale is a cut, never a flight. The four scale names on the map say which one is drawn: pressing one holds it, pressing it again lets the walk go on. Every figure says when it is from and carries a provenance word. A figure from `/observations` takes the node's rule for readouts (`model` for a model, `partial` otherwise), and what the node learned is `partial`. A source is named the way the Wall says it ("Sea, 5 km off"), and a sensor's name never appears.

title: Wall mode · The node, thinking aloud
text: Every ten minutes the Wall asks `POST /ask` with `prompt: wall`, so the model is the one chosen in Set up › Model (`AGENT_PREFER`). The node tells it to speak like a calm neighbour in six to eight plain sentences: what is happening inside, how it compares with the street and the neighbourhood, what it suggests for an ordinary day, and what the next hours may bring, with no units, at most two numbers, and never saying that anything is safe. The model is offered no tools, since every fact it may use is in the request, so it answers without thinking first: a few seconds on node #1's remote model, where thinking had taken more than four minutes and the box stayed empty. The Wall types the text at a reading pace. A story taller than its box then rolls up, a line every three seconds, in a loop that brings its start round again; under reduced motion it stands still at its start. The last text stays up while the next is written, held in the page's memory and never stored. The box calls itself a model's words from the node's figures, never a reading, and says "written online" when the keeper's choice sent the question out. With no model on the node, or `UI_ASK=off`, there is no box. The node gives the model only public facts, each a short labelled line with its unit and where it comes from (`live`, `model` or `satellite`): the time of day; each watched issue's day sentence, its values inside the home, on the street, in the neighbourhood and in the wider area, its line and its trend; every issue's readouts, such as the land's built and tree share and the sea's swell; how many public stations nearby read fine dust and how many are over the WHO line; what is usual for the place (from the outdoor sensors only); the next six hours of forecast; and every section a pack declares with `wall: true`. Each narration starts from an angle those facts can carry (the day so far, the stations around, what is usual here, the next hours, the land and the sea, fires, the ground's heat), and an angle with no facts is skipped.

title: Wall mode · What the Wall never shows
text: Anyone in the room reads the Wall, so it names no sensor, room, kit or person, and the model's facts carry none of them either. What is asked is the node's own sentence, never the alert's text, which can name a room. It never shows what the house learned, its diary, its things, a position or a button to answer. It is always dark, whatever register the other doors are in.

title: Wall mode · The classic wall
text: `/?layout=classic#wall` opens the classic dashboard's wall, which re-reads the node on `POLL_SECONDS` like every classic view. The line `planetai ui` prints for a wall screen (add `#wall`, it moves its own ladder, it needs `SHARE_LEVEL=open`) describes this one, although on `/` the same `#wall` opens the doors' Wall. At `off` it draws the refused page in the dark register, with the node's own sentence. **The top bar**, from the left: a **back** button, first in keyboard order; up to four metric chips (the one shown first, then the node's order, and "+N more" for `?vars=all`; `?var=` picks one, default `pm25`); the node's name, its city, `#wall`, a share level, and "the ladder moves every 8 s" or, under reduced motion, "the ladder stands still"; and at the right the variable, its unit and `15-min means`. **The grid.** Nineteen H3 cells, the node's own and two rings around it, at the current resolution, with no map under them. A cell with one station holds its 15-minute mean and its name; with several, how many and the range; the node's own cell, each of its own stations. An empty cell is drawn and left empty. **The ladder** is drawn as hexagons: the current rung filled ink, a rung whose cell may leave the machine filled in the cells blue at 0.16, a rung finer than the published resolution dashed. Every eight seconds it steps to the next rung and the grid re-draws, with no tween between rungs. Pressing a rung or a cell, or an arrow key, holds it for thirty seconds. Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` nothing moves. **The right column** has the headline issue (kicker, title, tagline, why and the alert), then "Answer on Telegram, not here.", the ladder with its key, the counts (cells with a station, stations in the node's cell, and of them its own), and the ρ row. The ρ row counts rings and never sizes them: one ring per alert up to 40, one per 10 up to 400, then one per 100, with the unit and the exact counts under it. Under the grid, the first five fragments the sections contribute through `wall()`, then "+N more in Now". The classic wall shows open alerts, not alert events, so on a node whose engine is `shadow` or `events` it can read "Nothing has been asked." while Decide has an event open. **The foot** has the as-of time, the version and the motion caption. When a poll got no answer the as-of time reads "Read at … · the node has not answered for N min". If the wall throws while it draws, it says "The wall did not render:" and why, rather than going black. > **Gap in v0.90.0.** On the classic wall the share level in the top bar always reads `off`, because `/health` > carries no share level, and the bold `stale` in the foot is a fixed label that shows whether or not the node is > answering. The as-of time beside it is the one to read.

title: Wall mode · Where this leads
text: Whatever the Wall shows as asked is answered on Telegram, over the radio or on the dashboard, and each of them writes the same row in `actions`: see [Channels](channels.md) and [the dashboard](dashboard.md). What the ρ row counts is [ρ](rho.md), and how the Wall is drawn is [Design](design.md).
